gags: Explains every game as a harvest.
Teaches Natalie a little humility, and she teaches him a little data.
Clanks the brass collar every time he nods.
uc-riverside.compassion: Deep. Looks out for kids from the Inland Empire.
uc-riverside.worldview: Patience and care win the long game. Believes the farmworkers and packers built this valley and deserve to be remembered for it.
uc-riverside.rube: No. Portrait reads white, but the wise long-view lean fits better as the desk elder; owner call.

uc-san-diego.bio: Natalie Lin grew up in Clairemont, San Diego, the daughter of Taiwanese-American marine scientists, and was a high school physics teacher and marching band director for ten years. She started explaining Tritons games on social media with whiteboard diagrams, and The La Jolla Mercury hired her. She explains every win like a science fair project and every loss like a surf report. She still wears her drum major uniform, because the band never asked for it back.
uc-san-diego.backstory: INVENTED. Raised in Clairemont by two oceanographers. Taught physics and led a high school marching band for a decade.
uc-san-diego.beat: INVENTED. Her whiteboard breakdowns of Tritons plays went viral, and the Mercury offered her a column in exchange for the diagrams.
uc-san-diego.look: Huge, laughing smile under a navy-and-gold drum major shako with a tall plume, in a navy tunic with gold braid, epaulets and UC SAN DIEGO across the chest (portrait).
uc-san-diego.favorite: To research: a real Tritons player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: UC Riverside is a nice team with no ocean.
La Jolla is the most underrated basketball town in San Diego, and the tide charts back her up.
Most teams would improve if they studied physics.
uc-san-diego.off_air: INVENTED. Married to Ken, a marine engineer, with twin daughters who play trumpet loudly. Surfs on weekends and keeps a lab notebook for her waves.
gags: Breaks out a whiteboard during timeouts.
Calls Malcolm 'Professor' and debates the long view.
Signals tempo with an invisible baton.
uc-san-diego.compassion: Warm. Cheers for the backup big men and the band.
uc-san-diego.humor: Science-teacher jokes with a big laugh.
uc-san-diego.worldview: Curiosity and evidence make everything better. Believes science should be shared, not hoarded.

uc-santa-barbara.bio: Caleb Thornton grew up in Isla Vista and spent twenty years as a surf instructor and sometime boat captain off the Santa Barbara coast. He started writing laid-back Gauchos columns for a local zine, and The Santa Barbara Spectator hired him. He seems half asleep and then drops the sharpest line in the room. The joke usually lands on him, usually involving sand. He wears a full pirate captain's outfit because he once crewed a tall ship for tourists and nobody made him return it.
uc-santa-barbara.backstory: INVENTED. Raised in Isla Vista, son of a lifeguard and a ceramics teacher. Taught surfing and captained tourist sailboats for decades.
uc-santa-barbara.beat: INVENTED. His sleepy, accidental-genius Gauchos zine columns got passed around enough that the Spectator hired him, partly as a dare.
uc-santa-barbara.look: Full brown beard and a calm squint under a navy-and-gold pirate tricorne with feathers, in a velvet captain's coat with gold braid, a leather baldric and lace cuffs (portrait).
uc-santa-barbara.favorite: To research: a real Gauchos player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Cal Poly is a lovely hike that thinks it's a basketball team.
Santa Barbara is the most relaxed basketball town in the country, and he means that as a threat.
Most teams would improve if they spent more time at the beach.
uc-santa-barbara.off_air: INVENTED. Single, with a dog named Tiller and a sailboat named for an ex-girlfriend. Surfs at dawn and eats avocado toast at noon.
gags: Says he'll go stand in the ocean after every loss, and does.
Accepts Heather's trail maps and then gets lost anyway.
Shakes sand out of the tricorne before every broadcast.
uc-santa-barbara.disposition: Easygoing, sneaky smart, a little lost.
uc-santa-barbara.worldview: Take it easy and look after your crew. Gets uncharacteristically serious about clean water and public beaches.

utah-valley.bio: Whitney Sorenson grew up in Provo, the daughter of a dairy farmer and a seamstress, and spent twenty years as a middle school art teacher. She started writing upbeat Wolverines recaps for her church newsletter and The Orem Sentinel picked her up. She roots with a kind word for everyone and a firm fact for anyone who doubts the mountain kids. She wears a steampunk top hat and goggles because her art students made them for her and she would never hurt their feelings.
utah-valley.backstory: INVENTED. Raised in Provo, the oldest of seven. Taught middle school art, where her classroom had the best bulletin boards in the district.
utah-valley.beat: INVENTED. Her cheerful Wolverines recaps in the church newsletter caught the Sentinel editor's eye, and she got a column within the week.
utah-valley.look: Warm, careful smile under a white top hat with brass goggles, in a white-and-forest-green steampunk band jacket fastened with buckles and UTAH VALLEY across the chest (portrait).
utah-valley.favorite: To research: a real Wolverines player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Sacramento State is a lovely team that hasn't seen real mountains.
Orem is the friendliest basketball town in the West.
Good sportsmanship wins more games than anyone admits.
utah-valley.off_air: INVENTED. Married to Dale, a dentist, with five grown kids and a growing pile of grandchildren. Paints mountain landscapes and enters them in the county fair.
gags: Thanks the other team, sweetly and sincerely, every single time.
Sends Connor homemade cookies with a firm note about the Delta breeze.
Adjusts her goggles before every big fact.
utah-valley.compassion: Abundant. Sends get-well cards to injured players on both teams.
utah-valley.worldview: Kindness and fairness are the right way to play. Believes good neighbors include the new ones.

davidson.bio: Sterling Prescott grew up in Mooresville, North Carolina, the son of a racetrack announcer and a church organist, and spent thirty years as a ringmaster for a traveling circus that played county fairs across the South. When the circus retired, he settled in Davidson, and The Davidson Spectator hired him to cover the Wildcats. He announces every game like the greatest show on earth, even when the crowd has gone home. He has never once said 'game' when he could say 'spectacle.'
davidson.backstory: INVENTED. Raised in Mooresville with a racetrack microphone always in reach. Spent three decades as a traveling circus ringmaster playing county fairs.
davidson.beat: INVENTED. Announced the Wildcats' starting lineup from the stands one night without being asked, and the Spectator editor hired him on the spot.
davidson.look: Handlebar mustache and a big showman's grin under a tall black top hat, in a red sequined ringmaster tailcoat with gold fringe epaulets, a black waistcoat and a bow tie (portrait).
davidson.favorite: To research: a real Wildcats player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Duquesne is a powdered wig in search of a basketball team.
Davidson is the best small town in the South, and the show's been running for years.
Every game deserves a drumroll.
davidson.off_air: INVENTED. Married to Evangeline, a retired trapeze artist who now runs a yoga studio. Keeps a retired circus pony named Bartholomew on a small farm outside town.
gags: Announces every substitution like a new act.
Calls Barnaby 'my lord' in a voice that suggests a sideshow.
Takes a bow after every win, regardless of who earned it.
davidson.compassion: Big. Treats every fan like a front-row guest.
davidson.humor: Grand theatrical bluster; the joke is on him.
davidson.worldview: The show is for everyone, and everyone gets a seat. Thinks small towns put on the best performances.

dayton.bio: Roxanne Vega grew up in Dayton's East End, the daughter of a Mexican-American machinist and a nurse, and spent twelve years as a flight test engineer at the air base before The Dayton Dispatch hired her to cover the Flyers. She calls every game like a mission control briefing, calm and precise with a quiet thrill underneath. She knows Dayton's place in flight history and isn't shy about it. She wears a full flight suit to work because, she says, you never know.
dayton.backstory: INVENTED. Raised in the East End with a dad who fixed jet engines and a mom who worked night shifts. Spent twelve years running flight tests at the base.
dayton.beat: INVENTED. Wrote a mission-style briefing of a Flyers game for an engineers' newsletter, and the Dispatch editor hired her the same week.
dayton.look: Dark wavy hair and a bright, confident smile, in a red-and-blue flight suit with DAYTON across the chest, mission patches and the helmet ring still attached (portrait).
dayton.favorite: To research: a real Flyers player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Saint Louis is a lovely theater with no launch pad.
Dayton invented flight, and the Flyers play like they know it.
Every good possession is a launch sequence.
dayton.off_air: INVENTED. Married to Marco, a high school chemistry teacher, with a son who builds model rockets in the garage. Takes the family to the air museum every month.
gags: Counts down the final ten seconds like a launch.
Gives Anastasia a polite launch window for her monologues.
Reports the crowd's altitude after big runs.
dayton.compassion: Strong. Celebrates everyone on the crew, not just the pilot.
dayton.humor: Precise, dry, with a quiet grin.
dayton.worldview: Every mission needs a team. Thinks the people who build and fix things should get as much credit as the ones who fly them.

duquesne.bio: Barnaby St. Clair grew up in Pittsburgh's Squirrel Hill, the son of a hardware store owner and a piano teacher, and discovered in college that he enjoyed pretending to be an aristocrat. He spent twenty years giving costumed tours of historic Pittsburgh mansions, then The Pittsburgh Clarion hired him to cover the Dukes. He regards the Dukes as nobility and everyone else as rabble. He is often the last to realize the rabble has won. He takes his tea with three sugars.
duquesne.backstory: INVENTED. Raised in Squirrel Hill above his father's hardware store. Gave costumed mansion tours for two decades and never broke character.
duquesne.beat: INVENTED. Gave a Dukes booster club tour in full costume and delivered a scouting report from a balcony, which the Clarion editor attended and printed.
duquesne.look: One raised eyebrow and a smirk, under a powdered white periwig, in a red, navy and gold brocade coat with a lace jabot and DUQUESNE embroidered across it (portrait).
duquesne.favorite: To research: a real Dukes player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Davidson is a circus, and he means that literally.
Pittsburgh's rivers are the noblest in America.
A proper bounce pass should be delivered with a curtsy.
duquesne.off_air: INVENTED. Lives alone with a pug named Lord Wiggleton. Collects antique teacups and has a standing Sunday tea for the neighborhood kids.
gags: Writes strongly worded letters to no one after losses.
Calls Sterling 'the circus fellow' and secretly loves his show.
Lifts his pinky every time he sips coffee on air.
duquesne.disposition: Snobbish on the surface, soft underneath.
duquesne.compassion: Big. Tips the ushers lavishly and calls them 'good sirs and madams.'
duquesne.humor: Pompous fool comedy; he's the joke.
duquesne.worldview: Pretends to believe in rank and privilege, but in practice treats everyone like royalty. Has no patience for actual billionaires who behave like actual aristocrats.

fordham.bio: Carmine Bellini grew up in the Bronx's Belmont neighborhood, the son of a butcher and a seamstress, and spent twenty years as a tango instructor at a dance studio on Arthur Avenue. He started writing dramatic Rams columns for a neighborhood paper, and The Bronx Sentinel hired him. He covers every game like a duel in the ring, every pause intense, even when he's looking for his notes. He wears a full matador's suit of lights because a dance student sewed it for him and he cannot say no.
fordham.backstory: INVENTED. Raised in Belmont above his father's butcher shop. Taught tango and ballroom for two decades on Arthur Avenue.
fordham.beat: INVENTED. His dramatic Rams recaps in a neighborhood paper caught the Sentinel editor's eye, and he got the beat after a very long pause.
fordham.look: Slicked dark hair and a smoldering stare, in a maroon-and-gold sequined matador suit with FORDHAM across the chest and a maroon tie (portrait).
fordham.favorite: To research: a real Rams player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: St. Bonaventure's gadgets will never beat the Rams' passion.
The Bronx is the toughest and most romantic place in New York.
Every game is a duel, and most teams don't know the steps.
fordham.off_air: INVENTED. Single, with a big family that sends him leftovers every Sunday. Still dances on Friday nights and owns a dozen suits, all too tight.
gags: Pauses dramatically for the comeback that does not come.
Calls Jasper's contraptions 'toys' and secretly wants one.
Loses his notes during every dramatic pause.
fordham.compassion: Deep. Looks after the neighborhood kids at the dance studio.
fordham.humor: Dramatic intensity that collapses into comedy.
fordham.worldview: Pride in your place and your people. Believes the Bronx has always been underestimated by people with more money than sense.

george-mason.bio: Zelda Vance grew up in Fairfax, the daughter of a federal accountant and a dance teacher, and spent twelve years as a competitive figure skater and then a coach at a local ice rink. She started recapping Patriots games like skating routines on social media, and The Fairfax Courant hired her. She is bubbly and breathless, giggles at good news and gasps at bad, but she never misses a call. She has never once left the house without rhinestones.
george-mason.backstory: INVENTED. Raised in Fairfax, spent most of her childhood on the ice. Skated competitively, then coached kids at a local rink.
george-mason.beat: INVENTED. Her rink-side recaps of Patriots games went viral among skating parents, and the Courant editor hired her for the energy.
george-mason.look: Big bright smile and rhinestone-studded eye makeup in green and gold, with her hair slicked into a tight updo, in a gold sequined skating dress with green trim and GEORGE MASON across it (portrait).
george-mason.favorite: To research: a real Patriots player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: George Washington is a speech in search of a team.
Fairfax has the most underrated fans in the DMV.
Every good possession has a landing, and most teams wobble.
george-mason.off_air: INVENTED. Lives with her sister and a toy poodle named Axel. Still skates every Saturday morning and judges local competitions.
gags: Scores every play like a skating panel.
Gives Reginald's speeches a technical score, usually low.
Giggles uncontrollably at big wins and gasps at turnovers.
george-mason.compassion: Big. Cheers for every effort, even the falls.
george-mason.humor: Bubbly enthusiasm with a judge's precision.
george-mason.worldview: Everyone deserves a chance to stick the landing. Believes in hard work and second tries.

george-washington.bio: Reginald Chesterfield grew up in Alexandria, Virginia, the son of a history teacher and a bakery owner, and spent twenty-five years as a costumed historical interpreter giving speeches at monuments and museums. The Foggy Bottom Banner hired him to cover the Revolutionaries after he delivered a stirring halftime oration nobody asked for. He treats every game like a founding moment and speechifies through highs and lows, often missing the actual play. He has drafted more proclamations than the Continental Congress.
george-washington.backstory: INVENTED. Raised in Alexandria in a rowhouse full of history books. Spent twenty-five years as a costumed interpreter at museums and monuments around the capital.
george-washington.beat: INVENTED. Gave an impromptu halftime speech at a Revolutionaries game that went on so long the Banner's editor hired him to put it in writing instead.
george-washington.look: Gray hair under a navy-and-gold tricorne, mouth open mid-oration, in a navy-and-buff Continental Army coat with gold epaulets, brass buttons, a white cravat and GEORGE WASHINGTON stitched on the chest (portrait).
george-washington.favorite: To research: a real Revolutionaries player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: George Mason is a lovely routine with no constitution.
Foggy Bottom is the true heart of the capital, and he's said so in several speeches.
A good possession needs a preamble.
george-washington.off_air: INVENTED. Married to Dorothy, a retired librarian who edits his speeches down by half. Collects quill pens and still writes letters by hand.
gags: Misses the game-winning shot while drafting a proclamation.
Gives Zelda's routines a long, solemn review.
Reads the box score aloud as if it were a founding document.
george-washington.disposition: Pompous, sincere, deeply patriotic in the good way.
george-washington.compassion: Real. Treats every fan like a fellow citizen.
george-washington.humor: Grand oratorical bluster; the joke is how long he talks.
george-washington.worldview: Liberty means everybody gets a say. Has no patience for anyone, in any administration, who treats the republic like a private club.

la-salle.bio: Yvette Moreau grew up in Philadelphia's Germantown, the daughter of a Haitian-born tailor and a church choir director, and spent fifteen years singing in regional opera choruses and then teaching voice. The Philadelphia Compass hired her after she sang an Explorers recap at a neighborhood open mic. She treats every game like a grand finale, every win an aria and every loss a tragic third act. She knows this city has booed better shows and still bought the cheesesteak after.
la-salle.backstory: INVENTED. Raised in Germantown, the youngest of four. Sang opera chorus for fifteen years, then taught voice lessons in a rowhouse studio.
la-salle.beat: INVENTED. Sang a La Salle recap at an open mic night, and the Compass editor, who happened to be there, offered her a column with a lyric sheet.
la-salle.look: Hair swept into an elegant updo and a dazzling smile, with chandelier earrings, a blue velvet opera cape, a fluffy gold feather boa and a blue sequined gown with LA SALLE across it (portrait).
la-salle.favorite: To research: a real Explorers player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Saint Joseph's is a lounge act; La Salle is grand opera.
Philadelphia is the toughest audience in America and the best one.
Every season needs a third act, and most teams forget the libretto.
la-salle.off_air: INVENTED. Divorced, with a grown son who's a jazz drummer. Hosts opera nights in her living room and feeds everyone pastries.
gags: Sings a short aria after every big win.
Calls Paco 'the lounge act' and secretly hums his songs.
Collapses dramatically at turnovers, then recovers for the next play.
la-salle.compassion: Big. Champions every overlooked kid on the roster.
la-salle.worldview: Art and sport are for everyone, especially the people in the cheap seats. Believes the city's grit is its greatest beauty.

loyola-chicago.bio: Father Dante Russo grew up in Chicago's Taylor Street neighborhood, the son of a bricklayer and a nurse, and has served as a parish priest on the North Side for decades. He started giving Ramblers updates at the end of Sunday Mass, and The Rogers Park Almanac asked him for a column. He is patient as a long vigil and forgives a cold half if the team defends like it means it. He trusts the lake wind over any scouting report. He has blessed more basketballs than he can count.
loyola-chicago.backstory: INVENTED. Raised on Taylor Street, the oldest of five. Has spent his whole priesthood serving North Side parishes, mostly within walking distance of the lake.
loyola-chicago.beat: INVENTED. His Sunday Mass Ramblers updates got more questions than his homilies, so the Almanac editor, a parishioner, gave him a column.
loyola-chicago.look: Gray hair and a warm, crinkly smile, in a maroon puffer vest with LOYOLA CHICAGO stitched on the chest, over a gold sweater (portrait).
loyola-chicago.favorite: To research: a real Ramblers player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Rhode Island's captain is a good man with too much salt water in his ears.
Rogers Park is the most beautiful neighborhood in Chicago, and the lake wind keeps it humble.
A charge taken is an act of faith.
loyola-chicago.off_air: INVENTED. Lives in the rectory with two other priests and an old cat named Ignatius. Walks Sheridan Road every morning and knows every shopkeeper by name.
gags: Blesses the team before tipoff and the opponents too, quietly.
Exchanges gentle sea-and-lake proverbs with Declan.
Reads the lake wind before giving his pregame prediction.
loyola-chicago.compassion: Boundless. Serves the poor and the visiting team's fans alike.
loyola-chicago.humor: Gentle, wise humor with a twinkle.
loyola-chicago.worldview: Everyone is welcome at the table. Believes faith is shown by feeding people and welcoming strangers, not by power.
loyola-chicago.rube: Yes: the lovable lake-wind parish rube.

rhode-island.bio: Capt. Declan O'Malley grew up in Narragansett, the son of a fishing boat captain and a schoolteacher, and spent ten years as a commercial fisherman and harbor pilot. He started calling Rams games from the deck of his boat over a marine radio, and The Kingston Register hired him. He is all hands for the Rams and blames the tide for every loss, never quite admitting the tide does not reach the gym. He wears an old diving suit because it was his grandfather's.
rhode-island.backstory: INVENTED. Raised in Narragansett on the docks, the oldest of four. Worked as a commercial fisherman and harbor pilot for a decade.
rhode-island.beat: INVENTED. His marine radio Rams calls got picked up by every boat in the bay, and the Register editor, a fisherman, hired him.
rhode-island.look: Ginger hair, a big red beard and a hearty grin, in a vintage brass-collar diving suit of pale blue canvas stenciled RHODE ISLAND (portrait).
rhode-island.favorite: To research: a real Rams player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Loyola's priest is a good man who thinks Lake Michigan is an ocean.
Kingston is the heart of Rhode Island, and the bay is its soul.
Every loss is the tide's fault, and he will not be taking questions.
rhode-island.off_air: INVENTED. Married to Siobhan, a marine biologist who corrects his tide claims. Has three kids, all of whom can tie a bowline before they can ride a bike.
gags: Blames every loss on the tide.
Swaps proverbs with Father Dante, mostly misquoted.
Fogs up an imaginary helmet when he cheers too hard.
rhode-island.compassion: Big. Would pull anyone out of the water.
rhode-island.humor: Booming sea-captain bluster; the joke's on him.
rhode-island.worldview: All hands on deck, and nobody gets left behind. Believes the ocean belongs to everyone and the fishermen deserve a say.

richmond.bio: Savannah Beaumont grew up in Richmond's Fan District, the daughter of a jazz trumpeter and a bank teller, and spent eight years as a high school band director. She started counting out Spiders possessions in her classroom, and The Richmond Spectator hired her. She is crisp and exacting, roots openly for the Spiders but grades them on rhythm, and has no patience for chaos dressed up as a game plan. She still wears the full drum major uniform.
richmond.backstory: INVENTED. Raised in the Fan District with a trumpet always playing downstairs. Directed a high school marching band for eight years.
richmond.beat: INVENTED. Her classroom drills counting out Spiders possessions went viral, and the Spectator editor hired her to bring the tempo.
richmond.look: Huge laugh under a red-and-navy drum major shako with a tall plume, in a red tunic with gold braid, epaulets and RICHMOND across the chest (portrait).
richmond.favorite: To research: a real Spiders player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: VCU's havoc is just noise without a metronome.
Richmond is the most musical city in Virginia.
A rehearsed team beats a talented one every time.
richmond.off_air: INVENTED. Married to Javier, a percussionist, with a toddler who already keeps time. Directs a community band on weekends.
gags: Counts possessions aloud: five, six, seven, eight.
Calls Diamond's press 'a dance with no choreography.'
Taps a baton on the desk during timeouts.
richmond.compassion: Strong. Proud of every kid who learns the rhythm.
richmond.humor: Bandleader precision with a big laugh.
richmond.worldview: Discipline and practice are love in action. Believes music and sport build community.

saint-josephs.bio: Paco Mendoza grew up in North Philadelphia, the son of a Puerto Rican barber and a church organist, and spent twenty years as a lounge singer at hotels and supper clubs up and down the East Coast. The Philadelphia Lantern hired him after he crooned a Hawks recap at a wedding reception. He croons through the wins, forgives the losses with a wink and treats every Big 5 night like a sold-out residency. He believes the Hawk will outlast everyone, including him.
saint-josephs.backstory: INVENTED. Raised in North Philadelphia above his father's barbershop. Sang in lounges and supper clubs for two decades.
saint-josephs.beat: INVENTED. Crooned a Hawks recap at a wedding where the Lantern's editor was a guest, and got the beat before the cake was cut.
saint-josephs.look: Slicked dark hair and a huge, warm grin, in a crimson-and-silver rhinestone jumpsuit with a high collar and SAINT JOSEPH'S across the chest (portrait).
saint-josephs.favorite: To research: a real Hawks player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: La Salle is grand opera; the Hawks are a hit single.
Philadelphia is the best basketball city in America, and Hawk Hill is its stage.
A good game should feel like a slow song.
saint-josephs.off_air: INVENTED. Married to Carmen, a hairdresser, with three daughters who all sing harmony. Still plays a Sunday brunch set at a local diner.
gags: Croons the final score.
Duets with Yvette, sort of, during rivalry week.
Waits by an imaginary piano after losses.
saint-josephs.compassion: Big. Sings at every hospital visit the team makes.
saint-josephs.humor: Smooth lounge-singer charm with a wink.
saint-josephs.worldview: Music and basketball bring a city together. Believes in loyalty to your people and kindness to your rivals.

saint-louis.bio: Anastasia Volkov grew up in St. Louis's Tower Grove, the daughter of a Russian-born violinist and a Midwestern stage manager, and spent twenty years directing community Shakespeare productions in Forest Park. The St. Louis Examiner hired her after she reviewed a Billikens game in iambic pentameter. She roots for the Billikens like a devoted director, reviews every game as theater and has no mercy for a sloppy second act. On air she dresses for carpool; in her head it is always Elizabethan.
saint-louis.backstory: INVENTED. Raised in Tower Grove, the only child of two theater people. Directed community Shakespeare in Forest Park for twenty years.
saint-louis.beat: INVENTED. Her Billikens review in iambic pentameter circulated around the city, and the Examiner editor offered her a column with no meter required.
saint-louis.look: Shoulder-length blonde hair and a warm, confident smile, in a royal-blue SAINT LOUIS quarter-zip, looking more PTA president than Shakespearean director (portrait).
saint-louis.favorite: To research: a real Billikens player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Dayton's mission control needs a better script.
St. Louis is a city of grand theater and grander comebacks.
A sloppy second act ruins a perfectly good game.
saint-louis.off_air: INVENTED. Married to Gregory, a set designer, with a teenage son who refuses to act. Hosts Shakespeare readings in her living room every Sunday.
gags: Reviews every game in five acts.
Gives Roxanne stage directions she didn't ask for.
Quotes the Bard during timeouts, sometimes accurately.
saint-louis.humor: Grand theatrical wit with a sharp edge.
saint-louis.worldview: Art and community belong together. Believes every story deserves an audience.

st-bonaventure.bio: Jasper Whitmore grew up in Olean, New York, the son of a machinist and a high school science teacher, and spent five years building gadgets in a basement workshop that his mother called 'the hazard.' The Olean Beacon hired him to cover the Bonnies after his homemade prediction engine correctly called three wins in a row. He believes every win was predicted by a machine he built and every loss by a machine he hasn't finished. He is giddy, all in, and slightly singed.
st-bonaventure.backstory: INVENTED. Raised in Olean, the only child of a machinist and a science teacher. Built gadgets in the basement for years and occasionally set off the smoke detector.
st-bonaventure.beat: INVENTED. His prediction engine called three straight Bonnies wins, and the Beacon editor hired him before the fourth game, which it got wrong.
st-bonaventure.look: Round face and a delighted grin, under a brown top hat with brass goggles, in a brown-and-cream steampunk jacket with leather buckles and ST. BONAVENTURE across the chest (portrait).
st-bonaventure.favorite: To research: a real Bonnies player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Fordham's matador has never fixed a single thing with a wrench.
Olean is the best small town in New York, snow and all.
Every game can be predicted, given the right machine.
st-bonaventure.off_air: INVENTED. Lives with his mother, who keeps a fire extinguisher by the basement door. Builds automata for the town's holiday window displays.
gags: Unveils a new contraption every broadcast, and it never quite works.
Offers Carmine a gadget to help with his dramatic pauses.
Fogs his goggles every time he gets excited.
st-bonaventure.compassion: Big. Builds toys for kids in the hospital.
st-bonaventure.humor: Giddy inventor comedy; the joke is always him.
st-bonaventure.worldview: Curiosity and tinkering can fix almost anything. Believes small towns hold the best inventors.

vcu.bio: Diamond Brooks grew up in Richmond's Jackson Ward, the daughter of a gospel organist and a city bus driver, and spent ten years as a club DJ and event promoter. The Richmond Observer hired her to cover the Rams after she DJed a watch party so loud it made the paper. She roots loud for the Rams, calls the press a groove and never lets the other side of town forget who brought the party. She has never once worn a non-sequined outfit to a game.
vcu.backstory: INVENTED. Raised in Jackson Ward with gospel on Sundays and funk every other night. Spent a decade DJing clubs and throwing parties.
vcu.beat: INVENTED. DJed a Rams watch party so packed the Observer covered it, and the editor ended up hiring the DJ.
vcu.look: Big, glossy curls and a radiant smile, in a black-and-gold mirror-ball sequined tuxedo with gold lamé lapels, a gold bow tie and VCU across the front (portrait).
vcu.favorite: To research: a real Rams player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Richmond's drum major can't keep up with havoc.
Richmond is the best party city in Virginia, and the Rams are the headliner.
Defense is a dance, and the press is the best song.
vcu.off_air: INVENTED. Lives with her partner Tasha, a nurse, and a cat named Groove. Still spins a Saturday set downtown.
gags: Drops an imaginary beat after every steal.
Offers Savannah a dance lesson every rivalry week.
Sparkles on air no matter what.
vcu.compassion: Big. Throws parties for the student section.
vcu.worldview: Joy is resistance, and everybody belongs on the dance floor. Has no patience for anyone trying to keep folks out of the party.

canisius.bio: Paulie Brennan drove a Buffalo snowplow for most of his working life and tended bar on weekends, which is where he picked up every story he now tells slowly, lovingly and slightly wrong. He edits The Buffalo Picayune from a corner stool and covers the Golden Griffins with total, unembarrassed devotion. Paulie believes a small gym during a lake-effect storm is the finest room in American sports. He also believes blue cheese is a moral question. Ask him about the old days and clear your evening.
canisius.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up above his uncle's tavern in South Buffalo, the son of a city plow driver and a parish secretary. Drove a plow himself for decades and poured drafts on the side.
canisius.beat: INVENTED. Wrote a 'Bar Stool Box Score' on the back of coasters for regulars; the Picayune's old sports editor started running them, and Hardwood Bricks eventually gave him an actual stool.
canisius.look: Heather-blue quarter-zip with gold shoulders and a Canisius crest, short gray hair, outdoor tan and an easy closed-mouth smile (portrait).
canisius.favorite: To research: a real Golden Griffins player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: A small gym in a snowstorm is the best room in American sports.
Lewiston is a lovely place to take your aunt to see the water.
Wings come with blue cheese, and he will not be taking questions.
canisius.off_air: INVENTED. Married to Maureen, a retired ER nurse who corrects his stories in real time from the kitchen. Coaches his grandson's biddy league team and routinely loses track of the score.
gags: Starts a story about a Griffs game 'back in the day' and finishes it about a different game, possibly a different sport.
Blames the snow for road losses in fully enclosed arenas.
Leaves Alicia long voicemails about the old days; she rates each one in waterfalls.
canisius.temperament: Slow to boil, slower to cool off.
canisius.disposition: Nostalgic, generous, certain the old days had better jump shots.
canisius.appropriateness: PG, with one 'for cryin' out loud' per broadcast.
canisius.compassion: Will shovel your walk before he learns your name.
canisius.humor: Corner-bar shaggy dog stories where the punchline is usually that he got it wrong.
canisius.worldview: A city is the people who show up when it snows; he's learning, happily, that the people showing up now don't all look like his old block.

fairfield.bio: Olivia Romano grew up in Stratford, spent a few years keeping architects on schedule, and now keeps the Fairfield Stags on schedule from the Hardwood Bricks desk. She edits The Fairfield Lantern with a red pen and a stopwatch. Olivia loves a crisp possession, an extra pass, and any game that ends before the Post Road jams up. She has no patience for wasted timeouts, yacht-club attitude, or her crosstown rival's volume. She has never once been late. She has been early, alone, many times.
fairfield.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in Stratford, the daughter of a hardware store owner and a school librarian. Worked as a project coordinator for an architecture firm, where she was famous for ending meetings early.
fairfield.beat: INVENTED. Live-posted possession-by-possession efficiency grades of Stags games for fun; the Lantern hired her to tighten its copy, and Hardwood Bricks followed the trail.
fairfield.look: Red polo with white side panels and a Fairfield wordmark, shoulder-length brown hair, small composed smile (portrait).
fairfield.favorite: To research: a real Stags player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: A wasted possession is a small crime against everyone who drove in on the Post Road.
Sacred Heart shares a town with the Stags, which is generous of the Stags.
Every game should finish in under two hours, and the Stags are welcome to help.
fairfield.off_air: INVENTED. Runs a color-coded calendar for her entire extended family. Leaves for Sunday dinner so early to beat traffic that she usually arrives to an empty house and sets the table herself.
gags: Times her own segments with a stopwatch and apologizes for two-second overruns.
Sends Tommy an article about indoor voices every time he yells on air.
Keeps a live traffic map in the corner of her monitor during games and narrates it at halftime.
fairfield.disposition: A tidy optimist who believes most problems are scheduling problems.
fairfield.compassion: Higher than she lets on; always saves a seat for whoever's running late.
fairfield.worldview: Respect means showing up prepared and not wasting anyone's evening; she's skeptical of money that mistakes itself for merit.

iona.bio: Vinnie Moretti sold restaurant supplies across Westchester for decades and called sports radio after every Iona game until somebody gave him a microphone just to free up the phone lines. He edits The New Rochelle Messenger and believes the Gaels are the best team in New York, a position he defends at length and mostly in sauce metaphors. Vinnie still eats Sunday dinner at his mother's table, where she reviews his broadcasts out loud. Her notes are tougher than any critic's, and she is usually right.
iona.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up on the West End of New Rochelle, the youngest of five, in a house where his mother ran the kitchen like a general. Sold restaurant supplies up and down Westchester for most of his life.
iona.beat: INVENTED. Called a local sports talk show after every Gaels game for years; the Messenger asked him to write it down instead, and Hardwood Bricks claims it hired him as a public service to the switchboard.
iona.look: Maroon Iona hoodie with big gold letters and a matching maroon cap, gray hair under the brim, sun-creased friendly face (portrait).
iona.favorite: To research: a real Gaels player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: The Gaels are the best team in New York, and he'll explain why as soon as he finds the start of the sentence.
Manhattan College is in the Bronx, which he still finds suspicious.
A game without a red sauce dinner afterward didn't really happen.
iona.off_air: INVENTED. His mother, Rosa, still hosts Sunday dinner and grades his broadcasts on a scale of one to five meatballs. Grows plum tomatoes in the backyard and talks to them before big games.
gags: Laughs so loud the board operator keeps a dedicated 'Vinnie' fader.
Explains the Gaels' greatness through a sauce recipe and loses the thread at the garlic.
Calls Siobhan 'the kid from the Bronx'; she fact-checks him while he's still laughing.
iona.temperament: Volcanic and quick to cool, like a pot left on high.
iona.appropriateness: PG. 'Madonn'' counts as a full sentence.
iona.compassion: Feeds anyone who looks hungry and asks questions later.
iona.humor: Big laugh first, joke second, occasionally no joke at all.
iona.worldview: Everybody gets a seat at the table, even Manhattan fans, eventually.

manhattan.bio: Siobhan Kelly taught high school English in the Bronx, graded essays on the 1 train every night, and eventually started grading Manhattan Jaspers games the same way. She edits The Bronx Examiner and covers the Jaspers with a red pen in one hand and a protective arm around them with the other. She roasts their mistakes because she loves them, and heaven help any outsider who tries it. Siobhan reads a novel a week underground. Her margin notes on box scores have their own fan club.
manhattan.backstory: INVENTED. Raised in Woodlawn, the daughter of a subway conductor and a Catholic school teacher. Taught high school English in Kingsbridge for years.
manhattan.beat: INVENTED. Started marking up Jaspers box scores on her commute the way she marked up essays; a reader mailed one to the Examiner, and the editor printed it red ink and all.
manhattan.look: White quarter-zip with a green zipper and collar and a Manhattan wordmark, light brown hair past the shoulders, steady half-smile (portrait).
manhattan.favorite: To research: a real Jaspers player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: The ride up to Riverdale is the most honest commute in New York sports.
Iona is loud. Loud is not the same as good.
Only she gets to criticize the Jaspers; everyone else can take a number.
manhattan.off_air: INVENTED. Still reads a novel a week on the subway. Plays Tuesday trivia with her two sisters and wins the sports round on spite alone.
gags: Pulls out the red pen during timeouts and marks up the box score in real time.
Fact-checks Vinnie's Gaels history live, then pats his hand.
Announces subway delays like injury reports.
manhattan.appropriateness: PG. The eyebrow does all the swearing.
manhattan.compassion: Fierce for the underdog and the kid in the last row.
manhattan.humor: Fast and cutting, then a wink.
manhattan.worldview: Loyalty means telling the truth to the people you love and standing between them and the bullies.

marist.bio: Evan Gallagher wrestled in high school, taught middle school gym for years, and has never met a fundamental he didn't want to rewind. He edits The Poughkeepsie Ledger and breaks down every Marist Red Foxes game like a coaching clinic, usually while everyone else has moved on to the next play. Evan grades both benches fairly, speaks in a calm coach's voice, and then completely loses it over a perfect box-out. He folds laundry in his old wrestling singlet. He insists it's about mobility.
marist.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up on Poughkeepsie's Northside, the son of a postal carrier and a church organist. Wrestled in high school, then spent years as a middle school PE teacher and assistant wrestling coach.
marist.beat: INVENTED. Ran a free film night for youth coaches in a church basement; the Ledger asked for a column, and Hardwood Bricks asked for the column out loud.
marist.look: Red and white Marist wrestling singlet, close-cropped hair and salt-and-pepper stubble, eyes wide and mouth open in a full-throated shout of joy (portrait).
marist.favorite: To research: a real Red Foxes player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Every problem in basketball is a footwork problem.
Siena tells stories. Marist watches tape.
A Hudson Valley February is the best film-study weather on earth.
marist.off_air: INVENTED. Married to Lorraine, a pediatric nurse who hides the remote during playoff season. Still wears the singlet around the house and calls it 'workwear.'
gags: Still on the first half when the game ends and begs the producers not to spoil it.
Explains every screen as a wrestling takedown.
Sends Sean a frame-by-frame breakdown of the story he didn't finish.
marist.temperament: Calm on the surface, absolutely thrilled underneath; the portrait shows underneath.
marist.disposition: Patient, thorough, endlessly delighted by fundamentals.
marist.compassion: A teacher's heart; nobody sits out in his clinics.
marist.humor: Dry delivery that dissolves into joy at a good box-out.
marist.worldview: Do the small things right and the big things follow, for kids, towns and teams alike.

merrimack.bio: Brooke Tremblay talks fast, roots hard, and has not taken off her headset since college radio. She grew up in Methuen, managed a coffee shop, and called games for the campus station until The North Andover Messenger made her its editor. Now she covers the Merrimack Warriors for Hardwood Bricks with nonstop, sunny energy and a large iced coffee, even in January. Especially in January. Brooke treats every Warriors win as wicked good news and every loss as a speed bump. Her rival's emotional range is her personal project.
merrimack.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in Methuen, the daughter of a Vietnamese-American pharmacist and a French-Canadian electrician. Managed a busy coffee shop while calling games for her college radio station.
merrimack.beat: INVENTED. Her campus radio recaps got more listeners than the morning show; the Messenger hired her, and Hardwood Bricks asked her to keep the headset.
merrimack.look: Navy Merrimack hoodie with gold lettering and drawstrings, broadcast headset with a boom mic, dark hair pulled back, mouth wide open in pure excitement (portrait).
merrimack.favorite: To research: a real Warriors player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Iced coffee in January is a lifestyle, not a mistake.
Quinnipiac's anchor should have one visible feeling on air, at least once a season.
North Andover is the best small town in Massachusetts and she'll argue it in any coffee line.
merrimack.off_air: INVENTED. Still picks up a Saturday shift at the coffee shop for fun. Has a rescue cat named Wicked who sits on the desk during podcasts.
gags: Never removes the headset, including at weddings.
Tracks her iced coffees per game like a stat line.
Keeps a running tally of her attempts to make Jared smile on air.
merrimack.temperament: Bubbly and fast; bounces back in seconds.
merrimack.appropriateness: G. 'Wicked' does all the heavy lifting.
merrimack.compassion: Knows every usher's name and birthday.
merrimack.worldview: Small schools rising is the best story in sports, and everybody should get to be part of it.

mount-st-marys.bio: Father Greg Connolly spent years as a high school chaplain and JV coach before parish life in the Catoctin foothills, and his homilies kept drifting toward free-throw form. The Emmitsburg Sentinel gave him a column to keep the sermons on topic. Now he covers the Mount St. Mary's Mountaineers for Hardwood Bricks with grace, patience and one unforgivable grudge against missed free throws. He laughs before his own punchlines, which somehow helps. Every Christmas he makes his mother's tamales for the whole parish.
mount-st-marys.backstory: INVENTED. Raised in Frederick, the son of an Irish-American mail carrier and a Mexican-American mother from San Antonio who taught him to cook and to forgive, in that order. Was a high school chaplain and JV basketball coach before taking a small parish.
mount-st-marys.beat: INVENTED. His Sunday homilies kept wandering into shooting mechanics; the Sentinel offered him a column so the congregation could get home on time, and Hardwood Bricks followed.
mount-st-marys.look: Navy and white Mount St. Mary's polo with a lapel mic clipped on, swept-back silver hair, laughing so hard his eyes nearly close (portrait).
mount-st-marys.favorite: To research: a real Mountaineers player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: A missed free throw is the one sin he struggles to forgive.
Emmitsburg sits close enough to heaven that the Mount deserves the benefit of the doubt on close calls.
Siena's anchor is a good man who has never finished a story, and he prays for him.
mount-st-marys.off_air: INVENTED. Makes his late mother's tamales for the parish every Christmas. Runs a free-throw clinic for kids in the church parking lot on summer evenings.
gags: Assigns penance for missed free throws: a decade of the rosary and a hundred practice shots.
Blesses both rims before tipoff, to be fair.
Offers to hear Sean's confession, mostly so he can finally get to the end of a story.
mount-st-marys.temperament: Serene, with one exception at the line.
mount-st-marys.compassion: Boundless; forgives the other team before the final horn.
mount-st-marys.humor: Gentle wit, perfect timing, usually at his own expense.
mount-st-marys.worldview: Grace first and effort always; a small town that looks after its neighbors is already winning.

niagara.bio: Alicia Kowalczyk grew up within earshot of the Falls and spent years narrating them from the deck of a tour boat before running a tourism office. She edits The Lewiston Pilot and covers the Niagara Purple Eagles like a tour guide who knows every overlook, pointing out backdoor cuts the way she once pointed out rainbows. Alicia laughs easily, cheers loudly, and believes every visiting team should see the Falls first so they understand what they're up against. Her snow globe collection is, she says, still growing.
niagara.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in Niagara Falls, New York, the daughter of a hotel night manager and a church choir director. Worked as a tour boat guide and later ran a regional tourism office.
niagara.beat: INVENTED. Slipped Purple Eagles score updates into her tour-boat narration until tourists began asking for box scores; the Pilot hired her, and Hardwood Bricks heard about it from a visitor.
niagara.look: Purple Niagara quarter-zip with white side panels and a matching purple cap, hair pulled back, mouth open in a delighted shout (portrait).
niagara.favorite: To research: a real Purple Eagles player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Every visiting team should tour the Falls first so they know what they're up against.
Canisius has a fine program and a very long-winded anchor.
Lewiston in early spring beats any vacation anyone has ever taken.
niagara.off_air: INVENTED. Married to Stan, a retired firefighter who makes pierogi for every home opener. Collects snow globes of the Falls and lines the studio shelf with them.
gags: Gives tour-guide directions to every play: 'and if you look to your left, a backdoor cut.'
Ends sentences with a big 'Ha!' whether or not they were jokes.
Rates Paulie's stories in waterfalls, never more than three.
niagara.compassion: Treats every visitor like a guest who drove all night to get there.
niagara.worldview: Home is something you share; the more people who see it, the better it gets.

quinnipiac.bio: Jared Goldstein was an insurance data analyst in Hartford until his weekly unsolicited spreadsheets grading Quinnipiac possessions finally earned him a job, mostly so the emails would stop. He edits The Hamden Spectator and judges the Bobcats on process, not the scoreboard, refusing to overreact to anything, including wins. He describes himself as calm and measured. His face, by every available account, does not agree. Jared does the crossword in pen and logs his completion times. He has never shared them.
quinnipiac.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in West Hartford, the son of an actuary and a legal aid lawyer. Spent years as an insurance data analyst, where he once built a model to predict the office coffee running out.
quinnipiac.beat: INVENTED. Emailed the Spectator a weekly spreadsheet grading every Bobcats possession for process; the editor hired him, and Hardwood Bricks borrowed the spreadsheet.
quinnipiac.look: Navy polo with gold collar trim and a Bobcat crest, curly brown hair, eyes wide and grinning like a man failing to hide his joy (portrait).
quinnipiac.favorite: To research: a real Bobcats player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Wins are lagging indicators.
Brooke's iced coffee consumption is not a sustainable process.
Hamden deserves a team that takes good shots even on nights the bad ones go in.
quinnipiac.off_air: INVENTED. Married to Rachel, a high school band director who reads his face far better than his spreadsheets. Does the crossword in pen and logs every completion time.
gags: Insists he's calm while beaming like a kid on a snow day.
Rates his own excitement on a five-point scale and never admits to more than a two.
Attaches confidence intervals to Brooke's adjectives.
quinnipiac.temperament: Claims perfect calm; the face disagrees.
quinnipiac.compassion: Gentle with players, merciless with shot selection.
quinnipiac.humor: Bone-dry, with his own grin as the punchline.
quinnipiac.worldview: Fair process beats flashy results, in basketball and in public life.
quinnipiac.rube: Yes: the lovable spreadsheet guy whose face gives away every feeling.

rider.bio: Denise Holloway spent a long career balancing state budgets in Trenton, and she covers the Rider Broncs the same way: no fluff, no excuses, and a red line through anything wasteful. She wrote such pointed letters to The Lawrenceville Courant's sports page that the editor eventually handed her the page. Denise loves the Broncs, loves a stingy defense, and judges every night by whether she beat the Route 1 traffic home. Her sarcasm is dry. Her laugh is enormous. You'll hear both.
rider.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in Trenton's West Ward, the daughter of a city bus driver and a nurse. Worked for decades as a state government budget analyst.
rider.beat: INVENTED. Her letters to the Courant about the Broncs' defense were sharper than the coverage, so the editor offered her the section; Hardwood Bricks asked her to read them aloud.
rider.look: Cranberry and white Rider quarter-zip, short natural hair, mid-way through a big open laugh (portrait).
rider.favorite: To research: a real Broncs player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Route 1 after a weeknight game is a test of character.
Saint Peter's charm is a defensive strategy, and it works.
An excuse is just a turnover with paperwork.
rider.off_air: INVENTED. Married to Curtis, a retired high school band teacher. Their grown son lives in Philadelphia and receives weekly traffic advisories he did not request.
gags: Gives a Route 1 traffic report in place of a halftime report.
Laughs loudly at her own sarcasm, which is the only way to know it was sarcasm.
Trades holiday cookie tins with Carmen every December; both claim victory.
rider.temperament: Brisk, impatient with nonsense, delighted by competence.
rider.appropriateness: PG. 'Lord, give me patience' is as strong as it gets.
rider.compassion: High, though it arrives formatted like a budget memo.
rider.humor: Dry sarcasm followed by a huge laugh.
rider.worldview: Do the work, skip the excuses, and make sure the people who do the work get paid for it.

sacred-heart.bio: Tommy DiNapoli was a personal trainer in Bridgeport who posted Sacred Heart reactions between sets until The Fairfield Courier hired him, mostly because his comment section was the only one where nobody fought. He covers the Pioneers for Hardwood Bricks with pure gym-rat hype, treats every win as a personal record, and regularly forgets which half it is. Tommy meal-preps in labeled containers and brings a protein shaker to every broadcast. He believes everybody can get better, himself very much included.
sacred-heart.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in Bridgeport's North End, the son of a firefighter and a dental hygienist. Worked as a personal trainer at a strip-mall gym.
sacred-heart.beat: INVENTED. Filmed Pioneers reactions from the squat rack; the Courier hired him for the wholesome comment section, and Hardwood Bricks hired him for the volume.
sacred-heart.look: Red Sacred Heart hoodie with white arched letters and a matching red cap, light stubble, mouth wide open in a joyful scream (portrait).
sacred-heart.favorite: To research: a real Pioneers player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Every Pioneers win counts as leg day.
Fairfield should share its town with a lot more enthusiasm.
Halftime is the most important set of the night.
sacred-heart.off_air: INVENTED. Meal-preps every Sunday in containers labeled by game day. His golden retriever, Protein, attends every home game in spirit.
gags: Forgets which half it is, asks the producer, then celebrates anyway.
Uses his protein shaker as a noisemaker.
Asks Olivia to spot him through emotional losses; she sends him a calendar invite.
sacred-heart.temperament: All gas, no brakes, no hard feelings.
sacred-heart.appropriateness: PG. 'Let's go' counts as a paragraph.
sacred-heart.compassion: Golden retriever energy; everybody is his bro.
sacred-heart.humor: Unfiltered hype; laughs at himself constantly.
sacred-heart.worldview: Everybody gets better when somebody believes in them, him included.
sacred-heart.rube: Yes: the lovable gym-rat golden retriever.

saint-peters.bio: Carmen Rosario spent her whole career as a public school guidance counselor in Jersey City, and she still treats everyone who walks through the door like a student who deserves a second chance. After retiring she hosted Saint Peter's watch parties in her living room, and The Jersey City Clarion asked her to write them up. She edits it now. Carmen adores the Peacocks, welcomes every visitor warmly, and quietly enjoys watching big-budget programs squirm. Her flan has ended more arguments than any referee.
saint-peters.backstory: INVENTED. Born in Greenville, Jersey City, the eldest of six in a Puerto Rican family. Worked her entire career as a public school guidance counselor.
saint-peters.beat: INVENTED. Her living-room watch parties got so popular that the Clarion asked her to report what the guests said; she reported what she said instead, and readers preferred it.
saint-peters.look: Peacock-blue polo with white piping and a Saint Peter's wordmark, long dark hair streaked with silver, warm wide smile (portrait).
saint-peters.favorite: To research: a real Peacocks player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Little schools carry more heart per square foot.
Big-budget programs look their best when they're nervous.
Rider's anchor is sharp, and she's always welcome at Carmen's table.
saint-peters.off_air: INVENTED. Grandmother of five who makes pasteles for the whole block every Christmas. Keeps a framed photo of the peacock she swears once wandered into her yard.
gags: Calls every player, referee and rival 'my dear.'
Brings flan to the desk to soften up visiting anchors.
When a big program starts to squirm, she says nothing and slowly sips her coffee.
saint-peters.worldview: The little guy deserves the same respect as the giant, and Jersey City has always known it.

siena.bio: Sean McDonough Jr. hosted pub trivia in Albany so long-windedly that a regular who edited The Loudonville Almanac offered him a column, figuring print at least had an ending. It does. His stories don't. He covers the Siena Saints for Hardwood Bricks with cheerful, shameless loyalty, and every game sends him into a tale from his grandfather that he can never quite finish. Sean loves an Albany winter, a packed gym, and a round for the table. He plays the tin whistle badly at family parties.
siena.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in Albany's Pine Hills, raised partly by a grandfather who told stories at the kitchen table. Worked as a motor vehicles clerk by day and a pub trivia host by night.
siena.beat: INVENTED. A trivia regular who edited the Almanac offered him a column on the theory that print has word counts; Hardwood Bricks has learned that broadcasts do not.
siena.look: Gold quarter-zip with a dark green collar and Siena wordmark, ginger hair and a full red beard, eyes wide and grinning (portrait).
siena.favorite: To research: a real Saints player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: An Albany winter builds character, and Siena has character in bulk.
Marist watches tape. Siena makes memories.
Every gym needs a grandfather in row three yelling kindly at the referees.
siena.off_air: INVENTED. Married to Kathleen, who has heard the first half of every story he owns. Plays the tin whistle badly, and enthusiastically, at every family party.
gags: Begins a grandfather story during every timeout and never reaches the end.
Says 'Slainte' after every made free throw.
Evan sends him tape breakdowns of his own unfinished stories, with timestamps.
siena.compassion: Warm and generous; buys the round.
siena.humor: Shaggy-dog stories with no ending, delivered with total confidence.
siena.worldview: Family and neighbors are the real story; the score is just the excuse to gather.
siena.rube: Yes: the lovable storyteller who lost the ending.

brown.bio: Barnaby Thayer taught maritime history at a small Rhode Island community college for decades and still believes every lecture deserves at least three detours. He edits The Providence Sentinel and grades the Brown Bears like a beloved seminar, generous with partial credit and prone to forgetting to mention who won. Barnaby wears a smoking jacket on air without irony. He considers the quahog underappreciated and a good tangent the intellectual equivalent of a fast break. His wife navigates his sentences for him.
brown.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in Fox Point, Providence, the son of a jewelry factory foreman and a public librarian. Taught maritime history at a community college for most of his career.
brown.beat: INVENTED. Began stapling Bears box scores to his lecture handouts; a former student who edits the Sentinel offered him a column with no word limit, a decision since revisited.
brown.look: Red plaid sequined smoking jacket with crimson velvet lapels and a Brown crest, cravat, round tortoiseshell glasses, silver hair and gray mustache, gesturing with a 'B' microphone (portrait).
brown.favorite: To research: a real Bears player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: The quahog is underrated, and so are the Bears.
Dartmouth plays like it's late for the ski lift.
A good tangent is just a fast break for the mind.
brown.off_air: INVENTED. Married to Ines, a retired harbor pilot who steers his sentences back to port. Keeps a shed full of half-built ship models he describes as 'in progress.'
gags: Delivers a full recap and forgets to say who won.
Assigns himself reflection essays after losses and never reaches the game.
Answers Winnie's ski metaphors with a lecture on glaciers.
brown.compassion: Kind to every student, especially the ones who skipped the reading.
brown.humor: Rambling professorial tangents where the joke is the destination he never reaches.
brown.worldview: Curiosity is a civic virtue, and a library card beats a trust fund.

columbia.bio: Henrietta Morningside grew up backstage, the daughter of a stagehand and a piano teacher, and spent years as an understudy before becoming a neighborhood theater critic. On a dare she reviewed a Columbia Lions game as an opening night. The Morningside Courier ran it, readers demanded an extended run, and now she edits the paper. Henrietta is generous to a great second act and merciless to a lazy curtain call. She rides the 1 train to every home game and calls it the best pregame show in the city.
columbia.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in Washington Heights, the daughter of a Broadway stagehand and a piano teacher. Worked as an understudy, then as a critic for a neighborhood weekly.
columbia.beat: INVENTED. Reviewed a Lions game like an opening night on a dare; the Courier printed it, and Hardwood Bricks booked her for the full season.
columbia.look: Columbia-blue sequined military coat with silver frogging, ruffled white collar and cameo brooch, auburn hair in a sculpted updo, holding a lion-flagged microphone (portrait).
columbia.favorite: To research: a real Lions player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Every second half deserves a stronger second act.
Ithaca is lovely if you like your drama outdoors and frozen.
The 1 train is the best pregame show in New York.
columbia.off_air: INVENTED. Teaches a Saturday acting class for kids in Harlem. Has seen her favorite musical more times than she will admit in writing.
gags: Gives every game a star rating, and the officials a separate one.
Calls timeouts 'intermission' and halftime 'the interval.'
Mails Libby a pair of opera glasses so she can see past the snow.
columbia.humor: Theatrical and arch, and fully aware of it.
columbia.worldview: The city belongs to the people who keep the show running: stagehands, conductors, ushers.

cornell.bio: Libby Hartwell grew up on a dairy farm outside Ithaca and spent years planning snow routes for the county highway department, which explains why she grades Big Red wins in inches of snowfall. She edits The Ithaca Argus and covers Cornell with cheerful precision and zero tolerance for teams that won't box out. Libby believes the gorges are the best home-court advantage in the league. She insists she owns a monocle. Nobody at Hardwood Bricks has ever seen it.
cornell.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up on a dairy farm outside Trumansburg, the daughter of farmers who milked before dawn. Planned snow-plow routes for the county highway department.
cornell.beat: INVENTED. Her personal snowfall log started including Big Red scores; an Argus editor noticed the column of numbers and offered her the sports desk.
cornell.look: Carnelian-red sequined field vest with mesh pockets and a Cornell patch over a white rolled-sleeve shirt, curly hair pinned up, holding a 'C' microphone and grinning; no monocle in sight (portrait).
cornell.favorite: To research: a real Big Red player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: If you can't box out, you can't shovel either.
Columbia's anchor has never personally dug out a car.
Ithaca's gorges are the best home-court advantage in the Ivy.
cornell.off_air: INVENTED. Lives with her partner Sam, a fiddle player, and two goats with strong opinions. Keeps a snow shovel in every vehicle she has ever owned.
gags: Reports every Big Red win in inches of snowfall.
Has misplaced her monocle and mentions it every broadcast.
Issues Henrietta winter weather advisories before every road trip.
cornell.compassion: First one out with a shovel when a neighbor's car is stuck.
cornell.worldview: Communities that dig each other out stick together.

dartmouth.bio: Winnie Hollis taught skiing and led trail crews around Hanover before she ever picked up a microphone, and she still covers the Dartmouth Big Green like a powder day. She edits The Hanover Lantern and expects her team to climb the hard pitches without complaint. Winnie wears her goggles on her head well into February. She calls every hot streak first chair and every cold one a wax problem. She thinks her rival's tangents are wildly off-piste and tells him so, warmly.
dartmouth.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in Lebanon, New Hampshire, the daughter of a ski patroller and an ER nurse. Worked as a ski instructor and summer trail-crew leader.
dartmouth.beat: INVENTED. Called Big Green games over the ski lodge PA until skiers asked for a written version; the Lantern hired her, and Hardwood Bricks gave her a real microphone.
dartmouth.look: Dartmouth-green sequined Fair Isle tuxedo jacket with snowflakes and pine trees, black bow tie, tousled updo, mic in hand, mid-cheer (portrait).
dartmouth.favorite: To research: a real Big Green player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: A tough road game is just a black diamond with a scoreboard.
Brown's anchor would be great company on a chairlift, where nobody can leave.
Hanover in January is the best place on earth to be indoors watching basketball.
dartmouth.off_air: INVENTED. Waxes her own skis in the station parking lot. Has a three-legged dog named Moguls who outskis most people.
gags: Calls every run a powder day.
Wears ski goggles on her head into late February.
Tells Barnaby his tangents are off-piste and offers him a trail map.
dartmouth.compassion: Ski-patrol instincts; she always checks who fell.
dartmouth.worldview: Everybody climbs, and nobody gets left on the mountain.

harvard.bio: Prudence Ashworth grew up in Somerville, argued her way through a legal aid career, and now covers the Harvard Crimson like a closing argument: crisp, evidence-based, and quietly certain she's already won the room. She edits The Cambridge Dispatch and coaches a middle school debate team on weekends. Prudence wears a Puritan collar on air and laughs like a sailor. She believes preparation beats pedigree and enjoys proving it to her rival in New Haven, ideally before he finishes his sherry.
harvard.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in Somerville, the daughter of a public school debate coach and a union electrician. Worked as a legal aid attorney.
harvard.beat: INVENTED. Delivered closing arguments about the Crimson at her neighborhood bar; a Dispatch editor overheard, raised no objection, and offered her a column.
harvard.look: Crimson velvet coat covered in sequins with a broad white Puritan collar and cuffs and a Harvard crest, short swept-back hair, laughing into the microphone (portrait).
harvard.favorite: To research: a real Crimson player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Yale's anchor has never once been on time for a fast break.
Somerville produces better rebuttals than any law school.
Money doesn't win games. Preparation does.
harvard.off_air: INVENTED. Coaches a middle school debate team in Somerville. Keeps a rebuttal notebook on her nightstand in case she thinks of a better one at 3 a.m.
gags: Shouts 'Objection!' at bad calls.
Rests her case after every win.
Rebuts Thurston before he's finished his first sip.
harvard.temperament: Brisk and certain, generous in victory.
harvard.compassion: Fights hardest for the client nobody else wanted.
harvard.worldview: Evidence and fairness over pedigree; she came from Somerville, not the club.

penn.bio: Benjamin Quill spent years as a historical reenactor and tour guide in Old City, and never quite changed out of the waistcoat. He edits The University City Spectator, where he writes every Penn Quakers win like a founding document and every loss like a clerical error. Benjamin considers the Palestra the cathedral of the sport and will hear no appeals. He drafts his proclamations in quill and ink, which is why he usually finishes reading them aloud after the building has emptied.
penn.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in South Philadelphia above his family's picture-framing shop. Worked as a costumed historical reenactor and walking-tour guide.
penn.beat: INVENTED. Started writing Quakers recaps with a quill and iron-gall ink; the Spectator agreed to typeset them, slowly, and Hardwood Bricks agreed to wait.
penn.look: Red and blue sequined colonial waistcoat with a Penn shield, white lace jabot, round wire spectacles and long wavy hair, beaming over a Penn microphone (portrait).
penn.favorite: To research: a real Quakers player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: The Palestra is the cathedral of the sport, and no appeal will be heard.
Princeton's anchor throws a lovely party at the wrong address.
Every loss can be traced to the draft from the east doors.
penn.off_air: INVENTED. Married to Deborah, a city bus mechanic who answers his proclamations in plain modern English. Owns more tricorn hats than the situation requires.
gags: Finishes reading his proclamation after the arena has emptied.
Blames the ink, the lighting and the draft before any Quaker.
Challenges Chip to a duel of adjectives every rivalry week.
penn.disposition: Pompous, sweet, a half beat behind.
penn.compassion: Large; believes in liberty and playing time for all.
penn.humor: Mock-heroic oratory where he is the joke.
penn.worldview: Founding ideals were meant for everybody, and he's still reading the fine print on that with enthusiasm.

princeton.bio: Chip Van Doren ran banquets at a hotel near Princeton for years and still treats every Tigers game like a black-tie soiree he is personally hosting. He edits The Princeton Intelligencer, reviews shot charts like guest lists, and considers the backdoor cut the most elegant arrival in sports. Chip calls everyone darling. He has a bow tie for every opponent and a gift for being in the wrong hallway with the canapes at the exact moment the party moves rooms. The Tigers forgive him. So does everyone.
princeton.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in Lawrence Township, the son of a wedding caterer and a florist. Worked as a hotel banquet manager.
princeton.beat: INVENTED. Emceed watch parties in the hotel bar so stylishly that the Intelligencer asked him to write them up, and Hardwood Bricks sent an invitation.
princeton.look: Orange-and-black tiger-stripe sequined tuxedo jacket with a tiger crest, black bow tie, slicked dark pompadour, beaming into a vintage gold microphone (portrait).
princeton.favorite: To research: a real Tigers player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: The backdoor cut is the most elegant move in sports.
The Palestra is gorgeous, though the canapes are lacking.
Every gym deserves better lighting.
princeton.off_air: INVENTED. Throws themed dinner parties for his neighbors every rivalry week. Owns a bow tie for every opponent on the schedule.
gags: Misses the big moment because he's in the wrong hallway with the canapes.
Calls players, referees and the scoreboard operator 'darling.'
RSVPs formally to each of Benjamin's proclamations.
princeton.worldview: A party is better when everyone's invited, walk-ons included.
princeton.rube: Yes: the lovable party host lost in his own house.

yale.bio: Thurston Whitmore poured wine at a New Haven steakhouse for years, delivering Bulldogs commentary with every bottle until the owner suggested he find a different audience. The New Haven Mercury obliged. He covers Yale from a leather armchair, forgives the Bulldogs nearly anything, and is usually two plays behind because he was refilling the decanter. Thurston belongs to a club with four members and firm views on Harvard. He is learning, slowly and sincerely, that the club could use a few more chairs.
yale.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in Branford, the son of a boatyard owner. Spent years as a sommelier at a New Haven steakhouse.
yale.beat: INVENTED. His tableside Bulldogs commentary distracted so many diners that the Mercury hired him to give it somewhere else to go.
yale.look: Navy sequined smoking robe embroidered with Yale crests and skull-and-crossbones motifs, blue-and-white striped tie, silver hair, raised-eyebrow smirk (portrait).
yale.favorite: To research: a real Bulldogs player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Harvard is a fine school for people who couldn't decide.
A glass of sherry improves any zone defense.
New Haven pizza is the true national championship.
yale.off_air: INVENTED. Belongs to the Elm Street Sherry and Lawn Bowling Society, which has four members and meets in his den. Grows orchids badly and names each one after a sherry.
gags: Two plays behind because he was refilling the decanter.
Writes stern letters to 'the committee,' which may not exist.
Prudence objects to his commentary before he's finished his sip.
yale.disposition: Clubbable, forgiving, slightly out of date.
yale.compassion: A soft heart under the velvet; tips everyone generously.
yale.worldview: Tradition is lovely as long as the door is open, and he's propping it wider every year.

campbell.bio: Hamza Vance was an undersized high school power forward who became a physical therapist, which means he has spent his whole life thinking about rebounds and the knees that chase them. He edits The Buies Creek Courant and calls Campbell Camels games straight and plain, gives the other bench its due, and checks the rebounding margin before the score. Hamza saves his real warmth for the folks who drive the back roads in to watch. He grills for his entire street on the Fourth of July and again on Eid.
campbell.backstory: INVENTED. Raised in Dunn, North Carolina, the son of a Pakistani-American family doctor and a local schoolteacher. Played high school ball as an undersized power forward, then became a physical therapist.
campbell.beat: INVENTED. Kept a rebounding chart from the bleachers and taped a copy to the Courant's office door every week until the editor gave him the sports section.
campbell.look: Long orange-and-black paisley sequined brocade jacket with a Campbell patch, neatly trimmed beard and styled dark hair, holding a mic flag with his name on it, easy smile (portrait).
campbell.favorite: To research: a real Camels player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: The rebounding margin never lies.
Elon's anchor narrates comebacks the way other folks pray for rain.
The back roads into Buies Creek are prettier than any interstate.
campbell.off_air: INVENTED. Grills for his whole street on the Fourth of July and again on Eid. Plays pickup ball on Wednesday mornings and boxes out like it's a tournament game.
gags: Reads the rebounding margin before the final score.
When Phoenix predicts a comeback, he silently points at the glass.
Keeps a running list of the farthest drives fans made to games, read aloud with reverence.
campbell.compassion: Warmest toward the people who drove the farthest.
campbell.worldview: Do the hard, unglamorous work, and give the other side its due.

charleston.bio: Bea Beauregard grew up on James Island in a Gullah Geechee family and ran one of the busiest catering businesses in the Lowcountry before a booster dinner toast turned into a scouting report. The Charleston Ledger asked for it in writing, and she's edited the paper since. Bea is gracious to every guest and merciless about their manners. She roots for the Charleston Cougars like it's a family obligation and runs the room like she owns the house. She keeps a guestbook. Visiting teams are noted in it.
charleston.backstory: INVENTED. Born on James Island to a Gullah Geechee family; her grandmother sold sweetgrass baskets on the roadside. Ran a catering business for most of her career.
charleston.beat: INVENTED. Gave a toast at a Cougars booster dinner she was catering that turned into a full scouting report; the Ledger asked her to write it down, and Hardwood Bricks asked her to read it aloud.
charleston.look: Maroon-and-white seersucker sequined blazer with sparkling lapels and a cougar patch, bow tie, big pearl earrings, short dark hair, laughing (portrait).
charleston.favorite: To research: a real Cougars player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Manners are a defensive scheme.
UNCW's anchor would wear flip-flops to a wedding.
A Charleston January is how the Lord apologizes for August.
charleston.off_air: INVENTED. Teaches Sunday school and a Tuesday night cooking class. Makes every visitor to her home sign the guestbook, including the plumber.
gags: Reads visiting teams' guestbook entries aloud after the game.
Deploys 'bless your heart' as a tactical timeout.
Mails Sid a dress code before every rivalry game.
charleston.appropriateness: PG, all of it in the subtext.
charleston.compassion: Generous to guests, fiercely protective of family.
charleston.worldview: Hospitality is a duty and a power, and Charleston's story should be told by everyone who built it.

drexel.bio: Draco McAllister designed escape rooms in Philadelphia before he started designing imaginary heists for the Drexel Dragons. He edits The Powelton Examiner and treats every half-court possession as a caper he personally planned, then is genuinely delighted when the players improvise something better. Draco carries a notebook full of diagrams, nearly all of them wrong. He picks locks as a party trick, only with permission, and he takes Towson's full-court press as a personal insult to his craft.
drexel.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in Olney, the son of a Korean-American locksmith and a Scottish-American math teacher. Designed escape rooms for a small Philadelphia company.
drexel.beat: INVENTED. Built a Dragons-themed escape room so elaborate that the Examiner reviewed it, then hired him to diagram actual possessions.
drexel.look: Navy and gold dragon-scale sequined blazer with a Drexel patch and navy tie, swept-up black hair, wide-eyed and open-mouthed as if a play just surprised him (portrait).
drexel.favorite: To research: a real Dragons player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Every half-court set is a heist.
Towson's press is loud, but every lock can be picked.
A Powelton porch is the best scouting seat in Philadelphia.
drexel.off_air: INVENTED. Keeps a notebook of elaborate heist plans he will never use. Picks locks at parties, strictly with the host's permission.
gags: Announces he called the whole game, except every part that actually happened.
Takes Priya's steals as a personal insult to his planning.
Leaves diagrammed napkins behind at every diner in University City.
drexel.disposition: A schemer with a big heart.
drexel.worldview: The best plans include everybody, and the best plays come from people you didn't plan for.
