elon.bio: Phoenix Fontaine taught high school drama in Burlington, North Carolina, and she still reads every basketball game like a three-act play with a guaranteed comeback. She edits The Elon Spectator and narrates Phoenix rallies before they happen, which makes her right just often enough to be dangerous. She grew up in her parents' bakery and still makes the Sunday pan dulce. Phoenix runs a community theater in the off-season. She believes no deficit is final and no rival's rebounding chart is all that interesting.
elon.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in Burlington, North Carolina, the daughter of Salvadoran-American bakers. Taught high school drama for years.
elon.beat: INVENTED. Predicted three straight Phoenix comebacks in her neighborhood group chat; the Spectator hired her before she could get one wrong.
elon.look: Maroon cape blazer covered in gold flame-feather sequins with an Elon patch, long dark wavy hair, mic in one hand and the other palm open, bright grin (portrait).
elon.favorite: To research: a real Phoenix player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Every Phoenix deficit is just the setup.
Campbell's anchor would read a love letter for its rebounding margin.
Second halves are where the real story starts.
elon.off_air: INVENTED. Bakes the family pan dulce every Sunday. Runs a community theater that has staged the same musical three summers in a row by popular demand.
gags: Announces the comeback before the deficit even happens.
Treats halftime as the end of Act One.
Sends Hamza a dramatic monologue whenever he mentions the glass.
elon.compassion: Never writes anyone off, including herself.
elon.humor: Big dramatic flourishes with a wink.
elon.worldview: Every story has a second act, and people deserve the chance to rise.

hampton.bio: Capt. Kendra Shaw earned her title on the water, working as a merchant deck officer and harbor tug captain before coming ashore. She edits The Hampton Sentinel and runs her Hampton Pirates coverage like a ship's log: crisp, proud and unimpressed by sloppy ball handling. Kendra is fiercely loyal to a disciplined crew and drills her readers on turnovers the way she once drilled deckhands on knots. She still salutes the flag over the arena and expects the point guard to keep the ball as secure as cargo.
hampton.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in Phoebus, Hampton, the daughter of a Navy machinist and a shipyard welder. Served as a merchant deck officer, then captained a harbor tug.
hampton.beat: INVENTED. Kept a formal ship's log of every Pirates game from the bleachers; the Sentinel printed one as written, and the column never stopped.
hampton.look: Royal-blue sequined sea-captain coat with white lapels, gold buttons and fringed gold 'Hampton' epaulettes, natural hair pulled up, one hand on hip, wide smile (portrait).
hampton.favorite: To research: a real Pirates player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: A turnover is cargo lost overboard.
NC A&T's band is wonderful, and Hampton's crew is better.
Home by the sea is the best home court there is.
hampton.off_air: INVENTED. Ties sailor's knots to relax and can do most of them blindfolded. Takes her grandmother sailing on the bay every Sunday in summer.
gags: Reads the box score as a ship's log, entry by entry.
Assigns turnover drills to the audience.
Trades salutes with Dominique, and both insist they saluted first.
hampton.compassion: Loyal to her crew; nobody is left behind.
hampton.worldview: Discipline and care keep a crew afloat, and every crew member matters.

hofstra.bio: Sal Rizzuto worked the counter at his family's deli on Long Island for twenty years and wrote Hofstra previews on the specials board between orders. A Hempstead Clarion editor photographed one while waiting for a hero, and the job came with a sandwich. Sal covers the Pride like Sunday dinner, roots without shame, and keeps mixing up basketball terms with the specials board. He calls rebounds 'seconds' and a zone 'the combo plate.' He wears a ringmaster's coat on air and won't explain why.
hofstra.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in Franklin Square, the son of deli owners. Worked the counter of the family deli for two decades.
hofstra.beat: INVENTED. Wrote Pride game previews on the deli's specials board; a Clarion editor photographed one while waiting on an order, and Hardwood Bricks saw the photo.
hofstra.look: Royal-blue sequined ringmaster coat with gold frogging, fringed epaulettes and a Hofstra patch, gold bow tie, salt-and-pepper hair and stubble, mid-laugh with a microphone (portrait).
hofstra.favorite: To research: a real Pride player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: A good game plan is just a good deli order.
Stony Brook's anchor checks the tide chart more than the scoreboard.
Hempstead on game night smells like victory and provolone.
hofstra.off_air: INVENTED. Married to Gina, who runs the deli now and won't let him near the slicer. Coaches his daughter's CYO team with a clipboard that's mostly a sandwich menu.
gags: Calls rebounds 'seconds' and a zone 'the combo plate.'
Promises sandwiches to everyone and always forgets his wallet.
Sends Skipper a hero every rivalry week, labeled 'for the boat.'
hofstra.disposition: Shameless booster with a big heart.
hofstra.humor: Deli-counter wisecracks; the joke is usually on him.
hofstra.worldview: Everybody eats, and nobody leaves the table hungry.

monmouth.bio: Jersey Jo Romano ran a boardwalk ring-toss stand every summer and drove a school bus every winter, which gave her two great skills: talking smack and knowing every exit on the Garden State Parkway. She edits The West Long Branch Courier and covers the Monmouth Hawks as their most shameless booster, with boardwalk swagger and a voice built to carry over the surf. Jo counts Parkway exits on the way to road games out loud. She is no relation to Fairfield's Olivia Romano, and both of them would like that noted.
monmouth.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in Long Branch, the daughter of a lifeguard captain and a diner waitress. Ran a boardwalk ring-toss stand in summer and drove a school bus in winter for years.
monmouth.beat: INVENTED. Barked Hawks scores from the ring-toss stand until the crowd came for the updates instead of the prizes; the Courier hired her, and Hardwood Bricks gave her a bigger crowd.
monmouth.look: Navy and silver sequined bandleader jacket with gold trim and a Monmouth patch, long wavy brown hair, laughing into the microphone (portrait).
monmouth.favorite: To research: a real Hawks player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: The Shore is the best home-court advantage in New Jersey.
Stony Brook's anchor is a nice man who should step off the boat once in a while.
The Parkway is a test of faith and the Hawks are worth it.
monmouth.off_air: INVENTED. Still runs the ring-toss stand on summer weekends. Has three teenage sons and a parakeet who says 'Go Hawks.'
gags: Counts Parkway exits out loud on the way to every road game.
Talks smack like she's running a ring toss: 'Step right up, Seawolves.'
Clarifies she is no relation to Olivia, and Olivia clarifies it back.
monmouth.compassion: Protective of every kid on her old bus route.
monmouth.worldview: Shore towns take care of their own, and everybody is welcome on the boardwalk.

nc-at.bio: Dominique Vance led the band as a drum major in college and spent years as a middle school band director in Greensboro before stepping in front of a microphone. She edits The Greensboro Chronicle and calls NC A&T Aggies games like she's leading the band onto the field, every possession in rhythm. She gives proud, measured credit to any opponent who can keep step. Dominique still wears the plumed shako on big nights. She is no relation to Campbell's Hamza Vance, though they've agreed to be cousins for the holidays.
nc-at.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in east Greensboro, the daughter of a church organist and a retired textile mill worker. Was a college drum major, then a middle school band director.
nc-at.beat: INVENTED. Her halftime show breakdowns went viral in the neighborhood, so the Chronicle asked her to break down the games too.
nc-at.look: Royal-blue and gold sequined drum major uniform with an A&T crest, tall plumed shako with a gold feather, bright wide smile (portrait).
nc-at.favorite: To research: a real Aggies player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Tempo wins games, and the band sets the tempo.
Hampton's crew is disciplined, and the Aggies are on beat.
Greensboro on a game night is the best show in the state.
nc-at.off_air: INVENTED. Still directs a youth marching band on Saturdays. Has a closet with more plumes than shoes.
gags: Counts off possessions in eight-beat phrases.
Grades halftime shows with the same rigor as the game.
Trades salutes with Kendra, and both insist they saluted first.
nc-at.compassion: Lifts every section, not just the stars.
nc-at.worldview: Everybody has a part to play, and the whole thing works when we all keep the beat.

northeastern.bio: Nora Sullivan grew up in Dorchester, did a string of co-ops through school, and covers the Northeastern Huskies like one more co-op she plans to ace. She edits The Fenway Almanac, talks faster than the Green Line has ever moved, and has no patience for a lazy closeout. Nora wears a sequined parka with a fur hood on air because the arena is cold and she refuses to apologize. She keeps a written list of every lazy closeout of the season. It is long, and it is alphabetized.
northeastern.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in Dorchester, the daughter of a trolley operator and a hospital billing clerk. Did a series of co-ops, including one at a hospital, before landing as a project manager.
northeastern.beat: INVENTED. Ran a game recap newsletter from the Green Line on her commute; the Almanac hired her, and Hardwood Bricks noticed the commute times in the margins.
northeastern.look: Red and black sequined parka with a fur-trimmed hood, a Northeastern patch and her name tag, long red hair, holding an 'NE Huskies' microphone with a big smile (portrait).
northeastern.favorite: To research: a real Huskies player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: The Green Line is a test of character.
Hofstra's anchor is lovely but needs a schedule.
Huntington Ave on a big night beats anything in town.
northeastern.off_air: INVENTED. Lives with three roommates and a cat named Co-op. Runs along the river every morning, rain or snow.
gags: Keeps an alphabetized list of every lazy closeout.
Gives Green Line delay times as halftime stats.
Tells Sal his game plan is 'all appetizers.'
northeastern.compassion: Looks out for the walk-ons and the interns.
northeastern.worldview: Hard work deserves a fair shot, whether you're a co-op kid or a walk-on.

stony-brook.bio: Skipper Callahan captained a Long Island Sound ferry for decades and spent his summers volunteering at a lighthouse, so he reads every Stony Brook Seawolves game like a tide chart. He edits The Stony Brook Register and gives the other side a fair wind, a fair grade and a hearty wave. Skipper is easygoing, generous and usually the last aboard when the momentum shifts. He checks the ferry schedule during timeouts. He has never once been seasick, a fact he mentions more often than anyone has asked.
stony-brook.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in Port Jefferson, the son of a ferry deckhand and a nurse. Captained a Long Island Sound ferry for most of his working life and volunteered as a summer lighthouse keeper.
stony-brook.beat: INVENTED. Called Seawolves scores over the ferry PA until passengers started riding just to hear them; the Register hired him, and Hardwood Bricks gave him a bigger deck.
stony-brook.look: Red sequined keeper's coat with navy panels and gold trim over a black turtleneck, white hair and a trim white beard, holding a microphone and smiling warmly (portrait).
stony-brook.favorite: To research: a real Seawolves player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Every game turns on the tide.
Hofstra's anchor talks like a deli at lunch rush.
The Sound in February is cold, honest and beautiful.
stony-brook.off_air: INVENTED. Married to Grace, a retired harbor master. Keeps a tide chart taped to the fridge and a lighthouse model on the mantel.
gags: Checks the tide chart and ferry schedule during timeouts.
Gives every play a nautical rating.
Waves to Sal from the deck like he's passing a fishing boat.
stony-brook.compassion: Gives everyone, rivals included, a fair wind.
stony-brook.worldview: Fair winds for everyone; a good harbor welcomes every boat.

towson.bio: Tiger Priya earned her nickname as a high school point guard who pressed full court for thirty-two minutes and never apologized. She later worked as a corporate fraud investigator, which taught her to spot a lazy pass from the parking lot. She edits The Towson Observer and covers the Towson Tigers with a grin full of teeth, treating every steal like a trophy. Priya has opinions about York Road traffic and shares them during timeouts. Drexel's anchor plans heists. She catches thieves.
towson.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in Parkville, the daughter of a Tamil-American anesthesiologist and a high school wrestling coach. Played point guard in high school, then worked as a corporate fraud investigator.
towson.beat: INVENTED. Ran a defensive-stats blog called 'The Press' that the Observer bought, and Hardwood Bricks followed the trail of steals.
towson.look: Gold-and-black tiger-stripe sequined blazer with a Towson patch, dark wavy shoulder-length hair, holding a microphone and grinning (portrait).
towson.favorite: To research: a real Tigers player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Every steal is a trophy.
Drexel's anchor plans heists. She catches thieves.
York Road traffic is a full-court press of its own.
towson.off_air: INVENTED. Married to Nikhil, a high school chemistry teacher. Runs a youth defense clinic on Saturday mornings.
gags: Treats every steal like a trophy for the shelf.
Gives a York Road traffic report during every timeout.
Tells Draco she's already read his notebook.
towson.compassion: Protective of the scrappy kids on the bench.
towson.worldview: Pressure reveals character, and everyone deserves a team that has their back.

uncw.bio: Surfer Sid was born on Oahu to a Samoan-Hawaiian family, moved to Wrightsville Beach as a teenager, and spent years as a surf instructor and lifeguard before he ever saw a box score. He edits The Wilmington Lantern and reads every UNCW Seahawks game like a surf report, rooting openly and drifting off mid-thought to check the swell. He usually catches up about three possessions late. Sid is short for Isidore, which only his grandmother uses. He considers a good fast break a barrel.
uncw.backstory: INVENTED. Born in Laie on Oahu to a Samoan-Hawaiian family, then moved to Wrightsville Beach when his mother took a nursing job in Wilmington. Worked as a surf instructor and lifeguard.
uncw.beat: INVENTED. Started giving Seahawks scores in his surf report on a beach radio show; the Lantern hired him, and Hardwood Bricks followed the swell.
uncw.look: Teal sequined naval blazer with gold captain stripes on the sleeves and a UNCW patch, wavy dark hair, big easy smile, holding a microphone (portrait).
uncw.favorite: To research: a real Seahawks player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Every fast break is a barrel.
Charleston's anchor would wear a tuxedo to the beach.
Wilmington in January is basically still summer.
uncw.off_air: INVENTED. Surfs every morning before the sun is up. Lives with two roommates and a surfboard named Isidore.
gags: Drifts off to check the swell and catches up three possessions late.
Calls every three-pointer a 'ten-foot set.'
Shows up to rivalry games in flip-flops to annoy Bea.
uncw.compassion: Lifeguard instincts; he'll paddle out for anyone.
uncw.worldview: Everybody catches a wave eventually, and you help them paddle out.

william-mary.bio: Sir Alistair Finch was born in Leicester to an Indian family, moved to Virginia as a boy, and spent years as a costumed interpreter in Williamsburg's historic district before finding his way to the Tribe. The knighthood is self-awarded and he will not discuss it. He edits The Williamsburg Courier, applauds good defense from both benches, and treats the free throw as the last refuge of decorum. Alistair is forever three courtesies behind the action, usually because he's tipping his hat to the officials.
william-mary.backstory: INVENTED. Born in Leicester, England, to an Indian family that moved to Newport News when he was a boy. Worked as a costumed interpreter in Williamsburg's historic district.
william-mary.beat: INVENTED. Gave impromptu Tribe score updates to tour groups in full colonial dress; the Courier hired him, and Hardwood Bricks kept the wig.
william-mary.look: Dark green sequined velvet coat with gold trim and a William & Mary crest, white lace jabot, powdered white wig, holding a microphone with a sly smile (portrait).
william-mary.favorite: To research: a real Tribe player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: The free throw is the last refuge of decorum.
Hampton plays with admirable discipline, and he says so, with a bow.
Williamsburg in winter is the finest setting for a basketball game.
william-mary.off_air: INVENTED. Married to Meera, a pediatrician who has never once worn a wig. Collects antique teacups and uses them for halftime tea.
gags: Tips his hat to the officials after every call, even the bad ones.
Applauds both benches, occasionally the wrong one.
Sends Kendra a formal letter of congratulations after every Hampton win.
william-mary.compassion: Kind to everyone, including the officials.
william-mary.worldview: Decency is a team sport, and good manners cost nothing.

binghamton.bio: Dana Kessler dispatched school buses in the Southern Tier for most of her career, which means she has made more snow-day calls than any meteorologist alive. She edits The Binghamton Clarion and covers the Bearcats with veteran calm, measuring every season in cloudy days and spiedie sandwiches. Dana is unflappable, warm and impossible to rush. She believes gray skies make bright nights in the arena feel brighter, and she will defend the local spiedie marinade against all comers, including her rival in Albany.
binghamton.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in Johnson City, the daughter of a shoe factory worker and a church secretary. Spent decades as a school bus dispatcher in Broome County.
binghamton.beat: INVENTED. Her snow-day announcements always ended with a Bearcats score, so the Clarion gave her a column and Hardwood Bricks gave her a desk.
binghamton.look: White Binghamton hoodie with green lettering and drawstrings, chin-length graying bob, calm closed-mouth smile (portrait).
binghamton.favorite: To research: a real Bearcats player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Gray skies make the arena feel brighter.
Albany's anchor talks like a committee hearing, and Dana means that kindly.
A spiedie is the best postgame meal in America.
binghamton.off_air: INVENTED. Widowed, with two grown daughters who call every Sunday. Marinates her spiedies for exactly as long as her mother did and won't say how long.
gags: Counts the season in cloudy days.
Gives every win a spiedie rating.
Sends Renee a marinade recipe with key ingredients blacked out.
binghamton.compassion: High; knows every bus driver's name.
binghamton.worldview: Small towns take care of each other on gray days, and that's the whole job.

bryant.bio: Marcus Bell graduated from business school, launched a startup selling artisanal ice that melted almost immediately, and pivoted to covering the Bryant Bulldogs. He edits The Smithfield Pilot and talks about wins in business-school language: quarterly returns, market share, synergy. He has a ten-year plan for the program and a five-year plan for his apartment. Marcus is young, earnest and frequently wrong about what words mean. He believes the Bulldogs are a startup on the rise and that he is, too.
bryant.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in Cranston, the son of a car dealership finance manager and a dental office manager. Graduated from business school and briefly ran an artisanal ice startup.
bryant.beat: INVENTED. Pitched Hardwood Bricks a slide deck on 'disrupting mid-major coverage'; they hired him to stop the slides.
bryant.look: Black quarter-zip with gold shoulders and a Bryant wordmark, short dark hair, clean-shaven, polite closed-mouth smile (portrait).
bryant.favorite: To research: a real Bulldogs player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Every Bulldogs win is a strong quarter.
UMass Lowell's anchor would make a great operations VP.
Smithfield is a growth market and the Bulldogs are a buy.
bryant.off_air: INVENTED. Lives with two roommates and a whiteboard full of business ideas. Owns three identical quarter-zips and considers that a capsule wardrobe.
gags: Uses business jargon wrong with total confidence.
Pitches the Bulldogs as a 'buy' on air.
Tells Kerry her grit has 'great ROI'; she does not take it as a compliment.
bryant.compassion: Sincere; wants everyone to succeed, especially startups.
bryant.worldview: Growth is for everyone, and he's slowly learning that a market isn't a community.
bryant.rube: Yes: the lovable business-school kid who keeps pivoting.

maine.bio: Hollis Grant plowed roads for the state and ran a hardware store in Old Town, and he talks the way Mainers shovel: only as much as necessary. He edits The Orono Courier and covers the Maine Black Bears with laconic Down East fairness, saving his rare praise for a team that plays through the cold. Hollis drives I-95 to every road game and knows every rest stop by name. He has said 'Ayuh' on air more than any other word. Folks in Orono consider that efficient.
maine.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in Old Town, the son of a paper mill worker and a school cook. Plowed roads for the state and ran a hardware store.
maine.beat: INVENTED. Posted Black Bears scores on the hardware store sign; the Courier hired him, and Hardwood Bricks found him by driving past.
maine.look: Navy polo with light-blue shoulders and a Maine script logo, short gray hair, tan, calm closed-mouth smile (portrait).
maine.favorite: To research: a real Black Bears player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Snow is just weather.
UNH's anchor is a hockey fan who wandered into the wrong rink.
I-95 at night is the most honest road in New England.
maine.off_air: INVENTED. Married to Ruth, a retired postmistress who does the talking for both of them. Splits firewood every Saturday morning.
gags: Says 'Ayuh' as a full analysis.
Names every I-95 rest stop on the way to road games.
Gives Tom one sentence of praise a season and makes him earn it.
maine.compassion: Quiet, but he shows up with a shovel.
maine.worldview: Say less and do more, and the town will notice.
maine.rube: Yes: the lovable Down East man of few words.

njit.bio: Priya Raman spent years as a structural engineer on bridge retrofits in North Jersey, and she still sees every game as a load-bearing problem. She edits The Newark Argus and diagrams every NJIT Highlanders win as a sound structure and every loss as a design review. Priya grew up in Newark in a Trinidadian family, which is why she's fluent in both calypso and engineering spec sheets. She's quick, precise and funny. She has inspected the Highlanders' arena seating and found it structurally excellent.
njit.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in Vailsburg, Newark, the daughter of a Trinidadian bridge inspector and a Jersey-born nurse. Worked as a structural engineer on bridge retrofits.
njit.beat: INVENTED. Wrote a Highlanders recap as a structural inspection report and posted it to her firm's bulletin board; the Argus saw it, and Hardwood Bricks followed.
njit.look: Red NJIT hoodie with navy sleeves and big white letters, natural curly hair framing her face, calm closed-mouth smile (portrait).
njit.favorite: To research: a real Highlanders player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: A good pick-and-roll is load-bearing.
UMBC's anchor plans four moves ahead and forgets the shot clock.
Newark has the best engineers in the world, and the Highlanders prove it.
njit.off_air: INVENTED. Plays steel pan with a community band. Has a houseplant she has load-tested.
gags: Diagrams every play as a structural load.
Files a 'design review' after every loss.
Sends Renee building code citations during close games.
njit.compassion: High; mentors young women engineers on weekends.
njit.worldview: Build things that hold up and that hold everyone, not just the people at the top.

new-hampshire.bio: Tom Leary drove an ice resurfacer at a Seacoast rink for decades and coached peewee hockey on weekends, which is why he keeps calling three-pointers 'slap shots.' He edits The Durham Beacon and covers the UNH Wildcats with the passion of a lifelong hockey fan still learning basketball. Tom cheers a beat too late and hollers 'shoot the puck' at least once a game. He is a shameless homer and a sweetheart. He has never admitted he likes basketball more now, but he does.
new-hampshire.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in Dover, New Hampshire, the son of a lineman and a school nurse. Drove an ice resurfacer at a Seacoast rink for most of his life and coached peewee hockey.
new-hampshire.beat: INVENTED. Called Wildcats basketball games from the rink's PA by accident when the hockey game was snowed out; the Beacon heard it, and Hardwood Bricks adopted him.
new-hampshire.look: Blue and white UNH quarter-zip with a Wildcat logo, short white hair, tanned and lined face, easy closed-mouth smile (portrait).
new-hampshire.favorite: To research: a real Wildcats player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Basketball needs a penalty box.
Maine's anchor would be a great goalie: never says a word.
Durham in January belongs on a postcard.
new-hampshire.off_air: INVENTED. Married to Peg, a retired figure skating coach. Still skates every morning at the rink he used to resurface.
gags: Calls three-pointers 'slap shots.'
Cheers a beat too late.
Asks Hollis whether basketball has icing.
new-hampshire.compassion: Big-hearted; coaches every kid who shows up.
new-hampshire.worldview: It's never too late to learn a new game, or a new neighbor.
new-hampshire.rube: Yes: the lovable hockey guy in the wrong arena.

ualbany.bio: Renee Castillo worked as a legislative aide in Albany, counting votes in the hallways of the state capitol, and now she counts possessions for the UAlbany Great Danes. She edits The Albany Lantern and treats every win like a measure passed without amendment and every loss like a filibuster. Renee is quick, warm and fiercely fond of the people who wait in the capitol's long lines. She believes in procedure, fair play, and that every citizen deserves a hearing, including the bench.
ualbany.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in Albany's South End, the daughter of a Dominican-American state clerk and a court stenographer. Worked as a legislative aide counting votes.
ualbany.beat: INVENTED. Wrote Great Danes recaps in the style of legislative summaries and left them in the capitol cafeteria; the Lantern hired her, and Hardwood Bricks followed the paper trail.
ualbany.look: Purple polo with a gold UAlbany logo, long light-brown hair, calm closed-mouth smile (portrait).
ualbany.favorite: To research: a real Great Danes player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Every win is a motion carried.
Binghamton's anchor is lovely but filibusters every snow day.
Albany is the most underrated city in New York.
ualbany.off_air: INVENTED. Volunteers at a legal aid clinic on weekends. Owns a gavel she uses to open Sunday brunch.
gags: Calls every win a 'motion carried.'
Files 'amendments' to bad calls.
Sends Dana a formal notice of hearing before every rivalry game.
ualbany.compassion: High; believes everyone deserves a hearing.
ualbany.worldview: Government works when the people in the long lines get heard.

umbc.bio: Darnell Hughes taught middle school math and coached the chess club in Catonsville for years before he started coaching his readers through UMBC Retrievers games. He edits The Catonsville Sentinel and sees every game as a chess match, always four moves ahead and usually forgetting the shot clock. Darnell is cool, strategic and fond of reminding people the Retrievers can bite. He believes the long game is the only game. He once lost a chess match to his own student and framed the board.
umbc.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in Arbutus, Maryland, the son of a federal records clerk and a church secretary. Taught middle school math and coached the chess club.
umbc.beat: INVENTED. Diagrammed Retrievers possessions as chess notation in the faculty newsletter; the Sentinel hired him, and Hardwood Bricks took the board.
umbc.look: Black UMBC hoodie with gold lettering and a gold-lined hood, short brown hair, clean-shaven, calm closed-mouth smile (portrait).
umbc.favorite: To research: a real Retrievers player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Every possession is a chess move.
NJIT's anchor builds bridges; he builds traps.
The Retrievers can bite, and everyone should remember it.
umbc.off_air: INVENTED. Married to Carla, a high school principal. Plays chess with his students on Thursday nights.
gags: Plans four moves ahead and forgets the shot clock.
Calls every steal a 'fork.'
Challenges Priya to chess before every rivalry game; she inspects the board for structural flaws.
umbc.compassion: Quiet, deep; mentors every kid who loses.
umbc.worldview: Play the long game and teach the kids to see the whole board.
umbc.rube: Yes: the lovable chess teacher who forgot the clock.

umass-lowell.bio: Kerry Flanagan grew up in Lowell's Acre neighborhood, the granddaughter of mill workers, and spent years working swing shifts at a machine shop before she ever picked up a pen. She edits The Lowell Spectator and covers the UMass Lowell River Hawks like a shift supervisor: she wants to see the team punch the clock and grind out the hard minutes. Kerry is quick-tongued, fair and proud of her city. She thinks basketball is honest work and that honest work deserves a good paycheck.
umass-lowell.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in the Acre, Lowell, the granddaughter of mill workers. Worked swing shifts at a machine shop.
umass-lowell.beat: INVENTED. Wrote River Hawks recaps on the back of time cards; a foreman passed one to the Spectator, and Hardwood Bricks found it on the break-room board.
umass-lowell.look: Navy and red UMass Lowell quarter-zip, long straight brown hair, bright friendly smile (portrait).
umass-lowell.favorite: To research: a real River Hawks player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Every win is a full shift.
UNH's anchor still thinks there's a puck.
Lowell built America, and the River Hawks play like it.
umass-lowell.off_air: INVENTED. Lives with her grandmother in a triple-decker. Bowls candlepin every Thursday night.
gags: Calls every win 'a full shift.'
Punches a time clock on the desk before every broadcast.
Tells Tom the whistle is not a faceoff.
umass-lowell.compassion: High; fights for the night shift.
umass-lowell.worldview: Honest work deserves honest pay, and a mill town knows how to look after its own.

vermont.bio: Asa Whitcomb grew up on a hill farm outside Burlington and ran a sugarhouse for most of his life, and he still believes every basketball season should be measured in maple taps. He edits The Burlington Chronicle and covers the Vermont Catamounts with gentle Green Mountain patience, drifting into sugaring stories mid-game. Asa is reliably the last to know the Catamounts were favored. He keeps a jug of syrup on the desk. He considers it a measuring tool.
vermont.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up on a hill farm in Jericho, Vermont, the son of dairy farmers. Ran a sugarhouse and drove a milk truck for decades.
vermont.beat: INVENTED. Gave Catamounts score updates to customers at the sugarhouse; the Chronicle hired him, and Hardwood Bricks followed the steam.
vermont.look: Gold polo with green trim and a Vermont script logo, short gray hair, tanned and lined face, calm closed-mouth smile (portrait).
vermont.favorite: To research: a real Catamounts player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Basketball season should be measured in maple taps.
Albany's anchor would make a good sugarhouse manager.
Burlington in January is the best place to watch basketball, and to boil sap.
vermont.off_air: INVENTED. Married to Edie, a retired schoolteacher. Still taps his own trees every spring.
gags: Drifts into sugaring stories mid-game.
Learns the Catamounts were favored only after the game.
Sends Renee a jug of syrup with a note reading 'for the hearing.'
vermont.compassion: Warm; shares his syrup with everyone.
vermont.worldview: Good things take time, and neighbors are what make the waiting sweet.

charlotte.bio: Desmond Okoye grew up in Plaza Midwood, where his stepfather Emeka ran the rec center gym and taught him to box out before he could ride a bike. He spent fifteen years as a middle school PE teacher and JV coach before The Charlotte Courant asked him to cover the 49ers. He grades fairly, prefers a good possession to a highlight, and keeps a binder of rotations nobody asked for. He has never once found his car in an uptown parking deck on the first try.
charlotte.backstory: INVENTED. Raised in Plaza Midwood by his mother and his stepfather Emeka, who ran the neighborhood rec center gym. Taught middle school PE and coached JV for fifteen years.
charlotte.beat: INVENTED. Wrote a seven-page letter to The Charlotte Courant about a missed boxout in a 49ers loss; the editor hired him to keep writing them, shorter.
charlotte.look: Gold quarter-zip with green trim and CHARLOTTE on the chest, short dark hair, clean-shaven, steady half smile (portrait).
charlotte.favorite: To research: a real 49ers player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Uptown's glass towers are lovely, but none of them can defend a ball screen.
A charge taken in the first half is worth more than a dunk in the second.
Greenville barbecue is fine; Greenville rebounding is the real problem.
charlotte.off_air: INVENTED. Married to Renee, a pharmacist who timed his first date with a stopwatch to prove a point. Coaches his daughter's rec team and makes the kids say 'contest' before every shot.
gags: Draws a boxout diagram on any napkin within reach, including other people's.
Gets lost in every uptown parking deck and narrates his escape like a broken press break.
Politely corrects Tamsin's barbecue facts; she politely ignores him.
charlotte.temperament: Even-keeled; raises his voice only for a missed rotation.
charlotte.disposition: Earnest, orderly, a little square, proud of it.
charlotte.compassion: High for kids learning the game; patient with anyone who tries.
charlotte.humor: Dry and accidental; funniest when he doesn't know he's being funny.
charlotte.worldview: The fundamentals are a kind of respect: for teammates, for the work, for the people in the stands.
charlotte.rube: Yes: the earnest fundamentals nerd who can't work a parking deck.

east-carolina.bio: Tamsin Whitley grew up in Pitt County in a family that has argued about vinegar sauce for four generations. She spent her twenties as a night-shift respiratory therapist at ECU Health, catching Pirates games on the breakroom radio, before The Greenville Ledger offered her a column. She grades a loss honestly and defends Greenville's honor to anyone outside it. Every argument she has ever had, she has settled with barbecue, and the barbecue is undefeated.
east-carolina.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up outside Greenville, the youngest of four in a family that cooks whole hog for every wedding and funeral. Worked night shifts as a respiratory therapist at ECU Health.
east-carolina.beat: INVENTED. Her breakroom game recaps went around the hospital by text until a Ledger editor's mother was a patient and passed one along.
east-carolina.look: Purple hoodie with gold drawstrings and EAST CAROLINA across the chest, brown hair pulled back, wide bright smile (portrait).
east-carolina.favorite: To research: a real Pirates player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Tomato in barbecue sauce is a decision you make alone, and you live with it.
Charlotte has more buildings than Greenville and fewer good nights out.
A loud Tuesday crowd in Greenville is worth six points and a hush puppy.
east-carolina.off_air: INVENTED. Lives with her rescue beagle, Pork Chop, and a smoker she bought before she bought a couch. Calls her granddaddy after every game for his grade.
gags: Rates every opponent's town by its barbecue, then by its basketball.
Mails Desmond a bottle of vinegar sauce after every Pirates win; he sends back a diagram.
Breathing coach voice when the Pirates blow a lead: 'In for four, out for four.'
east-carolina.temperament: Quick to fire, quick to forgive, quickest to laugh.
east-carolina.disposition: Proud, loud, and loyal to the bone.
east-carolina.appropriateness: PG, with some Down East color she gets bleeped for.
east-carolina.compassion: Deep; she's held a lot of hands at three in the morning.
east-carolina.humor: Big, warm, and pointed, with a punchline in a takeout box.
east-carolina.worldview: Eastern North Carolina gets overlooked, so it has to be loud, and it has earned the right.

memphis.bio: Calvin Booker played bass in Midtown bar bands for twenty years and tuned pianos for the churches that paid better. He hears every Tigers run as a horn section coming in and will forgive a sloppy first half if the second one swings. The Memphis Lantern hired him after his letters to the editor started arriving in verse. He is a shameless homer, and he is not sorry. He once called a timeout a key change.
memphis.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in Cooper-Young, the son of a record store owner. Played bass in bar bands and tuned pianos across Shelby County for twenty years.
memphis.beat: INVENTED. Sent The Memphis Lantern a season of Tigers recaps written as liner notes; they ran one as a joke, the readers wrote back, and he got a desk.
memphis.look: Heathered blue-gray quarter-zip with MEMPHIS stitched in white, short graying brown hair, tan, calm closed-mouth smile (portrait).
memphis.favorite: To research: a real Tigers player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: A good run has a bass line, and if you can't hear it you're not listening.
Birmingham has steel; Memphis has soul, and soul travels better.
Halftime is a set break, and some teams need to change the setlist.
memphis.off_air: INVENTED. Married to Lorraine, who manages a hardware store and books him gigs he forgets about. Still owns every record his father couldn't sell.
gags: Calls every timeout a key change.
Hums the bass line of a Tigers run on air and can't be stopped.
Swaps playlists with Terrence before rivalry games and pretends to hate his.
memphis.temperament: Mellow until the second half swings, then fully on his feet.
memphis.appropriateness: PG. Says 'Lord have mercy' at a volume.
memphis.compassion: Big; he forgives a bad half the way you forgive a wrong note.
memphis.humor: Musician's patter, warm and a little corny.
memphis.worldview: Memphis makes beautiful things out of hard times, and its team should too.
memphis.rube: Yes: the lovable old bass player who hears horns that aren't there.

north-texas.bio: Wade Kittredge spent twelve years holding a stop-slow sign on I-35 and has opinions about every lane closure between Denton and Dallas. He roots hard for the Mean Green, trusts the courthouse square more than any stat sheet, and still can't name the defense they played. The Denton Courier hired him because his game notes doubled as a traffic report. He has arrived at tip-off on time exactly once and talks about it like a championship.
north-texas.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in a ranch house off Loop 288, son of a school bus mechanic. Worked highway traffic control on I-35 construction for twelve years.
north-texas.beat: INVENTED. Called in to a Denton radio show with a traffic update and a Mean Green take in the same breath; the Courier's editor was listening in a merge lane.
north-texas.look: Black cap, black hoodie with NORTH TEXAS in green, light stubble, easy grin (portrait).
north-texas.favorite: To research: a real Mean Green player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: The courthouse square on a Saturday tells you more about this town than a box score.
San Antonio thinks it has traffic. San Antonio has never met I-35 in Denton.
Every loss is at least ten percent the construction's fault.
north-texas.off_air: INVENTED. Married to Marisa, a band teacher who navigates. Owns four orange safety vests and wears one to cut the grass.
gags: Gives the game's flow as a traffic report: 'heavy congestion in the paint.'
Never knows the opponent's defense; guesses 'zone' with total confidence.
Sends Ximena photos of I-35 orange barrels as 'scouting reports.'
north-texas.temperament: Easygoing, mildly frazzled, permanently running late.
north-texas.appropriateness: G, with the occasional 'come on, now.'
north-texas.compassion: Kind to everyone stuck in traffic, which is everyone.
north-texas.humor: Self-deprecating, the joke is always on him.
north-texas.worldview: A town is the people stuck in the same jam together, being decent about it.
north-texas.rube: Yes: the lovable highway-cone rube who's still parking at the half.

rice.bio: Eleanor Pryce taught AP English in Houston for eighteen years and never once gave a paper an A without comments. She grades every Owls possession the same way, and she is proudest when they win by being smarter than they are bigger. The Houston Almanac hired her after she sent in a marked-up box score. She keeps a red pen behind her ear on air and has been asked, kindly, to stop circling things on the monitor.
rice.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in the Heights, daughter of a bookbinder and a church organist. Taught AP English at a Houston public high school for eighteen years.
rice.beat: INVENTED. Mailed The Houston Almanac a box score with her margin notes and a letter grade; the editor called the next morning.
rice.look: Royal-blue polo with gray shoulders and RICE on the chest, shoulder-length brown hair, composed half smile (portrait).
rice.favorite: To research: a real Owls player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: An assist is a sentence with a subject and a verb; a turnover is a fragment.
Size is a gift; intelligence is a habit.
New Orleans food is wonderful, and Beau's analysis is a footnote to it.
rice.off_air: INVENTED. Married to Paul, a ship pilot who can't follow basketball and asks good questions anyway. Runs a neighborhood book club that keeps reading sports novels by accident.
gags: Grades every half like a term paper: 'B minus, strong thesis, weak transitions.'
Circles quick threes in red ink on the monitor.
Corrects Beau's grammar during rivalry week; he thanks her with a muffuletta.
rice.temperament: Composed, exacting, quietly delighted by a well-made play.
rice.appropriateness: G. 'Disappointing' is her worst word and she means it.
rice.compassion: Firm and kind; she believes everyone can improve.
rice.worldview: Being smart and generous on the court is a civic virtue, and so is being smart and generous off it.

south-florida.bio: Nico Albrecht grew up in Seminole Heights and spent his early twenties renting kayaks on the Hillsborough River, which made him an expert on the four o'clock thunderstorm. He thinks every Bulls win starts a dynasty and every loss is the weather's fault, and he is cheerfully wrong about both. The Tampa Argus hired him after his weather blog accidentally became a Bulls blog. His dynasty column has been drafted eleven times and published zero.
south-florida.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in Seminole Heights with a German grandfather who ran a bakery. Rented kayaks on the Hillsborough River and kept a weather blog on the side.
south-florida.beat: INVENTED. His weather blog started rating Bulls games by lightning delay; the Argus noticed when the traffic beat their sports page.
south-florida.look: Gold cap and gold polo with green trim and SOUTH FLORIDA on the chest, short beard, boyish grin (portrait).
south-florida.favorite: To research: a real Bulls player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Every Bulls winning streak is the start of a dynasty until proven otherwise.
Akron can keep its snow; a Tampa thunderstorm has real stage presence.
The arena should have a lightning delay just for drama.
south-florida.off_air: INVENTED. Lives with two roommates and a parrot named Doppler. Checks the radar before every decision, including lunch.
gags: Blames the four o'clock storm for losses at seven.
Drafts a dynasty column after every win; his editor deletes it.
Sends Marcus a radar screenshot every time it snows in Akron.
south-florida.temperament: Sunny, excitable, quick to overreact in both directions.
south-florida.disposition: Boundless optimist with a soggy streak.
south-florida.compassion: Big-hearted; will lend anyone his last umbrella.
south-florida.humor: Goofy, overconfident, the punchline is always him.
south-florida.worldview: Every season can be the one, and that's the fun of it.
south-florida.rube: Yes: the sunburned optimist who thinks every win is a dynasty.

temple.bio: Gina Falcone drove a SEPTA bus up and down Broad Street for twenty-six years and learned to respect anyone who holds their ground. She respects a charge taken more than a dunk made, and she grades the Owls with North Philly honesty: she'll tell them when they stink and defend them to anyone else. The North Philadelphia Clarion hired her after a passenger turned out to be the editor. She still announces timeouts like stops.
temple.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in a rowhouse in Fishtown, one of five, father a roofer, mother a lunch lady. Drove a SEPTA bus on Broad Street for twenty-six years.
temple.beat: INVENTED. Gave a rider an unprompted breakdown of Temple's zone over four stops; the rider ran the Clarion's sports page.
temple.look: Cherry quarter-zip with white collar and TEMPLE on the chest, chin-length brown bob, firm closed-mouth smile (portrait).
temple.favorite: To research: a real Owls player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: A charge is the bravest play in basketball, and it should count for three.
Philadelphia snow is not weather; it's a test of character.
Greenville can keep its barbecue; we've got toughness and a cheesesteak.
temple.off_air: INVENTED. Widowed, close with her three sisters, and grandmother to twins. Bowls Thursday nights and keeps a scorecard on the fridge.
gags: Announces timeouts like a bus stop: 'Broad and Cecil B. Moore, everybody off.'
Keeps a running count of charges taken on a tally board she made herself.
Tells Tamsin her barbecue is 'very nice, dear,' which is the worst thing she can say.
temple.temperament: Tough as a February bus shelter, soft underneath.
temple.appropriateness: PG-13 in her heart, PG on air.
temple.compassion: Fierce for the working people in the stands; no patience for slackers.
temple.humor: Deadpan Philly, with a wink at the end.
temple.worldview: Work hard, look out for your block, and don't let anybody tell you North Philly isn't worth it.

tulane.bio: Beau Thibodeaux worked the fryer at a Magazine Street po'boy shop for fifteen years and still grades every Green Wave game against what he ate that day. Somehow the po'boy always wins. The New Orleans Spectator hired him after his food reviews kept wandering into the second half. He roots openly and follows about half of it, the other half being lunch. He has blamed losses on skipping gumbo and has never once been right.
tulane.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in the Irish Channel, son of a streetcar operator. Worked the fryer at a Magazine Street po'boy shop for fifteen years.
tulane.beat: INVENTED. Wrote restaurant reviews for the Spectator until one review was mostly about a Tulane comeback; readers wanted more.
tulane.look: Sky-blue polo with olive trim and TULANE on the chest, short brown hair, wide easy smile (portrait).
tulane.favorite: To research: a real Green Wave player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: The pregame meal decides more games than the pregame speech.
Houston has a lot of good restaurants, and it doesn't deserve them.
A Tuesday night in February in New Orleans beats a Saturday anywhere else.
tulane.off_air: INVENTED. Married to Odile, a nurse who sets his lunch alarms. Rides the streetcar to every home game and tells strangers the score.
gags: Rates every win on a scale of one to five po'boys.
Blames losses on skipping the gumbo.
Mails Eleanor a muffuletta to apologize for his grammar every rivalry week.
tulane.appropriateness: PG. 'Mais, no' is as rough as it gets.
tulane.compassion: Feeds people first and asks questions later.
tulane.worldview: A city is its table, and everybody gets a seat.
tulane.rube: Yes: the lovable food-first rube who watches half the game.

tulsa.bio: Darla Pruitt spent thirty-four years as an aircraft mechanic at the American Airlines maintenance base and retired with steady hands and strong opinions about art deco. She calls the Golden Hurricane like a weather report: calm, accurate, and a little proud when the wind picks up. The Tulsa Dispatch hired her after she wrote a letter grading their coverage. She drives Route 66 to every road game she can reach, and some she can't.
tulsa.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in a bungalow off Route 66 in east Tulsa, daughter of a diner cook and a phone company lineman. Worked thirty-four years as an aircraft mechanic.
tulsa.beat: INVENTED. Retired, bored, and sharp; her letter correcting the Dispatch's box score was so precise they offered her a column instead of a correction.
tulsa.look: Royal-blue quarter-zip with gold shoulders and TULSA on the chest, chin-length brown bob, calm composed smile (portrait).
tulsa.favorite: To research: a real Golden Hurricane player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Tulsa's art deco downtown is the best-dressed skyline in the country, and nobody has to agree.
Wichita has the wind; Tulsa knows what to do with it.
A good defense should be inspected like a jet engine: every rivet, every time.
tulsa.off_air: INVENTED. Married forty years to Carl, a retired band director who hums through her broadcasts. Gives walking tours of deco buildings to anyone who stands still.
gags: Gives the game's flow as a forecast: 'gusts in the second half.'
Inspects the scorer's table like a preflight check.
Tells Hank his farm-equipment metaphors need a maintenance log.
tulsa.disposition: Practical, observant, warmer than she lets on.
tulsa.appropriateness: G. Her worst is 'well, that's a shame.'
tulsa.compassion: Steady and practical; shows up with a casserole and a toolbox.
tulsa.worldview: Do the work right and the beautiful things last; Tulsa is proof.

uab.bio: Terrence Mabry welded beams in a Birmingham fabrication shop for twelve years, like his father and grandfather before him. He sees every Blazers game as iron work and values the hard hat over the highlight. The Birmingham Intelligencer hired him after he called in to a radio show and described a zone defense as a truss. He roots without apology, and every win, to him, is forged. He still wears steel-toe boots to the press box.
uab.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in Ensley, third generation in the iron and steel trades. Welded structural beams in a fabrication shop for twelve years.
uab.beat: INVENTED. Called in to a Birmingham radio show from his lunch break and explained a Blazers zone using a truss diagram; the Intelligencer's editor was stuck in traffic listening.
uab.look: Gold hoodie with green trim and UAB across the chest, short brown hair, clean-shaven, confident smile (portrait).
uab.favorite: To research: a real Blazers player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: A team without a big man who sets screens is a building without rebar.
Memphis has music; Birmingham built the stage.
Highlights fade; foundations don't.
uab.off_air: INVENTED. Married to Brandi, a high school chemistry teacher who explains his metaphors back to him. Restores old cast iron skillets and gives them away.
gags: Grades every game by metallurgy: 'that half was cast, not forged.'
Wears steel-toe boots to the press box and won't say why.
Sends Calvin a skillet after Blazers wins; Calvin sends a record back.
uab.temperament: Solid, earnest, slow to boil and hard to cool.
uab.appropriateness: PG. Shop-floor words held back by a hard hat.
uab.compassion: Believes in the people who do the work nobody sees.
uab.humor: Earnest and literal; his metaphors run too long and he knows it.
uab.worldview: Birmingham was built by working people, and the team should play like it.
uab.rube: Yes: the earnest steelworker who explains every game as a weld.

utsa.bio: Ximena Salazar grew up on the South Side of San Antonio and coached high school girls basketball for ten years, where she learned to fix a turnover problem and throw a party in the same week. She calls the Roadrunners with Fiesta energy and a coach's eye, sharp on the X's and O's and generous with the confetti when it's earned. The San Antonio Beacon hired her after her film breakdowns went around town.
utsa.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up on the South Side, the oldest of five, with a grandmother who ran a taqueria. Coached high school girls basketball for ten years.
utsa.beat: INVENTED. Her film breakdowns for her players got passed around by parents until one reached the Beacon's sports editor, who'd been looking for someone who could diagram.
utsa.look: Navy cap and navy quarter-zip with orange zipper and UTSA on the chest, hair pulled back, small confident smile (portrait).
utsa.favorite: To research: a real Roadrunners player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Breakfast tacos are a performance-enhancing food, and someone should study it.
Denton traffic is a lifestyle choice.
A team that doesn't celebrate a good win doesn't deserve the next one.
utsa.off_air: INVENTED. Married to Javier, a firefighter who hides cascarones in her bag. Still runs her old team's summer camp.
gags: Cracks a cascaron on air after every big win.
Rates every opponent's breakfast tacos, then their press break.
Sends Wade traffic updates every time she gets anywhere on time.
utsa.appropriateness: PG. Her coach voice does the cursing for her.
utsa.compassion: High; she remembers every kid she coached.
utsa.humor: Festive and quick, with a coach's needle.
utsa.worldview: Work hard, celebrate harder, and bring everybody to the party.

wichita-state.bio: Hank Dreiling sold combines and grain carts across south-central Kansas for twenty-five years, and he still compares every Shocker to a piece of farm equipment. He is shamelessly yellow and black and is usually the last person in the building to notice the final buzzer. The Wichita Ledger hired him after his sales newsletter ran three straight issues about basketball. He talks about the wind and the wheat the way other people talk about family.
wichita-state.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up on a wheat farm outside Wichita, the youngest of six boys. Sold farm equipment across south-central Kansas for twenty-five years.
wichita-state.beat: INVENTED. His farm-equipment sales newsletter drifted into Shocker game recaps, and farmers started requesting it for the basketball; the Ledger noticed.
wichita-state.look: Bright yellow and black polo with WICHITA STATE on the chest, short graying hair, big friendly smile (portrait).
wichita-state.favorite: To research: a real Shockers player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: A good point guard is a combine: steady, reliable, and loud.
Tulsa wind is a breeze; Wichita wind is a weather system.
The best basketball happens in the coldest month, and that's no accident.
wichita-state.off_air: INVENTED. Married to Joyce, a retired crop insurance adjuster who keeps him off ladders. Restores old tractors and names them after Shocker point guards he can't remember.
gags: Compares every player to a piece of farm equipment.
Keeps calling the game a few seconds after the final buzzer.
Tries to explain combine metaphors to Darla, who corrects his torque figures.
wichita-state.disposition: Shameless homer with a good heart.
wichita-state.compassion: Big; he's helped every neighbor bring in a crop.
wichita-state.humor: Farm-country hyperbole with himself as the punchline.
wichita-state.worldview: Work the ground, help your neighbor, and cheer loud for the home team.

app-state.bio: Ruthie Calloway spent sixteen winters on ski patrol in the High Country and is the only anchor on the network with a wilderness EMT card in her wallet. She swears the Mountaineers play better up high and cites the thin air as tactics, half joking. The Boone Courier hired her after her avalanche-safety column turned into a basketball column. Every road game, she checks the elevation of the opponent's arena before she checks their roster.
app-state.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in Watauga County, daughter of a Christmas tree farmer. Spent sixteen winters on ski patrol and as a wilderness EMT.
app-state.beat: INVENTED. Her weekly mountain-safety column started including Mountaineer box scores as 'trail conditions'; the Courier's readers asked for more trail.
app-state.look: Black hoodie with APP STATE in gold across the chest, brown hair pulled back, steady smile (portrait).
app-state.favorite: To research: a real Mountaineers player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Elevation is a home-court advantage and anyone who says otherwise hasn't climbed to Boone in February.
Georgia Southern has gnats; we have weather.
Every team should practice in a snowstorm at least once.
app-state.off_air: INVENTED. Married to Jodie, a luthier who builds banjos. Owns three pairs of snowshoes and one pair of real shoes.
gags: Lists the opposing arena's elevation before tip-off, every game.
Warns visitors about altitude sickness with a straight face.
Sends Luke a fly swatter after every Mountaineer win.
app-state.temperament: Calm in a storm; louder in a close game.
app-state.compassion: High; she's carried people down mountains.
app-state.humor: Dry mountain humor with altitude puns.
app-state.worldview: The mountains make you humble and the mountains make you tough; both help on a Tuesday night in February.

arkansas-state.bio: Boyd Henley farms rice in the Delta outside Jonesboro and guides duck hunters before dawn, which is why he roots for the Red Wolves with a farmer's patience and a duck hunter's attention span. He misses the big play but never the concession stand. The Jonesboro Clarion hired him after he called in to a radio show from a duck blind. He once howled in press row after a win and has been asked, kindly, never to do it again.
arkansas-state.backstory: INVENTED. Third-generation Craighead County rice farmer who guides duck hunters in the off months. Took over the farm from his father at twenty-two.
arkansas-state.beat: INVENTED. Called in to a Jonesboro radio show from a duck blind at dawn with a Red Wolves take, whispered; the Clarion's editor thought it was the best thing he'd ever heard.
arkansas-state.look: Scarlet and black quarter-zip with ARKANSAS STATE on the chest, salt-and-pepper beard, graying hair, warm crinkly smile (portrait).
arkansas-state.favorite: To research: a real Red Wolves player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: The Delta light makes the court look slanted, and that's a real thing, probably.
Monroe is a nice town for a river town that isn't on our river.
Every arena should sell boiled peanuts, and every arena that doesn't is hiding something.
arkansas-state.off_air: INVENTED. Married to Patsy, who runs the farm books and the church bake sale with equal force. Owns a Labrador named Rebound who has never retrieved anything but a hot dog.
gags: Howls once in press row per win; the press row has filed a complaint.
Misses the game-winner every time because he's in the concession line.
Calls Celeste at dawn to argue about rivers.
arkansas-state.temperament: Patient, sleepy, then suddenly very loud.
arkansas-state.compassion: Big; he'll pull anybody's truck out of a ditch.
arkansas-state.humor: Gentle self-deprecation from a man who knows exactly who he is.
arkansas-state.worldview: Good land, good neighbors, good basketball, in that order.
arkansas-state.rube: Yes: the duck blind rube who missed the game-winner for a corn dog.

coastal-carolina.bio: Jada Pinckney managed a surf shop in Myrtle Beach and scouted rec-league talent on the side, and she still can't watch a pickup game without counting who doesn't get back on defense. She is young, quick, and teal to the bone, and covers the Chanticleers with beach-town ease and a scout's eye. The Conway Sentinel hired her after her rec-league scouting reports started circulating among actual coaches. She owns more teal than any one person should.
coastal-carolina.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in Conway, daughter of a shrimp boat captain and a hairdresser. Managed a Myrtle Beach surf shop and ran a summer rec league.
coastal-carolina.beat: INVENTED. Her rec-league scouting notes, written on surf wax receipts, got passed to a Sentinel editor who coached his kid's team.
coastal-carolina.look: Bronze polo with teal trim and COASTAL CAROLINA on the chest, brown hair pulled back, poised closed-mouth smile (portrait).
coastal-carolina.favorite: To research: a real Chanticleers player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Teal is not a color; it's a responsibility.
Boone is a lovely place to visit if you bring a coat and lower expectations.
Transition defense is a matter of character.
coastal-carolina.off_air: INVENTED. Surfs at dawn, rescues sea turtle nests with her mom on weekends. Has a teal surfboard, a teal car, and a teal cat collar for a cat who resents it.
gags: Counts possessions where nobody gets back on defense, out loud.
Rates every team's colors against teal; they all lose.
Sends Ruthie sunscreen before every App State road game.
coastal-carolina.appropriateness: PG. Surf slang in place of swearing.
coastal-carolina.compassion: Warm toward young players, cool toward lazy ones.
coastal-carolina.worldview: Small schools can be bright and bold, and Conway proves it.

georgia-southern.bio: Luke Bramlett spent ten years as a pest-control technician in Bulloch County, which makes him the only anchor alive who has a professional opinion about gnats. He bleeds blue and believes everything, including that swatting gnats counts as defense. The Statesboro Mercury hired him after his customers kept requesting his basketball takes along with their service. He is loudly confident and reliably a quarter behind, and he has never once calmed down.
georgia-southern.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up on a tobacco farm outside Statesboro, son of a church organist and a crop duster. Worked ten years as a pest-control technician.
georgia-southern.beat: INVENTED. Left handwritten Eagles takes on the back of service tickets; enough customers called the Mercury about it that they gave him a column.
georgia-southern.look: Navy quarter-zip with gold shoulders and GEORGIA SOUTHERN on the chest, full brown beard, wide friendly grin (portrait).
georgia-southern.favorite: To research: a real Eagles player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Gnats are part of the home-court advantage, and visitors should pay a fee.
Atlanta is just a very loud suburb of Statesboro.
A team that swats gnats can swat shots.
georgia-southern.off_air: INVENTED. Married to Kayla, an elementary school librarian who manages his blood pressure. Keeps a gnat-swatting tally on a whiteboard in his kitchen.
gags: Swats at gnats on air whether there are gnats or not.
Announces the score a quarter late with full confidence.
Keeps telling Keisha that Atlanta is 'a suburb'; she sends him a MARTA map.
georgia-southern.compassion: Big; he'll help anyone, including the gnats.
georgia-southern.humor: Earnest overstatement; the joke is that he means it.
georgia-southern.worldview: Statesboro is the center of the universe, and he can't be talked out of it.
georgia-southern.rube: Yes: the gnat-swatting optimist who's a quarter behind.

georgia-state.bio: Keisha Barnes drove MARTA trains on the downtown line for twelve years, which means she has watched more of Atlanta go by than almost anyone. She calls the Panthers at city speed, is impatient with lazy closeouts, and is proud of a commuter school that punches up. The Atlanta Spectator hired her after a rider recorded her play-by-play of a pickup game seen from the platform. She takes the train to every game and judges anyone who drives.
georgia-state.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in Kirkwood, daughter of a postal worker and a nurse. Drove MARTA trains on the downtown line for twelve years.
georgia-state.beat: INVENTED. A rider posted her intercom play-by-play of a pickup game near Five Points; the Spectator called her before the clip finished going around.
georgia-state.look: Blue and red Georgia State cap and blue hoodie with red hood and drawstrings, brown hair tucked back, calm confident smile (portrait).
georgia-state.favorite: To research: a real Panthers player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: A commuter school that plays this hard is the most Atlanta thing there is.
Statesboro is a fine town to visit when you need to remember what quiet is.
Closeouts are like train doors: if you're late, you missed it.
georgia-state.off_air: INVENTED. Lives with her sister and her nephew, whom she's raising to be a point guard. Keeps a map of every MARTA station she's eaten lunch near.
gags: Announces every timeout like a station stop.
Rides MARTA to the game and narrates it on air.
Sends Luke a MARTA map every time he calls Atlanta a suburb.
georgia-state.appropriateness: PG. Her eyebrows do the swearing.
georgia-state.compassion: High; she's watched the whole city ride by and knows who's struggling.
georgia-state.humor: Quick and dry, with a city-kid edge.
georgia-state.worldview: A city works when everyone gets where they're going; so does a team.

james-madison.bio: Grant Lockhart led cavern tours in the Shenandoah Valley for eighteen years and still narrates the Dukes like he's pointing out stalactites. He is a purple-and-gold optimist, reliably moved, and occasionally unsure which basket is ours. The Harrisonburg Chronicle hired him after a tour group of retired sportswriters asked for more of his halftime commentary. He knows every truck stop on I-81 by name and has a favorite at each.
james-madison.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up on a dairy farm outside Harrisonburg, son of a veterinarian. Led cavern tours in the Valley for eighteen years.
james-madison.beat: INVENTED. Started folding Dukes scores into his cavern tours; a group of retired newspaper editors on one tour sent the Chronicle a letter.
james-madison.look: Purple polo with gold piping and JAMES MADISON on the chest, short light brown hair, earnest closed-mouth smile (portrait).
james-madison.favorite: To research: a real Dukes player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: I-81 is the most interesting highway in America, and nobody can tell him otherwise.
Norfolk has a harbor; Harrisonburg has the Valley, and the Valley wins.
Every game is better with a tour guide's context.
james-madison.off_air: INVENTED. Married to Becca, a dairy goat farmer who rolls her eyes at his tours. Keeps a logbook of the license plates on I-81 tractor-trailers.
gags: Narrates a fast break like a cavern tour: 'and to your left, a layup.'
Points at the wrong basket at least once per game.
Gives Monique a guided tour of the Valley every rivalry week, whether she wants one or not.
james-madison.compassion: Big; he'll give anybody directions, usually wrong.
james-madison.humor: Tour-guide earnestness that turns funny on its own.
james-madison.worldview: The Shenandoah Valley is one of the most beautiful places on earth, and the Dukes are its pride.
james-madison.rube: Yes: the cavern tour guide who's pointing at the wrong basket.

louisiana.bio: Remy Fontenot repairs accordions for a living and plays rubboard in a zydeco band on weekends, so he keeps time to the music in his head through every Ragin' Cajuns game. He is shameless for the home team and has never once remembered the final score without checking. The Lafayette Observer hired him after his band's set breaks kept turning into game recaps. He danced a two-step in the press box once and still owes them a stat sheet.
louisiana.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in Carencro, son of a crawfish farmer and a church choir director. Learned to repair accordions from an uncle and has a shop off Johnston Street.
louisiana.beat: INVENTED. Gave Ragin' Cajuns updates during his band's set breaks; a Lafayette Observer reporter at the dance hall started quoting him, and then they hired him.
louisiana.look: Red cap worn backward with LOUISIANA on the strap, red and white polo, light stubble, wide easy grin (portrait).
louisiana.favorite: To research: a real Ragin' Cajuns player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Any team that can't dance to zydeco can't play transition defense.
Monroe is a fine town if you've never been to a fais do-do.
Every arena should have a band at halftime and a pot of gumbo at the door.
louisiana.off_air: INVENTED. Married to Gabrielle, a court reporter who checks the scores for him. His three kids all play accordion, badly, and he's proud of all of them.
gags: Two-steps in the press box after big wins.
Has to check the score before reporting it, every single time.
Sends Celeste zydeco playlists to 'loosen her up.'
louisiana.disposition: Shameless homer with a dance-floor heart.
louisiana.appropriateness: PG. 'Ça c'est bon' and nothing worse.
louisiana.compassion: Warm; he plays for free at every benefit in Acadiana.
louisiana.humor: Happy chaos, with the joke on him.
louisiana.worldview: Life's better with music and neighbors, and so is basketball.
louisiana.rube: Yes: the two-stepping accordion man who forgot the score.

louisiana-tech.bio: Lacey Gaspard spent twenty years as the parish extension agent in Lincoln Parish, teaching peach growers how to fight late frost and early bugs. She is piney-woods sharp and peach-sweet, in that order, a Bulldogs loyalist who praises a gritty win and politely shreds a lazy one. The Ruston Messenger hired her after a fruit-crop newsletter of hers ran a halftime analysis. She still judges effort by what she'd sell at the peach stand.
louisiana-tech.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up on a peach orchard outside Ruston, the daughter of a schoolteacher and an orchardist. Was the Lincoln Parish extension agent for twenty years.
louisiana-tech.beat: INVENTED. Her extension newsletter included a 'Bulldogs Report' in the margins; growers started calling the Messenger to ask for more.
louisiana-tech.look: Royal-blue quarter-zip with red shoulders and LOUISIANA TECH on the chest, blonde chin-length bob, warm smile (portrait).
louisiana-tech.favorite: To research: a real Bulldogs player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: A Ruston peach is worth the drive, and so is a Bulldogs game.
Monroe means well.
A lazy possession is like a bruised peach: you can still eat it, but nobody's paying full price.
louisiana-tech.off_air: INVENTED. Married to Dwight, a retired county surveyor who now runs the family peach stand. Makes peach cobbler for every home opener and refuses to share the recipe.
gags: Grades every half like a peach crop: 'firm, sweet, a little bruised.'
Politely shreds lazy closeouts with 'bless their hearts.'
Mails Celeste a peach every summer with a note: 'This is what Ruston does.'
louisiana-tech.appropriateness: G. 'Bless their hearts' does all the work.
louisiana-tech.compassion: High for growers, players, and anybody having a bad year.
louisiana-tech.humor: Southern politeness with a blade in it.
louisiana-tech.worldview: Hard work and good soil make something sweet; so does a good team.

marshall.bio: Dale Kinnaird carried mail in Huntington for thirty-three years and knows which porch on every route has the best pepperoni rolls. He is a gentle Herd lifer who measures every game in pepperoni rolls eaten, roots openly, and follows the action about one possession behind. The Huntington Courant hired him after he slipped game notes into mailboxes for years. He has never been rude to anyone, including referees, which some fans find suspicious.
marshall.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in a Huntington rowhouse, son of a railroad brakeman and a seamstress. Carried mail on the west side for thirty-three years.
marshall.beat: INVENTED. His handwritten Herd notes, left in mailboxes along his route, were collected by a retired Courant editor who sent them to the paper.
marshall.look: White quarter-zip with green trim and MARSHALL on the chest, short graying hair, warm crinkly smile (portrait).
marshall.favorite: To research: a real Thundering Herd player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: A pepperoni roll is the perfect halftime food, and science should back him up.
Boone is very high up for no good reason.
Slaw belongs on a hot dog and on a team that plays together.
marshall.off_air: INVENTED. Married to Shirley, a retired school secretary who keeps him off the rolls after nine. Volunteers at the food bank and knows every regular by name.
gags: Rates every game by pepperoni rolls eaten.
Arrives at every big play one possession late.
Mails Ruthie a pepperoni roll after every App State loss, with a sympathy card.
marshall.temperament: Gentle, patient, never in a hurry.
marshall.disposition: Kind, nostalgic, a little slow on the uptake.
marshall.compassion: Enormous; he's delivered good news and bad to every house in town.
marshall.worldview: A town is the people who keep showing up for each other.
marshall.rube: Yes: the gentle mailman rube who's one possession behind.

old-dominion.bio: Monique Tate spent eighteen years as a Navy officer and another ten as a harbor pilot, guiding container ships through the Norfolk channel. She is commanding, harbor-calm, and royal about it, and covers the Monarchs like the tide: patient, inevitable, and not inclined to apologize. The Norfolk Lantern hired her after she corrected their tide tables and their basketball coverage in the same letter. Her stare can stop a ship, and it has.
old-dominion.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in a Navy family in Ocean View, daughter of a chief petty officer and a schoolteacher. Served eighteen years as a Navy officer, then piloted ships through the harbor.
old-dominion.beat: INVENTED. Wrote the Lantern a letter correcting both their tide tables and their Monarchs recap; the editor hired her for the second correction.
old-dominion.look: Navy polo with silver trim and OLD DOMINION on the chest, long dark hair, olive skin, composed regal smile (portrait).
old-dominion.favorite: To research: a real Monarchs player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: The tide has never lost a game, and the Monarchs should take notes.
Harrisonburg is a lovely place to leave by I-81.
Good teams don't rush; they arrive.
old-dominion.off_air: INVENTED. Married to Ramon, a retired Coast Guard cook who keeps the house full of sofrito. Restores old ship clocks and sets them all to the tide.
gags: Gives the score as a tide report: 'high water, Monarchs.'
Straightens her imaginary crown after every bad loss.
Lets Grant finish his Valley tour, then sinks it with one sentence.
old-dominion.compassion: Steady; she's brought a lot of people home safely.
old-dominion.worldview: Patience, discipline, and showing up on time will carry you through most storms.

south-alabama.bio: Curtis Delchamps grew up on Mobile Bay's Eastern Shore and spent fifteen years running a bait shop that doubled as the neighborhood jubilee phone tree. He treats every Jaguars run like a jubilee: rare, glorious, and worth waking the whole neighborhood for. The Mobile Compass hired him after his late-night jubilee calls started including basketball scores. He has rung a cowbell in press row and been politely asked to stop.
south-alabama.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in Fairhope, son of a shrimper and a high school biology teacher. Ran a bait shop on the Eastern Shore for fifteen years.
south-alabama.beat: INVENTED. His 2 a.m. jubilee phone tree started including Jaguars scores; a Compass editor on the list was more excited about the scores than the flounder.
south-alabama.look: Navy and red hoodie with SOUTH ALABAMA across the chest, short brown hair, clean-shaven, bright grin (portrait).
south-alabama.favorite: To research: a real Jaguars player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: A jubilee and a Jaguars run are the same thing, and he can prove it with a gig and a bucket.
Troy is a lovely place with no water.
A Tuesday night game in February should start with a bell.
south-alabama.off_air: INVENTED. Married to Tamara, a nurse who has answered too many 2 a.m. phone calls. Owns six gigs and a bucket for every jubilee since he was nine.
gags: Rings a bell in press row for every big run.
Calls jubilees and Jaguar runs in the same voice.
Calls Earl at 2 a.m. after Jaguar wins; Earl calls back at 6 with the band.
south-alabama.temperament: Excitable, storytelling, wide awake at strange hours.
south-alabama.disposition: Joyful and sentimental about the bay.
south-alabama.compassion: Big; he'll share a cooler full of flounder with anybody.
south-alabama.humor: Tall-tale storytelling with himself as the fool.
south-alabama.worldview: The best things are rare and shared; the bay taught him that.
south-alabama.rube: Yes: the bait-shop storyteller who wakes the neighborhood.

southern-miss.bio: Savannah Rowe is a physical therapy assistant in Hattiesburg who runs the Longleaf Trace before dawn and measures effort in miles. She is Hub City quick and sharp-tongued, with no patience for anyone walking back on defense. The Hattiesburg Courant hired her after her running club's group chat posted her Golden Eagles breakdowns. She keeps a count of every lazy transition and will read it to you at mile eleven.
southern-miss.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in Hattiesburg, the youngest of three, daughter of a pharmacist and a high school track coach. Works as a physical therapy assistant.
southern-miss.beat: INVENTED. Her running club group chat got so many Golden Eagles breakdowns that a Courant reporter in the club forwarded them to the editor.
southern-miss.look: Black quarter-zip with gold zipper and SOUTHERN MISS on the chest, long brown hair, bright smile (portrait).
southern-miss.favorite: To research: a real Golden Eagles player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Walking back on defense is a choice and a character flaw.
Mobile Bay is pretty, but the Longleaf Trace has better pacing.
Every player should be able to run a ten-minute mile and a box-and-one.
southern-miss.off_air: INVENTED. Lives with her fiancee, Dana, and two greyhounds who are faster than any Golden Eagle. Has a marathon medal for every Mississippi county she's raced in.
gags: Counts every walk-back on defense, out loud.
Gives game pace in minutes per mile.
Sends Curtis a training plan every rivalry week.
southern-miss.compassion: High for injured players; none for lazy ones.
southern-miss.worldview: Effort is the one thing everyone can control, so everyone should.
