troy.bio: Earl Weatherby directed high school marching bands across the Wiregrass for thirty years, and he would trade a conference title for a good halftime show. He is a shameless Trojans man who forecasts every game wrong and announces it with total confidence. The Troy Clarion hired him after he spent a season writing band reviews that accidentally included the scores. He stands for the fight song, sits for nothing else, and owns his whistle still.
troy.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in Troy, son of a peanut farmer and a church pianist. Directed high school marching bands for thirty years.
troy.beat: INVENTED. Wrote band reviews for the Clarion that kept drifting into the second half; the editor moved him to sports so he could stop pretending.
troy.look: Cardinal cap and cardinal polo with silver piping and TROY on the chest, short graying hair, steady smile (portrait).
troy.favorite: To research: a real Trojans player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: A great halftime show is worth more than a conference title, and he will die on this hill.
Mobile can keep its bay; Troy has a band.
Every opponent should have to play a song before tip.
troy.off_air: INVENTED. Married forty years to Betty, a retired music teacher who can't stand his predictions. Keeps a whistle in every jacket and three in the truck.
gags: Predicts every game wrong, out loud, with absolute conviction.
Grades the halftime band before the first half.
Blows a whistle at Curtis when the Jaguars ring their bell.
troy.compassion: Big; he's taught a lot of kids to march in step.
troy.worldview: Everybody belongs in the band, and the band belongs in every game.
troy.rube: Yes: the marching band rube who predicts everything wrong.

ul-monroe.bio: Celeste Broussard dispatched barges on the Ouachita River for twelve years and learned how to stay calm while everything moves. She roots for the Warhawks with a river guide's patience and a scout's red pen, and she is quick on the draw when someone takes a bad shot. The Monroe Ledger hired her after her shot-selection notes, written on barge schedules, landed on an editor's desk. She has never lost an argument about the river.
ul-monroe.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in West Monroe, daughter of a towboat captain and a librarian. Dispatched barges on the Ouachita River for twelve years.
ul-monroe.beat: INVENTED. Wrote Warhawk shot charts on the backs of barge schedules; one got mixed into a delivery to the Ledger.
ul-monroe.look: Maroon hoodie with gold hood and UL MONROE across the chest, shoulder-length brown hair, composed smile (portrait).
ul-monroe.favorite: To research: a real Warhawks player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: The Ouachita River is underrated, and so are the Warhawks.
Ruston peaches are fine; the river has better fish.
A good shot and good shot selection are different things.
ul-monroe.off_air: INVENTED. Married to Julien, a high school band director who sends her zydeco when she's grumpy. Kayaks the river every Sunday and names the turtles.
gags: Gives the game's flow as a river report: 'current's running against us.'
Red-pens every bad shot on a clipboard.
Gets a peach from Lacey every summer and pretends not to be pleased.
ul-monroe.appropriateness: PG. River talk, low and steady.
ul-monroe.compassion: Steady; she knows everyone needs a calm voice sometimes.
ul-monroe.humor: Dry river wit, quick and understated.
ul-monroe.worldview: Rivers and teams both reward patience and punish shortcuts.

delaware.bio: Hank Sorensen sold poultry feed up and down the Delmarva Peninsula for twenty-eight years and had never been on an airplane for work until the Blue Hens joined Conference USA. Now he marvels at every airline mile, roots honestly for Delaware, and loses track of which time zone the opponent is in. The Newark Chronicle hired him after his feed-route newsletter started including box scores. He has gone to the wrong gate four times this season.
delaware.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up on a chicken farm outside Newark, son of a feed mill foreman. Sold poultry feed across Delmarva for twenty-eight years.
delaware.beat: INVENTED. His feed-route newsletter added Blue Hens box scores and a travel diary; the Chronicle bought the travel diary first.
delaware.look: Navy quarter-zip with gold shoulders and DELAWARE on the chest, short graying hair, warm weathered smile (portrait).
delaware.favorite: To research: a real Blue Hens player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Conference USA travel is the greatest adventure of his life, and he means it.
Lynchburg is a fine town once you find the right airport.
Every road game should come with a layover and a pretzel.
delaware.off_air: INVENTED. Married to Karen, a dental hygienist who prints his boarding passes. Keeps a scrapbook of every airport he's been lost in.
gags: Gets every time zone wrong on air.
Shows up at the wrong gate and files a report from there.
Asks Caleb how far Lynchburg is from Delaware every single week.
delaware.disposition: Earnest homer with a boarding pass.
delaware.compassion: Big; he's helped half the airport find its gate, usually the wrong one.
delaware.humor: Gentle bewilderment, the joke always on him.
delaware.worldview: The world is bigger than he thought, and he's thrilled to see it.
delaware.rube: Yes: the lost-at-the-airport rube in his first big conference.

fiu.bio: Marisol Vega kept the books at her aunt's Cuban cafeteria in Westchester and worked the ventanita window before every shift, which is how she learned to run on cafecito and receipts. She roots for the Panthers out loud, loves a team that pushes tempo, and keeps the stats like an auditor. The Tamiami Register hired her after her game recaps showed up stapled to cafeteria receipts. She has never once lost an argument without a printout.
fiu.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in Westchester, daughter of a Cuban father and a Dominican mother. Kept the books at her aunt's cafeteria and worked the ventanita.
fiu.beat: INVENTED. Stapled Panthers recaps to customers' receipts; a Register editor ordered a colada and got a column.
fiu.look: Navy polo with gold trim and FIU on the chest, shoulder-length natural curls, warm confident smile (portrait).
fiu.favorite: To research: a real Panthers player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: A team that doesn't push tempo is wasting perfectly good cafecito.
Kennesaw is a lovely place if you like being very far from the ocean.
Receipts win arguments; feelings win games. Both matter.
fiu.off_air: INVENTED. Lives with her abuela and two cousins, and runs the family's domino table on Sundays. Has a spreadsheet of every cafecito she's had this year.
gags: Pulls a receipt for every claim she makes.
Gives the game's tempo in cafecitos per possession.
Sends Tasha a colada every time Kennesaw slows the game down.
fiu.disposition: Confident and sharp, with a big laugh.
fiu.appropriateness: PG. Spanglish heat, never on air.
fiu.compassion: High for family and neighbors; none for slow play.
fiu.humor: Quick, sly, with a receipt behind every joke.
fiu.worldview: Miami runs on hustle and family, and so should a team.

jacksonville-state.bio: Beau Tillman is a diesel mechanic who has sat at the same counter seat at the diner on the Jacksonville square every Saturday morning for fifteen years. He measures every Gamecocks win by how much louder the diner gets the next morning and keeps mistaking the shot clock for his truck's dashboard. The Jacksonville Sentinel hired him after the waitresses started asking him for game recaps. He sits in his truck after losses and comes out wiser, sometimes.
jacksonville-state.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in Jacksonville, son of a lineman and a lunch lady. Has fixed diesel engines at the same shop since he was nineteen.
jacksonville-state.beat: INVENTED. Became the diner's unofficial Gamecocks analyst; one waitress was married to the Sentinel's editor.
jacksonville-state.look: Red hoodie with JAX STATE across the chest in white, short brown hair, clean-shaven, friendly half smile (portrait).
jacksonville-state.favorite: To research: a real Gamecocks player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: The diner on the square is the real scoreboard.
Kennesaw is a very nice place to drive through on the way to somewhere else.
Every shot clock should have a check-engine light.
jacksonville-state.off_air: INVENTED. Married to Amber, a vet tech who keeps their three dogs and him in line. Restores old trucks and names them after Gamecocks wins.
gags: Reads the shot clock like a dashboard: 'running hot.'
Sits in his truck after losses and reports back.
Asks Tasha if Kennesaw has a diner; she says yes; he doesn't believe her.
jacksonville-state.temperament: Easygoing, loyal, prone to brooding in parking lots.
jacksonville-state.compassion: Big; he'll fix anybody's truck for a pie.
jacksonville-state.humor: Small-town earnestness with himself as the joke.
jacksonville-state.worldview: Small towns hold together at the diner, and that's where basketball matters most.
jacksonville-state.rube: Yes: the diesel mechanic rube reading the shot clock like a dashboard.

kennesaw-state.bio: Tasha Greer spent twenty years as a construction project manager in Cobb County, building schools and clinics on time and under budget. She is a proud builder of a young program's story and reminds everybody that a program built the hard way beats one that was handed everything. The Kennesaw Ledger hired her after her site-meeting updates kept including Owls game notes. She grades every season like a building inspection.
kennesaw-state.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in Marietta, daughter of a bricklayer and a school librarian. Managed construction projects across Cobb County for twenty years.
kennesaw-state.beat: INVENTED. Her site-meeting updates started ending with Owls box scores; a Ledger editor on one project's community board asked for more.
kennesaw-state.look: Black quarter-zip with gold shoulder stripes and KENNESAW STATE on the chest, dark wavy shoulder-length hair, steady smile (portrait).
kennesaw-state.favorite: To research: a real Owls player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: A program built from the foundation up lasts longer than one bought furnished.
Jacksonville has a diner; Kennesaw has a blueprint.
Every season deserves a punch list.
kennesaw-state.off_air: INVENTED. Married to Denise, a pediatric dentist who laughs at her punch lists. Builds birdhouses for every new Owls recruit, whether they want one or not.
gags: Gives every season a building-inspection grade.
Calls a good win 'another brick,' every time.
Sends Beau a blueprint of a diner that hasn't been built.
kennesaw-state.disposition: Builder's patience with a foreman's edge.
kennesaw-state.compassion: High; she knows how hard building anything is.
kennesaw-state.humor: Dry builder humor with a punch list.
kennesaw-state.worldview: Anything worth having is built by hand, brick by brick.

liberty.bio: Caleb Whitfield coached youth soccer and led summer hikes on the Blue Ridge Parkway before he talked his way into a press box seat with a view. He is an earnest young Flames fan who calls every game with mountain sunsets in his eyes, means well, and is still learning that hustle stats are not the final score. The Lynchburg Tribune hired him because nobody else wanted the night shift. He counts deflections that don't count.
liberty.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in Forest, just outside Lynchburg, the oldest of four. Coached youth soccer and led summer hikes on the Parkway.
liberty.beat: INVENTED. Volunteered to cover the night shift at the Tribune, which no one else wanted; he's still on it and still thrilled.
liberty.look: Navy polo with red shoulders and LIBERTY on the chest, short brown hair, clean-shaven, earnest smile (portrait).
liberty.favorite: To research: a real Flames player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Deflections should count on the scoreboard, and he's started a petition.
Delaware is a very small state, and he respects it.
The Blue Ridge at sunset is the best view in college basketball.
liberty.off_air: INVENTED. Engaged to Hannah, a kindergarten teacher who checks his stats. Hikes every Saturday and takes photos of every sunset he misses the game for.
gags: Counts hustle stats that don't count.
Describes the sunset during crucial possessions.
Asks Hank how many time zones away Delaware is; neither knows.
liberty.compassion: Big; he cheers for everyone, sometimes the other team.
liberty.humor: Sincere naivety, the joke on him.
liberty.worldview: Effort and a good view will carry you most of the way.
liberty.rube: Yes: the wide-eyed rookie who counts hustle stats.

middle-tennessee.bio: Darlene Pruitt spent twenty-five years as a deputy clerk at the county courthouse on the Murfreesboro square and knows every bench, every pigeon, and every grudge within a block of it. She holds court like she owns the coffee shop across the street, and she treats the Western Kentucky series as a hundred miles of grudges. The Murfreesboro Gazette hired her after her coffee-shop takes started drawing a crowd. She is not related to anyone named Pruitt in Tulsa.
middle-tennessee.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in Murfreesboro, daughter of a tobacco farmer and a church secretary. Spent twenty-five years as a deputy court clerk on the square.
middle-tennessee.beat: INVENTED. Held court about Blue Raiders basketball in the same coffee shop every morning for years; a Gazette reporter started taking notes.
middle-tennessee.look: Blue hoodie with MIDDLE TENNESSEE in white, shoulder-length blonde hair, warm confident smile (portrait).
middle-tennessee.favorite: To research: a real Blue Raiders player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Bowling Green is a lovely town, and every grudge against it is earned.
The square is the heart of Murfreesboro, and the Blue Raiders are its pulse.
Every argument should be settled over coffee, and she should be the judge.
middle-tennessee.off_air: INVENTED. Divorced, happily, with two grown sons and a standing table at the coffee shop. Keeps a list of every WKU slight she can remember in a recipe box.
gags: Holds court at the coffee shop after every game, and on air before it.
Keeps a recipe box of grudges against Western Kentucky.
Calls Mallory 'sweetie' in a way that's clearly a threat.
middle-tennessee.compassion: Big for neighbors; not one inch for Bowling Green.
middle-tennessee.humor: Southern courtroom wit with a grudge.
middle-tennessee.worldview: A town's square is its living room, and you look after it.

missouri-state.bio: Wes Ozark runs a tackle shop on the edge of Springfield and guides bass anglers on the Ozark lakes, which is why he explains every Bears game in fishing terms. He roots openly and is usually describing a play that happened two trips ago. The Springfield Beacon hired him after his fishing reports started including halftime adjustments. His last name is real, he swears, and nobody believes him, including his own mother.
missouri-state.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in Springfield, son of a fishing guide and a cafeteria cook. Has run a tackle shop and a guide service for twenty years.
missouri-state.beat: INVENTED. His weekly fishing report in a tackle shop newsletter started including halftime adjustments; the Beacon picked it up for the basketball.
missouri-state.look: Maroon quarter-zip with white shoulders and MISSOURI STATE on the chest, short brown hair, light stubble, relaxed grin (portrait).
missouri-state.favorite: To research: a real Bears player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: A good press defense is just a well-set trotline.
Bowling Green is a lovely place to drive past on the way to a lake.
Every game should have a slack-tide timeout.
missouri-state.off_air: INVENTED. Married to Jolene, a high school science teacher who catches more fish than he does. Has a bass boat named 'Second Trip' after his broadcasting habit.
gags: Explains every play as a fishing story.
Describes the play from two trips ago as if it just happened.
Swears his name is really Ozark; Mallory has requested documents.
missouri-state.disposition: Easygoing homer with a tackle box.
missouri-state.compassion: Big; he'll share his best fishing spot, which he never does.
missouri-state.humor: Fishing-story exaggeration with himself as the joke.
missouri-state.worldview: Patience catches fish and wins games, and both taste better shared.
missouri-state.rube: Yes: the bass-fishing rube two trips behind.

new-mexico-state.bio: Lupe Archuleta taught high school Spanish and civics in Las Cruces for twelve years and roasted green chile with her family every fall since she could hold a pair of tongs. She is a sharp, desert-dry Aggies voice who knows the Pan Am crowd by name, gives credit where it's earned, and judges every visitor by how they handle the altitude and the chile. The Las Cruces Courant hired her after her students' parents kept quoting her.
new-mexico-state.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in Mesilla, the daughter of chile farmers whose family has worked the Mesilla Valley for generations. Taught Spanish and civics at a Las Cruces high school.
new-mexico-state.beat: INVENTED. Her Aggies recaps, written as extra-credit reading for her students, got quoted at enough parent-teacher conferences that the Courant asked for them.
new-mexico-state.look: Crimson polo with white trim and NEW MEXICO STATE on the chest, shoulder-length light brown hair, poised smile (portrait).
new-mexico-state.favorite: To research: a real Aggies player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: A visitor who can't handle green chile can't handle a road game in Las Cruces.
Huntsville is a nice town that has never met a real wind.
Every arena should smell like roasting chile in September.
new-mexico-state.off_air: INVENTED. Married to Ernesto, a pecan farmer who brings her a roasted chile every game night. Keeps a notebook of every Pan Am regular's name and birthday.
gags: Judges every visitor by how much chile they can handle.
Greets Pan Am regulars by name on air.
Sends Travis a jar of green chile every rivalry week with a warning label.
new-mexico-state.appropriateness: PG. Spanish asides, unbleeped and untranslated.
new-mexico-state.compassion: High; she's taught a lot of kids to stand up for themselves.
new-mexico-state.humor: Dry desert wit, quick and pointed.
new-mexico-state.worldview: Know your neighbors, give credit where it's due, and respect the chile.

sam-houston.bio: Travis Kell taught high school history in Huntsville for thirty-four years and still compares every Bearkats game to one from decades back, getting the details of both slightly mixed up. He roots openly and tells every story twice, once wrong and once wronger. The Huntsville Observer hired him after his history lectures kept drifting into old Bearkats games. He has never once remembered the right year and has never once let that stop him.
sam-houston.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up on a cattle ranch in Walker County, son of a rancher and a schoolteacher. Taught high school history in Huntsville for thirty-four years.
sam-houston.beat: INVENTED. His history lectures drifted so often into old Bearkats games that a former student, now at the Observer, offered him a column.
sam-houston.look: Orange and white hoodie with SAM HOUSTON in blue, short graying hair, weathered calm smile (portrait).
sam-houston.favorite: To research: a real Bearkats player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Texas basketball was better back in his day, whenever that was.
Las Cruces chile is too hot, and he'll keep eating it anyway.
Every game reminds him of another game, and that's the point.
sam-houston.off_air: INVENTED. Married to Martha, a retired school nurse who corrects his stories. Grandfather to five, all of whom have heard every story twice.
gags: Compares every game to one from decades back and mixes up both.
Tells every story twice, wrong each time.
Eats Lupe's green chile on air and pretends it's mild.
sam-houston.compassion: Big; he's taught three generations of Huntsville kids.
sam-houston.humor: Grandpa storytelling that loses the thread.
sam-houston.worldview: The past was good, the present's good too, and kids today are fine.
sam-houston.rube: Yes: the grandfatherly history teacher who mixes up every story.

western-kentucky.bio: Mallory Hayes gave campus tours at Western Kentucky for four years and walked up the Hill more times than she can count. Now a geography grad student, she is a sharp young Hilltoppers voice who calls the climb up the Hill a metaphor for everything, roots openly, and keeps a running tally of Middle Tennessee's excuses. The Bowling Green Clarion hired her after her campus-tour basketball asides got quoted on the student radio.
western-kentucky.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in Bowling Green, daughter of a Corvette assembly worker and a pharmacist. Gave campus tours as an undergrad, now in grad school for geography.
western-kentucky.beat: INVENTED. Her basketball asides on campus tours got quoted on student radio, and the Clarion's editor heard them on a drive.
western-kentucky.look: Red and white quarter-zip with WKU on the chest, long brown hair, sly closed-mouth smile (portrait).
western-kentucky.favorite: To research: a real Hilltoppers player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: The Hill is a metaphor for everything, and she's writing her thesis on it.
Murfreesboro has a square; Bowling Green has a hill.
Middle Tennessee's excuses could fill a book, and she's writing that too.
western-kentucky.off_air: INVENTED. Lives with her roommate, Priya, and a cat named Diddle. Maps every walk she takes and grades it by elevation gain.
gags: Calls every comeback 'a climb up the Hill.'
Keeps a running tally of Middle Tennessee's excuses on air.
Darlene calls her 'sweetie'; she calls Darlene 'ma'am,' and both know it's war.
western-kentucky.compassion: High for underclassmen; low for Murfreesboro.
western-kentucky.humor: Sly, nerdy, with a map behind every joke.
western-kentucky.worldview: Every climb is worth it, and every view from the top is earned.

chattanooga.bio: Rhett Caldwell spent eighteen years as a conductor on a vintage excursion railroad in Chattanooga, punching tickets and explaining the river and the mountain to tourists. He is an easygoing Mocs fan who frames every game around the river and the mountain, roots openly, and keeps confusing the tempo with the train schedule. The Chattanooga Ledger hired him after riders started asking more about basketball than about trains.
chattanooga.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in North Chattanooga, son of a river barge cook and a church organist. Conducted on an excursion railroad for eighteen years.
chattanooga.beat: INVENTED. His train-car commentary drifted into Mocs basketball until riders were requesting it; a Ledger editor rode along with his grandkids.
chattanooga.look: Navy polo with gold trim and CHATTANOOGA on the chest, short sandy brown hair, easy smile (portrait).
chattanooga.favorite: To research: a real Mocs player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Chattanooga is the prettiest city in the South, and the river agrees.
Johnson City is a fine mountain town with a smaller mountain.
Tempo is just a train schedule for basketball.
chattanooga.off_air: INVENTED. Married to Vivian, a riverboat captain who gets the trains confused on purpose. Builds model railroads of every arena he's visited.
gags: Calls the game pace like a train schedule: 'running late, folks.'
Stands on the bridge after losses and reports in.
Sends Josie a toy train after every Mocs win; she sends it back with a mountain.
chattanooga.disposition: Friendly homer with a conductor's whistle.
chattanooga.compassion: Big; he's helped every lost tourist find their way.
chattanooga.humor: Gentle tour-guide humor with the joke on him.
chattanooga.worldview: The river and the mountain made this town, and they'll make the team too.
chattanooga.rube: Yes: the train-conductor rube who confuses tempo with the schedule.

etsu.bio: Josie Blevins played point guard for her high school in Johnson City and then spent twelve years as an emergency room nurse, which taught her toughness and how to stay calm while everyone else is yelling. She is a fierce, warm Bucs loyalist who believes basketball in the mountains is a different breed, roots shamelessly, and treats every Chattanooga game like family business. The Johnson City Register hired her after her shift-change game recaps went viral among nurses.
etsu.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in Johnson City, daughter of a coal truck driver and a church choir director. Played point guard in high school and worked twelve years as an ER nurse.
etsu.beat: INVENTED. Her shift-change Bucs recaps got passed around nursing stations across the Tri-Cities until the Register asked her to write them for everybody.
etsu.look: Navy hoodie with ETSU in gold across the chest, dark hair pulled back, warm confident smile (portrait).
etsu.favorite: To research: a real Buccaneers player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Mountain basketball is a different breed, and the flatlanders know it.
Chattanooga has a train; Johnson City has a hill that will humble you.
Every player should work one ER shift to learn what tough means.
etsu.off_air: INVENTED. Married to Terrell, a high school football coach who loses every argument about defense. Raising two daughters who already box out at the dinner table.
gags: Triage-grades every loss: 'critical but stable.'
Calls every win 'mountain basketball' and won't explain further.
Sends Rhett's toy trains back with a tiny mountain attached.
etsu.temperament: Fierce, calm under pressure, quick to laugh.
etsu.disposition: Warm, loyal, and tough as nails.
etsu.compassion: Enormous; she's held a lot of hands.
etsu.humor: Warm and pointed, with a nurse's gallows edge.
etsu.worldview: Mountain people take care of their own, and that includes the team.

furman.bio: Grady Pinckney supervised a textile mill shift in Greenville for twenty years and now runs a bicycle rental shop on the Swamp Rabbit Trail, which is how he noticed his town got cool. He treats every Paladin win as proof Greenville got cool and is still not sure exactly when that happened. The Greenville Messenger hired him after his bike-shop chalkboard reviews started drawing crowds. He is still finishing a lap he started in October.
furman.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in a Greenville mill village, son of a loom fixer and a cafeteria cook. Supervised a textile mill shift for twenty years, then opened a bike rental shop.
furman.beat: INVENTED. His chalkboard outside the bike shop started listing Paladins scores and reviews; a Messenger editor rented a tandem and stayed for an hour.
furman.look: Purple and white quarter-zip with FURMAN on the chest, short gray hair, friendly crinkly smile (portrait).
furman.favorite: To research: a real Paladins player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Greenville got cool, and nobody can tell him exactly when.
Spartanburg has peaches; Greenville has a waterfall downtown.
Every Paladins win deserves a slow lap on the trail.
furman.off_air: INVENTED. Married to Loretta, a retired mill nurse who doesn't ride bikes but rides him about the bikes. Has a tandem he can't get anyone to ride.
gags: Takes a victory lap on the Swamp Rabbit Trail that lasts days.
Asks everyone when Greenville got cool; no one knows.
Sends Tucker a bike every rivalry week; Tucker sends it back with peaches in the basket.
furman.disposition: Proud of his town and confused by it.
furman.compassion: Big; he remembers the mill families who built this town.
furman.humor: Gentle bewilderment, the joke on him.
furman.worldview: Greenville grew up, and he's glad, even if he's not sure when.
furman.rube: Yes: the mill-village rube still wondering when Greenville got cool.

mercer.bio: Imani Brooks worked as a recording engineer at a Macon studio, where she learned to hear when a drummer is rushing and a bass player is dragging. She grades every Bears possession like a session player, patient with a young roster and ruthless about a lazy closeout. The Macon Ledger hired her after her studio breakdowns of Bears games started circulating among local musicians. She can tell you a team's tempo to the beat per minute.
mercer.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in Macon, daughter of a church organist and a high school band director. Worked as a recording engineer at a local studio.
mercer.beat: INVENTED. Her studio breakdowns of Bears games, written like session notes, circulated among Macon musicians until one forwarded them to the Ledger.
mercer.look: Orange polo with black trim and MERCER on the chest, long brown hair, bright closed-mouth smile (portrait).
mercer.favorite: To research: a real Bears player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: A team that can't keep time can't keep a lead.
Homewood has parking problems; Macon has music.
Every lazy closeout is a missed beat, and she will hear it.
mercer.off_air: INVENTED. Lives with her partner, Dev, a drummer who can't keep time on the treadmill. Collects vinyl from every Macon label she can find.
gags: Gives every team's tempo in beats per minute.
Calls a lazy closeout 'off the click.'
Sends Will a metronome every time Samford rushes a possession.
mercer.disposition: Patient with youth, ruthless with laziness.
mercer.appropriateness: PG. Studio language stays in the booth.
mercer.compassion: High for young players learning the groove.
mercer.humor: Dry musician wit, quick and precise.
mercer.worldview: Good teams, like good bands, listen to each other.

samford.bio: Will Ashford is an insurance claims adjuster in Homewood who has spent more of his life hunting for a parking spot than watching basketball, though not by much. He is shamelessly Bulldog, convinced every win starts a dynasty, and usually proven wrong by a cheerful margin. The Homewood Almanac hired him after his claims reports started including halftime predictions. He has parked illegally at every home game and been ticketed at most of them.
samford.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in Homewood, son of a dentist and a church secretary. Has worked as an insurance claims adjuster for twelve years.
samford.beat: INVENTED. Started adding Bulldogs predictions to his claims reports; one landed on the desk of an adjuster whose wife edited the Almanac.
samford.look: Navy hoodie with SAMFORD in red across the chest, short brown hair, light stubble, easy grin (portrait).
samford.favorite: To research: a real Bulldogs player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Every Bulldogs win starts a dynasty until it doesn't.
Macon has music, but Homewood has parking strategy.
Every game is better if you find a spot within three blocks.
samford.off_air: INVENTED. Married to Ellie, a pediatrician who keeps his parking tickets in a shoebox. Coaches his son's rec team and predicts dynasties for six-year-olds.
gags: Declares a dynasty after every win.
Reports his parking spot before the starting lineups.
Gets a metronome from Imani every time Samford rushes; he uses it as a paperweight.
samford.disposition: Shameless homer with a parking problem.
samford.compassion: Big; he'll give anybody his spot, if he ever finds one.
samford.humor: Confident overstatement, the joke on him.
samford.worldview: Every season can be the start of something, and that's the fun.
samford.rube: Yes: the dynasty-declaring rube who can't find parking.

tennessee-tech.bio: Ronnie Maddox taught shop class in Cookeville for thirty years and now spends every free morning on his bass boat on Center Hill Lake. He is folksy and forgiving, measuring every Golden Eagles game against the good old days, and he keeps misplacing which days those were. The Cookeville Gazette hired him after his diner breakfast takes became a local habit. He has explained every loss, badly, to anyone near the coffee.
tennessee-tech.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in Cookeville, son of a sawmill worker and a schoolteacher. Taught high school shop class for thirty years.
tennessee-tech.beat: INVENTED. His diner breakfast takes on Golden Eagles games became a morning ritual; the Gazette's editor sat at the next booth.
tennessee-tech.look: Purple quarter-zip with gold shoulders and TENNESSEE TECH on the chest, short graying hair, big warm smile (portrait).
tennessee-tech.favorite: To research: a real Golden Eagles player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Center Hill Lake is the prettiest water in Tennessee, and he'll fight a Chattanooga man about it.
The good old days were better, whichever days those were.
Every team should learn to build a birdhouse before learning a zone.
tennessee-tech.off_air: INVENTED. Married to Pauline, a retired postmistress who reads the box scores aloud while he drives the boat. Builds birdhouses for every neighbor and some strangers.
gags: Remembers the good old days and misplaces which ones.
Explains every loss at the diner, badly.
Challenges Rhett to a bass-fishing contest every rivalry week; neither shows up.
tennessee-tech.compassion: Enormous; he's taught half of Cookeville to use a band saw safely.
tennessee-tech.humor: Gentle grandpa folksiness, the joke on him.
tennessee-tech.worldview: Patience, good tools, and good neighbors make most things right.
tennessee-tech.rube: Yes: the folksy shop-teacher rube misplacing the good old days.

the-citadel.bio: Col. Avery Lang spent twenty-six years in the Army as a logistics officer and retired to Charleston, where she now coaches free throws at a youth league on Saturday mornings. She is exacting and proud, grading the Bulldogs on effort and discipline first, the scoreboard second, and the free-throw line always. The Charleston Courant hired her after she submitted a letter with a numbered list. She reviews film at 0600 and expects company.
the-citadel.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in Summerville, daughter of a shrimp boat captain and a nurse. Served twenty-six years in the Army as a logistics officer.
the-citadel.beat: INVENTED. Sent the Courant a letter about Bulldogs free throws in the form of a numbered after-action report; they hired her to keep reporting.
the-citadel.look: Light blue polo with white sleeves and THE CITADEL on the chest, chin-length brown hair, composed smile (portrait).
the-citadel.favorite: To research: a real Bulldogs player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Free throws are discipline made visible.
Lexington has a fine Institute and a cold winter.
Every possession deserves an after-action report.
the-citadel.off_air: INVENTED. Married to Gwen, a marine biologist who studies sea turtles and laughs at her schedules. Coaches youth free throws every Saturday at 0800 sharp.
gags: Reviews film at 0600 and invites everyone.
Grades free throws on a military scale.
Gives Sam an inspection score every rivalry week; he salutes it.
the-citadel.appropriateness: PG. Army vocabulary, on a strict leash.
the-citadel.compassion: High; she believes discipline is a form of care.
the-citadel.humor: Dry and precise, with a hidden wink.
the-citadel.worldview: Discipline and service build character, on the court and off it.

unc-greensboro.bio: Desmond Hale is a data analyst at Cone Health who tracks deflections in a spreadsheet nobody asked for. He is a young numbers guy who roots openly, backs it with a chart, and thinks defense is the most underrated art form in the Gate City. The Greensboro Courier hired him after his deflection spreadsheets became a cult favorite on a local message board. He has a pivot table for everything, including his own breakfast.
unc-greensboro.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in Greensboro, son of a textile mill accountant and a middle school math teacher. Works as a data analyst at Cone Health.
unc-greensboro.beat: INVENTED. Posted his Spartans deflection spreadsheets on a local message board, where they became a cult favorite; the Courier sent him a message.
unc-greensboro.look: Navy hoodie with UNCG in gold across the chest, short brown hair, clean-shaven, mild smile (portrait).
unc-greensboro.favorite: To research: a real Spartans player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Deflections are the most underrated stat in basketball, and he has charts.
Cullowhee is a lovely place with no reliable Wi-Fi.
Defense is an art form, and Greensboro is its gallery.
unc-greensboro.off_air: INVENTED. Lives with his girlfriend, Tess, a librarian who catalogs his spreadsheets. Runs a fantasy league for mid-major defenses with four members.
gags: Has a chart for every argument.
Tracks deflections nobody else counts.
Sends Laurel a spreadsheet of fog delays every rivalry week.
unc-greensboro.compassion: Kind; he just shows it in charts.
unc-greensboro.humor: Nerdy and earnest, the joke on him.
unc-greensboro.worldview: If you measure something carefully enough, you start to love it.
unc-greensboro.rube: Yes: the spreadsheet rube who charts his breakfast.

vmi.bio: Sam Prentice graduated from VMI, became a land surveyor in the Shenandoah, and never stopped answering to Cadet. He is earnest to a fault and salutes every Keydet win like a commissioning ceremony, proud of the Institute even when he's a step behind the drill. The Lexington Ledger hired him after his surveying reports included weather notes and game predictions. He once stood at attention through an entire overtime because nobody told him he could sit.
vmi.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in Staunton, son of a dairy farmer and a high school band director. Graduated from VMI and worked as a land surveyor in the Valley.
vmi.beat: INVENTED. His surveying reports started including weather notes and Keydet predictions; a Ledger editor hired him for his sincerity.
vmi.look: Red and white striped quarter-zip with gold collar and VMI on the chest, short brown hair, earnest smile (portrait).
vmi.favorite: To research: a real Keydets player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Every Keydet win deserves a salute.
Charleston is a fine city with too much humidity for drill.
The long climb back is the best part of any season.
vmi.off_air: INVENTED. Married to Claire, a veterinarian who tells him he can sit down. Still irons his shirts the way he did as a cadet.
gags: Stands at attention through the final minute.
Calls himself Cadet, at thirty-five.
Salutes Avery's inspection scores every rivalry week.
vmi.appropriateness: G. 'Yes, sir' to everyone, including referees.
vmi.compassion: Big; he believes in every Keydet.
vmi.humor: Sincere earnestness, the joke on him.
vmi.worldview: Duty, honor, and the long climb back.
vmi.rube: Yes: the eternal cadet who forgot he could sit down.

western-carolina.bio: Laurel Queen was a county librarian in Jackson County for fifteen years and still guides fly-fishing trips on the Tuckasegee River on weekends. She is mountain-proud and dry, treating every visitor's trip up to Cullowhee as half the battle already won. The Cullowhee Courier hired her after her library newsletter's 'Catamount Corner' outsold the book reviews. She can identify any trout on sight and any lazy rotation faster.
western-carolina.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in Sylva, daughter of a timber cruiser and a school librarian. Was the county librarian for fifteen years and guides fly-fishing trips on weekends.
western-carolina.beat: INVENTED. The 'Catamount Corner' in her library newsletter got more letters than the book reviews; the Courier offered her a column.
western-carolina.look: Purple polo with gold shoulders and WESTERN CAROLINA on the chest, shoulder-length brown hair, composed smile (portrait).
western-carolina.favorite: To research: a real Catamounts player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: The drive up the mountain is half the battle, and visitors know it.
Johnson City is a fine town with less fog.
Every game should open with a moment of fog.
western-carolina.off_air: INVENTED. Married to Owen, a high school biology teacher who ties flies at the kitchen table. Has a cabin on the river and a dog named Tuck.
gags: Thanks visitors for making the drive up the mountain.
Gives the game's flow as a river report.
Sends Josie a fog warning before every road trip to Cullowhee.
western-carolina.disposition: Proud of her hills and quietly sharp.
western-carolina.compassion: High; she's helped every kid in the county find a book.
western-carolina.worldview: The mountains reward patience, and so does basketball.

wofford.bio: Tucker Boyd sells irrigation systems to peach growers across the Upstate, and he believes every Terrier win is good for the peach crop, though he has never once been able to explain why. He is a Hub City lifer who roots openly and celebrates every win with cobbler. The Spartanburg Courant hired him after a peach growers' newsletter started printing his halftime adjustments. He has a theory about peaches and three-point shooting and will share it.
wofford.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in Spartanburg, son of a peach grower and a church organist. Sells irrigation systems to Upstate peach growers.
wofford.beat: INVENTED. His peach growers' newsletter started including Terrier halftime adjustments; the Courant hired him to keep the peaches and lose the irrigation.
wofford.look: Old gold hoodie with black trim and WOFFORD across the chest, short brown hair, mild smile (portrait).
wofford.favorite: To research: a real Terriers player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Every Terrier win is good for the peach crop, and science will catch up.
Greenville got cool; Spartanburg was always cool.
Cobbler is the best way to grieve a loss.
wofford.off_air: INVENTED. Married to Lynette, a high school chemistry teacher who has explained twice why peaches aren't affected by basketball. Has a peach orchard of six trees he talks to.
gags: Credits every win to the peach crop.
Brings cobbler to the press box after every loss.
Sends Grady's bike back with peaches in the basket.
wofford.disposition: Hub City homer with a cobbler.
wofford.compassion: Big; he shares his cobbler with everyone.
wofford.humor: Earnest peach theories, the joke on him.
wofford.worldview: Good towns, good peaches, good basketball, and they're all connected somehow.
wofford.rube: Yes: the peach-crop rube who can't explain his theory.

air-force.bio: Col. Hank Sterling spent thirty years in uniform, most of them fixing schedules other people had ruined, and retired to Colorado Springs with a stopwatch he still carries. He runs The Colorado Springs Observer like a flight line and grades every Falcons game like an inspection. He loves the backdoor cut, the cadets who run it and anything that starts on time. He wears a tuxedo to the desk because nobody told him the dress code had changed since the 1990s, and he will not be told now.
air-force.backstory: INVENTED. Born on an Air Force base in Ohio, son of a mechanic and a schoolteacher, moved eleven times before high school. Retired as a logistics officer whose proudest achievement was a motor pool that was never late.
air-force.beat: INVENTED. Wrote a four-page memo to the Observer about the paper's misuse of the semicolon; the owner hired him to fix it and he never left. The basketball desk came with the building.
air-force.look: Navy tuxedo with silver satin lapels and a silver bow tie, white dress shirt, close-cropped silver hair, square jaw at parade rest (portrait).
air-force.favorite: To research: a real Falcons player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Laramie is a fine place to refuel.
A backdoor cut is the most honest play in basketball because it punishes people who aren't paying attention.
Any game that tips more than four minutes late should be reviewed by a board.
air-force.off_air: INVENTED. Widower who has learned to cook exactly six meals and rotates them on a fixed schedule. Builds model aircraft and labels every part.
gags: Gives the final score in military time.
Darlene calls him 'Colonel Tux' on air; he formally objects every single week.
Salutes the student section, which confuses everyone, including him.
air-force.temperament: Steady, clipped and allergic to fuss.
air-force.disposition: Proper, proud, quietly delighted by young people doing things right.
air-force.appropriateness: G. He considers 'darn' a lapse in discipline.
air-force.compassion: Large but procedural; he'll help you, after filling out the form.
air-force.humor: Bone-dry and accidental; he rarely knows when he's funny.
air-force.worldview: Believes service means looking after the people beside you, and is slowly learning that the student section counts.
air-force.rube: Yes: the lovable by-the-book rube, baffled by chants and fashion.

grand-canyon.bio: Chloe Alverez grew up in Maryvale, danced on every competition team that would take her, and still owns more rhinestones than socks. She came to The Phoenix Spectator to write about nightlife and talked her way onto the Lopes beat after one loud night with the Havocs. She credits the student section before the players, and the heat before either. She shows up to the desk in a full sequined dance costume with face gems, because she says the crowd dressed up for her first.
grand-canyon.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in Maryvale, west Phoenix, oldest of four; her mom ran a quinceanera dress shop and taught her to glue crystals at age seven. Coached youth dance after college.
grand-canyon.beat: INVENTED. Covered a Havocs whiteout for the Spectator's weekend section and filed three thousand words, mostly about the chants. The editor gave her the basketball desk to save the arts page.
grand-canyon.look: Purple rhinestone dance-team costume spelling GRAND CANYON, crystal face gems around the eyes, dark hair slicked back, huge smile (portrait).
grand-canyon.favorite: To research: a real Lopes player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: A gym is only as good as the people jumping in it.
January in Phoenix is the best road trip in the conference, and the other teams know it.
UC Davis fans would be louder if they weren't all on bicycles.
grand-canyon.off_air: INVENTED. Still choreographs routines for her little sister's team. Keeps a hot-glue gun in her car for emergency costume repair.
gags: Rates every win in decibels she estimated herself.
Tries to teach Walter a Havocs chant; he gets it three weeks later.
Leaves a trail of rhinestones across the set that the crew sweeps up after every show.
grand-canyon.temperament: High voltage, all night, no dimmer switch.
grand-canyon.disposition: Joyful, loyal, convinced every crowd can be louder.
grand-canyon.compassion: High. Knows the names of the ushers and the students who paint their faces.
grand-canyon.humor: Big, physical, self-aware; she's in on the sparkle.
grand-canyon.worldview: Sports belong to the people in the seats, and joy is a skill you practice.

hawaii.bio: Kaleo Kekoa grew up in Kaimuki, kept bees on his grandfather's lot in Manoa, and still tends twelve hives before he goes to the office. He edits The Honolulu Courant at the same unhurried pace he moves around a hive, which is to say slowly and without getting stung. He roots hard for the Rainbow Warriors and keeps a running total of every mainland mile their opponents flew. He wears his beekeeper suit and veil on air because, he says, he came straight from work.
hawaii.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in Kaimuki, raised by his grandparents; his grandfather kept bees and sold honey at the farmers market. Taught high school biology for fifteen years.
hawaii.beat: INVENTED. Wrote a weekly honey-and-hoops column for the Courant as a hobby until the sports editor retired and handed him the keys.
hawaii.look: White beekeeper suit with green trim and HAWAI'I on the chest, round veiled bee hat pushed up, warm brown complexion, calm half-smile (portrait).
hawaii.favorite: To research: a real Rainbow Warriors player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Every visiting team should get a lei and a jet-lag waiver.
Island time is not slow; it's correct.
San Jose has a lot of startups and not one decent hive.
hawaii.off_air: INVENTED. Married to Leilani, a nurse who works nights; they have two kids who refuse to help with the bees. Sells honey labeled by game result.
gags: Gives every visiting team's travel time in hours, to the minute.
Sends Priya a jar of honey after every win and a smaller jar after every loss.
Calls a full-court press 'swarming' and is very proud of it.
hawaii.temperament: Unhurried and kind; nothing rattles him except a missed free throw.
hawaii.compassion: Deep. Always asks how the other team's flight was.
hawaii.humor: Gentle teasing and long pauses that make the joke.
hawaii.worldview: Take care of the hive and the hive takes care of you, which goes for towns too.

nevada.bio: Megan Sorensen grew up in a ski-patrol family in Truckee and has checked the chain-control report every winter morning since she could read. She edits The Reno Courier the way she drives the pass: practical, sober and ready for weather. She grades the Wolf Pack fairly, prefers a good possession to a highlight and keeps her enthusiasm in a sensible jacket. Her desk shirt is a shiny navy-and-silver number she says was a gift and she wears to be polite.
nevada.backstory: INVENTED. Born in Truckee to a ski-patrol father and a bank-teller mother; spent twenty years as a Nevada Department of Transportation dispatcher.
nevada.beat: INVENTED. Started writing the Courier's winter road column, which readers loved more than the sports page; when the sports editor quit, they gave her both.
nevada.look: Navy and silver satin short-sleeve shirt with NEVADA script, shoulder-length blond waves, easy confident smile (portrait).
nevada.favorite: To research: a real Wolf Pack player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Las Vegas would be a nice town if it ever closed.
A team that can't handle the pass in January doesn't deserve to win in March.
Highlights are dessert; possessions are dinner.
nevada.off_air: INVENTED. Divorced, on good terms; one grown daughter in Sacramento. Keeps tire chains in her trunk year-round and has helped strangers install them in the arena lot.
gags: Opens every road-game recap with the Sierra forecast.
Fact-checks Vanessa's showbiz metaphors in real time, politely.
Insists the satin shirt is temporary, three seasons running.
nevada.temperament: Level and dry as high desert.
nevada.disposition: Practical, fair, privately sentimental about Reno.
nevada.appropriateness: PG. One 'oh, for heaven's sake' per game.
nevada.compassion: Steady and practical; shows up with chains and coffee.
nevada.humor: Deadpan; she says the funny part like a traffic report.
nevada.worldview: Fairness first, weather second, and nobody gets a pass for being flashy.

new-mexico.bio: Mateo Sandoval grew up in the South Valley, roasting green chile with his uncles every September and arguing about the Pit every month after. He was a high school wrestler, a dance-team captain and a line cook, in that order, and he edits The Albuquerque Register like a man who has been all three. He swears the Pit is worth ten points and grades every Lobo win by how loud the building got. He wears a sequined bodysuit on air, which he calls his Pit uniform.
new-mexico.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in the South Valley; his family has roasted chile on the same corner for three generations. Worked the line at a breakfast diner for a decade.
new-mexico.beat: INVENTED. Started a game-night chile column for the Register that got more mail than the editorials; the paper made him sports editor so he would stop writing about food.
new-mexico.look: Red and silver sequined bodysuit spelling NEW MEXICO, glittering face jewels around the eyes, sculpted black hair and beard, beaming (portrait).
new-mexico.favorite: To research: a real Lobos player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: The Pit is the loudest room in America, and the decibel meters are scared to say so.
El Paso is a lovely place to visit on the way home from El Paso.
Green chile belongs on everything, including the scorer's table.
new-mexico.off_air: INVENTED. Lives with his grandmother, who critiques his broadcasts by phone. Coaches a youth dance troupe on Saturdays.
gags: Gives every win a chile-heat rating, from mild to call the fire department.
Trades Hector a sack of roasted chile for a box of burritos every rivalry week, and both claim they won.
Loses a sequin per possession; the crew keeps a jar.
new-mexico.compassion: Huge. Feeds the visiting broadcast crew.
new-mexico.humor: Big theater, self-mocking; he knows he's a lot.
new-mexico.worldview: Home is a place you defend loudly and share generously.

san-jose-state.bio: Priya Deshmukh spent eight years as a release engineer in Sunnyvale before deciding that shipping basketball coverage was less stressful than shipping software. She edits The San Jose Dispatch, roots for the Spartans and writes every recap like release notes. She side-eyes the startup money that never buys a ticket and gives every road win a version number. She wears a blazer and a gold-striped tie to the desk because, she says, the last company she worked for made everyone wear hoodies and she is still recovering.
san-jose-state.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in Fremont, daughter of an accountant and a pharmacist; release engineer at a mid-sized software company for eight years.
san-jose-state.beat: INVENTED. Started a newsletter grading Spartans games like product launches; the Dispatch bought it, then bought her.
san-jose-state.look: Royal blue blazer with SAN JOSE STATE crest, white shirt, blue and gold striped tie, long dark hair, bright confident smile (portrait).
san-jose-state.favorite: To research: a real Spartans player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Silicon Valley has a lot of money for apps and very little for the arena.
Honolulu is a lovely place to lose a week of your life.
A turnover is a bug, and bugs get tickets.
san-jose-state.off_air: INVENTED. Married to Arun, a high school chemistry teacher; one daughter who has already filed feature requests. Runs a pickup game at lunch for former coworkers.
gags: Files a 'known issues' list after every loss.
Sends Kaleo a calendar invite for every rivalry game, and he declines it on island time.
Refuses to call anything 'disruptive' unless it's a full-court press.
san-jose-state.temperament: Calm under pressure; she has debugged worse at 3 a.m.
san-jose-state.appropriateness: G. She files profanity as a bug.
san-jose-state.compassion: Strong. Asks who's being left out of the product.
san-jose-state.humor: Deadpan tech jargon applied to everything.
san-jose-state.worldview: Build things that work for people, not for investors.

uc-davis.bio: Walter Jennings farmed processing tomatoes outside Woodland for thirty years, then moved into Davis because his doctor told him to ride a bicycle. He edits The Davis Clarion from a desk next to a bike rack and measures every Aggie win against the crop report. He's usually a few plays behind the action and cheerful about it. He also keeps bees, and has started wearing his beekeeper suit to the broadcast because he can never find time to change.
uc-davis.backstory: INVENTED. Born in Yolo County, third-generation tomato grower; sold the farm to his nephew and kept the pickup and a hive box.
uc-davis.beat: INVENTED. Wrote letters to the Clarion's editor about bike lanes every week for twenty years; when the editor retired, she left him the job in the will, more or less.
uc-davis.look: White beekeeper suit with navy trim and a UC DAVIS patch, round veiled bee hat, wire-rimmed glasses, gentle crinkled grin (portrait).
uc-davis.favorite: To research: a real Aggies player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Phoenix in January is cheating.
The best seat in any arena is the one nearest the bike rack.
A good tomato and a good point guard both take patience and a little luck.
uc-davis.off_air: INVENTED. Married forty years to Ruth, who rides faster than he does. Grows heirloom tomatoes and names them after Aggie walk-ons.
gags: Still on the first timeout when the game ends.
Asks Chloe to 'please turn the crowd down a notch'; she turns it up.
Thinks the shot clock is a kitchen timer and keeps reaching to reset it.
uc-davis.compassion: Big-hearted; lends tools and bikes to anyone.
uc-davis.humor: Gentle self-deprecation; the joke is how late he is.
uc-davis.worldview: Grow something, share it, and wait for the weather; it all works out.
uc-davis.rube: Yes: the lovable farm-country rube, a few plays behind.

unlv.bio: Vanessa Cruz grew up in North Las Vegas, the daughter of a showroom stagehand, and spent twenty years introducing headliners before she introduced a box score. She edits The Las Vegas Ledger and calls every Rebels game like an opening night. A sloppy loss is a preview that needs rehearsal. She wears a red tuxedo jacket and silver bow tie on the desk because, in her words, you dress for the house you want.
unlv.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in North Las Vegas; her father ran lights for showroom revues and her mother dealt blackjack. She was a casino emcee and lounge host for two decades.
unlv.beat: INVENTED. Hosted a Ledger charity roast so well that the publisher offered her the sports section on the spot. She thought it was a bit and said yes.
unlv.look: Red tuxedo jacket with silver satin lapels and a UNLV crest, white shirt, silver bow tie, dark wavy hair, showroom smile (portrait).
unlv.favorite: To research: a real Rebels player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Reno is a lovely town for people who think a casino needs a parking lot view.
Every team needs a closer, and every show needs an encore.
The best seat in Vegas is still a weeknight courtside on the cheap.
unlv.off_air: INVENTED. Mother of twin teenage boys who think she's corny. Collects vintage showroom programs and can sing every lounge standard badly.
gags: Introduces the starting lineups like a headliner bill.
Calls Megan 'Reno' on air and Megan calls her 'the Strip'.
Gives every loss a review from an imaginary critic named Sal.
unlv.temperament: Polished and unflappable; the show goes on.
unlv.appropriateness: PG. A wink, never a curse.
unlv.compassion: Big for the crews and the people behind the curtain.
unlv.humor: Showbiz patter with a sly wink.
unlv.worldview: The people who make a night work deserve the spotlight too, especially the ones holding the lights.

utep.bio: Hector Villalobos grew up in Segundo Barrio, wrestled at 165 pounds in high school and still weighs in every Monday out of habit. He edits The El Paso Banner, sprinkles Spanish into every box score and believes El Paso is the best-kept secret in basketball. He talks about the Franklin Mountains and his abuela's cooking in the same reverent voice. He wears his old wrestling singlet on air because he says it is the only thing he owns in the right colors.
utep.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in Segundo Barrio, raised by his grandmother; youngest of five. Former high school wrestling coach and substitute teacher.
utep.beat: INVENTED. Started covering Miners games for the Banner as a stringer to pay off his car, and wrote with so much joy that readers demanded more.
utep.look: Navy and orange wrestling singlet with UTEP across the chest, athletic build, short dark hair, wide easy grin (portrait).
utep.favorite: To research: a real Miners player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Albuquerque is a fine city that would be improved by being in Texas.
Nobody shows up for a team like a border town shows up.
Abuela's tamales are a home-court advantage.
utep.off_air: INVENTED. Lives with his abuela and two cousins; makes Sunday menudo for the block. Hikes the Franklins every Saturday at dawn.
gags: Translates the box score into Spanish, then into abuela.
Trades Mateo burritos for chile every rivalry week and insists he got the better deal.
Weighs in on air before tip-off, literally.
utep.temperament: Joyful and quick; bounces back by the next segment.
utep.compassion: Enormous. Shouts out the cafeteria workers by name.
utep.worldview: Family, neighbors and the Sun City first, and everybody gets a plate.

wyoming.bio: Darlene Pickett ran cattle outside Laramie for forty years, raised three kids and outlasted two blizzards that made the national news. She edits The Laramie Chronicle the way she worked the ranch: show up, do the chores, and don't whine about the wind. She trusts any team that has seen a Laramie winter and very few that haven't. She wears a full suit of polished plate armor engraved WYOMING on air, because, she says, the wind up here is not playing around.
wyoming.backstory: INVENTED. Raised on a cattle ranch outside Laramie; took it over from her father at twenty-four and ran it until her knees retired before she did.
wyoming.beat: INVENTED. Wrote a fiery letter to the Chronicle about road plowing and the owner asked her to edit the paper; she agreed if she could also cover the Cowboys.
wyoming.look: Full suit of polished steel plate armor with brass trim and WYOMING engraved on the chest, silver bob, steady unimpressed gaze (portrait).
wyoming.favorite: To research: a real Cowboys player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Air Force is a fine team for people who think a schedule can stop the weather.
If you can play through a Laramie January, March is a picnic.
The wind is part of the scouting report whether the visitors like it or not.
wyoming.off_air: INVENTED. Widowed; three grown kids and nine grandkids who all ride better than she does now. Keeps a border collie named Biscuit who attends every home game.
gags: Calls the Colonel 'Hank' to his face, which no one else dares.
Clanks when she gets excited.
Measures every road trip in how many times she had to stop for wind.
wyoming.temperament: Tough, slow to anger, slower to forgive a lazy rebound.
wyoming.compassion: Fierce for the underdog and the neighbor in a ditch.
wyoming.humor: Raspy, deadpan, merciless with a punchline.
wyoming.worldview: Work hard, look after your neighbors, and don't trust people who've never been cold.

eastern-washington.bio: Cody Lindqvist sold insurance in Spokane for fifteen years and moved to Cheney after reading that small towns were good for the soul. He edits The Cheney Gazette and explains every Eagles game through the wheat harvest, which he has watched from his car but never actually worked. Local farmers correct him gently and often. He loves the red court, long drives on the back roads and anybody who boxes out. He is still trying to learn what a combine does.
eastern-washington.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in a Spokane suburb, son of a dentist; sold home and auto insurance for fifteen years and was very good at it.
eastern-washington.beat: INVENTED. Bought a subscription to the Gazette, wrote in to correct a box score, and was offered the sports page because nobody else applied.
eastern-washington.look: Red and white quarter-zip with EASTERN WASHINGTON script, neat brown hair, friendly salesman smile (portrait).
eastern-washington.favorite: To research: a real Eagles player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Moscow, Idaho is a lovely town that should stop pretending it's on the map twice.
A rebound is like a harvest, he thinks, though he has been told it isn't.
Nothing beats a Tuesday night on the red floor.
eastern-washington.off_air: INVENTED. Married to Becca, a vet tech who grew up on an actual wheat farm and finds him adorable. Two kids, one golden retriever, zero farm equipment.
gags: Mixes up threshing and thrashing on air at least once a month.
Josie fact-checks his farm metaphors with a raised eyebrow.
Keeps a laminated diagram of a combine on his desk, upside down.
eastern-washington.compassion: Kind and sincere; first to sign up for any volunteer sheet.
eastern-washington.humor: Mostly unintentional; the farm metaphors do the work.
eastern-washington.worldview: Small towns made him a better neighbor, and he's trying to earn the welcome.
eastern-washington.rube: Yes: the lovable suburban rube who thinks he's a farmer.

idaho.bio: Josie Carver grew up in Moscow, worked summers on Forest Service trail crews and spent ten years as a structural engineer for timber buildings. She edits The Moscow Courant and talks about the timber-built arena the way some people talk about cathedrals. She loves a Vandals team that defends and has very little patience for anyone who calls Moscow the other Moscow. She can tell you the load rating of every beam in the building, and occasionally does during a timeout.
idaho.backstory: INVENTED. Born in Moscow to a librarian and a wheat-and-lentil farmer; spent a decade designing mass-timber buildings for a firm in Boise.
idaho.beat: INVENTED. Came home when her father got sick, started writing about the arena's construction for the Courant and ended up running the paper.
idaho.look: Black and gold striped polo with IDAHO embroidered, long dark wavy hair, calm direct gaze (portrait).
idaho.favorite: To research: a real Vandals player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Cheney is a fine town if you need gas on the way to Spokane.
Defense wins in the Palouse because winter has already tested everybody.
There is no 'other Moscow'; there is only the one with a timber arena.
idaho.off_air: INVENTED. Lives in a small house she framed herself; partner Sam teaches middle school band. Cross-country skis to work when it snows.
gags: Corrects Cody's wheat metaphors with actual yield numbers.
Rates every win by how much the timber rafters creaked.
Refuses to explain her 'second time requires paperwork' rule.
idaho.appropriateness: PG. She saves her one swear for officials.
idaho.compassion: Solid; helps people move, literally and otherwise.
idaho.humor: Dry engineer humor with excellent timing.
idaho.worldview: Build things that last and look after the people who use them.

idaho-state.bio: Dale Pickett has kept a backyard weather station in Pocatello since 1994 and reports every Bengals result alongside the gusts. He edits The Pocatello Register and blames the wind for every loss and credits it for every win, despite repeated reminders that basketball is played indoors. He used to read meters for the power company and still knows every dog on the east side by name. No relation to the Wyoming Picketts, he says, though he has never checked.
idaho-state.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in Pocatello, son of a railroad brakeman; read power meters for twenty-six years and knows every backyard in town.
idaho-state.beat: INVENTED. Mailed his daily wind readings to the Register for a decade until they gave him a column, then the sports desk, mostly so the readings would stop.
idaho-state.look: Orange and black hoodie with IDAHO STATE across the chest, graying brown hair, easy squint-smile of a man who has stood in wind (portrait).
idaho-state.favorite: To research: a real Bengals player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Weber State would be decent if they ever played in a crosswind.
The wind in Pocatello is a sixth man, indoors or not.
A good anemometer is more reliable than any power ranking.
idaho-state.off_air: INVENTED. Married to Connie, who has asked him to stop reading the weather station during dinner. Grandfather of two who think his anemometer is a toy.
gags: Gives wind speed and direction before the final score.
Insists to Mitch that he's no relation to Darlene, then asks Mitch if he's related to Ogden.
Licks a finger and holds it up before every free throw.
idaho-state.appropriateness: G. 'Oh, for crying out loud' is his ceiling.
idaho-state.compassion: Warm; shovels his neighbors' walks before his own.
idaho-state.worldview: The world makes more sense if you write down the weather every day.

montana.bio: Wren Halvorsen grew up fishing the Clark Fork with her father and spent fifteen years as a river guide and fisheries technician. She edits The Missoula Clarion and reads a basketball game like a river: patient through the slow water and merciless when someone forgets to box out. She hikes to the M on the hill after every home win and has never missed one. She considers a lazy closeout a personal insult to the state of Montana.
montana.backstory: INVENTED. Born in Missoula to a fly-shop owner and a nurse; guided on the Blackfoot and Clark Fork, then counted trout for the state.
montana.beat: INVENTED. Wrote a fishing-report column for the Clarion that wandered into Griz basketball every February; the paper finally gave her the beat.
montana.look: Maroon fleece quarter-zip with MONTANA script, shoulder-length brown hair, composed level look (portrait).
montana.favorite: To research: a real Grizzlies player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Bozeman is a lovely place to buy a twelve-dollar coffee.
Boxing out is the closest thing basketball has to reading water.
Dahlberg on a cold Tuesday is the best ticket in the West.
montana.off_air: INVENTED. Lives with her husband Eli, a smokejumper, and a one-eyed lab named Riffle. Ties her own flies in Griz colors.
gags: Gives river-flow conditions as a metaphor for each half.
Tells Brody his ski-pass takes are 'upstream of reality'.
Hikes the M after every home win and reports the time.
montana.compassion: Strong and practical; shows up with a casserole and a chainsaw.
montana.humor: Understated and precise; the joke is in the metaphor.
montana.worldview: Respect the land, read the water, and box out.

montana-state.bio: Brody Kessler moved to Bozeman for one ski season eight years ago and never left. He's a shameless Bobcat who reads every win as a sign from the Bridgers, often upside down. He worked lift operations, then a coffee cart, then the front desk of The Bozeman Sentinel, where he talked his way onto the basketball page. He still has the ski pass from his first season clipped to his jacket and celebrates big wins by falling down Bridger Bowl.
montana-state.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in suburban Minneapolis, son of two accountants; came west for a gap year that became a decade of lift lines and latte art.
montana-state.beat: INVENTED. Covered a Bobcats game for the Sentinel when the regular writer got stuck in a snowstorm, filed it from his phone on the chairlift, and they kept him.
montana-state.look: Blue and gold polo with MONTANA STATE embroidered, swoopy brown hair, clean-shaven, eager grin (portrait).
montana-state.favorite: To research: a real Bobcats player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Missoula is a nice town for people who like being rained on.
A powder day and a home win are basically the same feeling.
The Bridgers can predict a season if you read them right, which he usually doesn't.
montana-state.off_air: INVENTED. Lives with three roommates and a sourdough starter he named after the Bobcats' leading rebounder. Snowboards badly and loves it.
gags: Reads the Bridger Range like tea leaves and is almost always wrong.
Wren corrects his river metaphors and he thanks her, sincerely.
Reports his own wipeouts with the same seriousness as the box score.
montana-state.compassion: Big; first to help push a car out of a snowbank.
montana-state.humor: Goofy and self-mocking; he is the joke.
montana-state.worldview: Life is good if you're outside and your team is winning.

northern-arizona.bio: Rita Yazzie spent twenty-five years running the visitor programs at an observatory outside Flagstaff, explaining dark skies to tourists with patience and a red flashlight. She edits The Flagstaff Almanac now and reminds every visiting team about the altitude and every Lumberjack about defensive footwork. She is warm, wry and unbothered, which she credits to living at seven thousand feet. She once delayed a column to wait for a meteor shower and doesn't regret it.
northern-arizona.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in Flagstaff, daughter of a forest ranger and a school cook; ran public stargazing programs for a quarter century.
northern-arizona.beat: INVENTED. Wrote the Almanac's monthly night-sky column for years; the editor retired and named her successor by pointing at her.
northern-arizona.look: Blue and gold hoodie with NORTHERN ARIZONA across the front, chin-length blond bob, warm unhurried smile (portrait).
northern-arizona.favorite: To research: a real Lumberjacks player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: St. George is a fine place to visit if you've forgotten what winter is.
Visiting teams should be issued oxygen and an apology.
Footwork is the first thing altitude exposes.
northern-arizona.off_air: INVENTED. Married to Dan, a retired snowplow driver; two grown kids and a telescope in the backyard. Hosts star parties after home wins.
gags: Gives the altitude before the score.
Mails Kenzie a sky chart every rivalry week with the rival's logo drawn as a dim star.
Times defensive slides with a stargazer's red flashlight.
northern-arizona.appropriateness: G. She whispers when she's angry.
northern-arizona.compassion: High. Notices the shy kid in every crowd.
northern-arizona.worldview: The universe is big and that's a reason to be kind, not small.

northern-colorado.bio: Gus Ferraro ran a diner on Eighth Avenue in Greeley for thirty-one years and still orders the same thing there every morning: two eggs over easy, hash browns extra crispy and a slice of pie for later. He edits The Greeley Argus and means everything with his whole chest. He defends Greeley's aroma, the Bears' defense and his diner order, in that order. He considers any criticism of the smell a personal attack on the local economy.
northern-colorado.backstory: INVENTED. Born in Greeley to an Italian railroad family; cooked, waited tables and finally owned the diner he started at as a dishwasher.
northern-colorado.beat: INVENTED. The Argus held its staff meetings at his diner for years; when the sports editor left, they offered him the job in lieu of paying the tab.
northern-colorado.look: Navy and gold quarter-zip with NORTHERN COLORADO, trim graying hair, lean build, kind lined face (portrait).
northern-colorado.favorite: To research: a real Bears player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Ogden is a fine town that would benefit from a real diner.
Greeley smells like money, and the money smells fine.
Pie is a postgame meal, a pregame meal and a halftime adjustment.
northern-colorado.off_air: INVENTED. Married forty years to Rosa, who now runs the diner and won't let him in the kitchen. Coaches a church-league team that has never won.
gags: Ranks wins by pie flavor.
Tells Mitch that Ogden 'smells like nothing' and means it as an insult.
Sits in the diner until the pie case explains the loss.
northern-colorado.compassion: Enormous. Feeds anyone who comes in cold.
northern-colorado.humor: Earnest and unaware; he's funny because he's dead serious.
northern-colorado.worldview: A town is a family that eats at the same counter.

portland-state.bio: Juniper Tran rode the streetcar to every Vikings home game as a student and never stopped. She worked as a TriMet route planner, then a food-cart reviewer, and now edits The Portland Ledger, where she covers the Vikings like a city beat. She is fair-minded and quick, with rain-soaked patience and a soft spot for anyone who took transit to the game. She has rated two hundred food-cart dumplings and keeps the spreadsheet open during broadcasts.
portland-state.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in Southeast Portland, daughter of a pharmacist and a bus driver; planned transit routes for four years after college.
portland-state.beat: INVENTED. Wrote a food-cart blog that the Ledger picked up; she kept slipping basketball into the reviews until they gave her the Vikings.
portland-state.look: White polo with green trim and PORTLAND STATE embroidered, long light brown hair pulled back, steady pleasant expression (portrait).
portland-state.favorite: To research: a real Vikings player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Cheney is a lovely town to drive through in under five minutes.
A team that plays downtown should be cheered by people who walked there.
Rain is a home-court advantage nobody wants to admit.
portland-state.off_air: INVENTED. Lives in a studio near the Park Blocks with a bike and a fern named Ruth. Volunteers at a Saturday food bank.
gags: Grades every arena by its transit access.
Sends Cody a streetcar map every rivalry week; he still drives.
Has a dumpling rating for every road trip in the conference.
portland-state.compassion: High. Notices who had to take two buses to get there.
portland-state.worldview: Cities work when they're built for people, and so do teams.

southern-utah.bio: Tanner Holt sold RVs in Cedar City for a decade before taking over The Cedar City Banner when its editor moved to St. George. He loves the T-Birds and the summer theater festival, though he has only ever read the posters and quotes plays he hasn't seen with great confidence. He coaches Little League in the spring and keeps a wall of festival posters in his office, arranged by color. He believes every basketball game has three acts, and he counts them wrong.
southern-utah.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in Cedar City, son of a hardware-store owner; sold RVs at the family dealership for ten years.
southern-utah.beat: INVENTED. Bought the Banner's ad space for the dealership for years and eventually just bought into the paper; the sports page was the part nobody else wanted.
southern-utah.look: Red and white hoodie with SOUTHERN UTAH across the front, short dark hair, neat stubble, steady sincere look (portrait).
southern-utah.favorite: To research: a real Thunderbirds player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: St. George is just Cedar City with more golf carts.
Every great game is a three-act play, and he's sure there are three.
The summer festival is the finest theater in America, according to the posters.
southern-utah.off_air: INVENTED. Married to Kelsey, a high school drama teacher who has given up correcting his quotes. Four kids, one minivan, many posters.
gags: Quotes Shakespeare from posters and gets the plays mixed up.
Calls Kenzie's program 'a promising first draft' every rivalry week.
Gives each half a curtain call.
southern-utah.compassion: Big; first to volunteer for the concession stand.
southern-utah.humor: Confidently wrong; the joke is on him.
southern-utah.worldview: Art and sports both make a small town feel big, even if he hasn't seen the play.

utah-tech.bio: Kenzie Larsen grew up in St. George watching the college move up a level at a time, and she says she is doing the same thing. She was a physical therapist before she joined The St. George Courier, and she covers the Trailblazers like a young program with something to prove, because it is, and so is she. She is bright and blunt, allergic to excuses and fond of a good trail run before tip-off. She keeps a whiteboard of program milestones and checks them off in red.
utah-tech.backstory: INVENTED. Born in St. George to a contractor and a nurse; physical therapist at a sports clinic for nine years.
utah-tech.beat: INVENTED. Started a podcast about the Division I move that got more listeners than the Courier's sports page; the paper hired her to stop the competition.
utah-tech.look: Navy and red quarter-zip with UTAH TECH, straight brown hair, athletic build, open confident smile (portrait).
utah-tech.favorite: To research: a real Trailblazers player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Cedar City is lovely if you like snow in April.
