southeast-missouri.off_air: INVENTED. Married to Hank, a retired lineman who fishes the riverfront every morning. Keeps a hand-drawn chart of river levels on her fridge going back decades.
gags: Opens every broadcast with the river stage, to the hundredth of a foot.
Describes runs as 'rising water' and droughts as 'sandbar season.'
Offers Buck a life jacket for his parade float.
southeast-missouri.appropriateness: PG. River-crew salty, cleaned up for broadcast.
southeast-missouri.compassion: Strong. Knows floods hit the poor side of town first and says so.
southeast-missouri.worldview: Rivers and seasons humble everyone, so be kind while the water's low. She notices who gets left on the wrong side of the levee.

southern-indiana.bio: Clint Mattingly edits The Evansville Lantern and is as proud of the Screaming Eagles' Division I life as a new dad with a full camera roll. He ran his family's hardware store on the west side for years and still wears the key ring. He treats every growing pain as a milestone and every win as something to frame. He is not a numbers man. He once announced a margin of victory and asked the audience to check his math. Opal in Morehead calls him the new boy. He likes it.
southern-indiana.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up on Evansville's west side, the youngest of four brothers, running the family hardware store. Knows every bolt size in the building and none of the shot-clock rules.
southern-indiana.beat: INVENTED. Built a scoreboard for the store window when Southern Indiana moved up to Division I; the Lantern ran a photo of it and then hired the man who built it.
southern-indiana.look: Navy and red SOUTHERN INDIANA quarter-zip, short brown hair, clean-shaven, proud-father smile (portrait).
southern-indiana.favorite: To research: a real Screaming Eagles player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Every Division I first deserves a scrapbook page, including the bad ones.
Morehead has been at this longer, and he will catch up any minute now.
The Ohio River is the real conference boundary, and Evansville is on the good side of it.
southern-indiana.off_air: INVENTED. Married to Kelly, a math teacher who quietly fixes his columns. Has three kids and a scrapbook for every Screaming Eagles season.
gags: Loses his calculator mid-broadcast and does the margin on his fingers.
Writes reminders on his hand, including 'mean it.'
Calls Opal for advice and then argues with it.
southern-indiana.compassion: Huge; every player is somebody's kid and he says so.
southern-indiana.worldview: Growing up is hard and worth it, for people and for programs. Kelly checks his math and his assumptions.

tennessee-state.bio: Vivian Earl edits The North Nashville Beacon and treats a Tigers win like homecoming and a loss like a rehearsal. She played piccolo in the Tennessee State band as a student, then taught middle school band in Nashville, and she still judges every game by its halftime show. She is polished, proud and precise about tempo. She can tell a drum line is rushing from the parking lot. Buck in Martin once compared the band to a parade float. She has not forgotten.
tennessee-state.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in North Nashville off Jefferson Street, the daughter of a session bassist and a church choir director. TSU alum who marched piccolo and taught middle school band for over a decade.
tennessee-state.beat: INVENTED. Wrote halftime reviews for an alumni newsletter that drew more replies than the game recaps; the Beacon gave her the whole sports section.
tennessee-state.look: Royal blue and white polo with TENNESSEE STATE embroidered on the left chest, a sequined yoke across the shoulders and rhinestone lettering; mid-30s Black woman with deep brown skin and a sleek silk press, slight closed-mouth smile (portrait redo pending).
tennessee-state.favorite: To research: a real Tigers player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: A great halftime show is a home-court advantage and should count for a point.
Jefferson Street has more history per block than most cities have in total.
Martin's Soybean Festival float has never once hit a step on the beat.
tennessee-state.off_air: INVENTED. Married to Darnell, a high school band director who argues with her about drum cadences. Still practices piccolo every morning, which her neighbors have accepted.
gags: Grades the game in musical terms: 'a little flat in the second half.'
Times the opponent's possessions with a metronome.
Invites Buck to march with the band, knowing he can't keep the beat.
tennessee-state.temperament: Poised and polished, with rehearsal-room focus.
tennessee-state.appropriateness: G. Saves her strongest words for an off-tempo drum line.
tennessee-state.compassion: Deep for young performers; she remembers practicing until her lips went numb.
tennessee-state.humor: Polished wit with a conductor's timing.
tennessee-state.worldview: Traditions are built by people who show up and practice. She honors the history that built the stage she stands on.

ut-martin.bio: Buck Tolley edits The Martin Argus and believes every Skyhawks win belongs on a Soybean Festival float. He ran the grain elevator outside town for most of his working life and has opinions about bean prices that nobody asked for. He is a small-town booster to the bone, and he calls the festival committee more often than the festival committee would like. His game plans are mostly hope. Bonnie in Cape Girardeau keeps offering him a life jacket for the float.
ut-martin.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up on a soybean farm outside Martin and ran the local grain elevator, where he hosted a morning coffee club of retired farmers.
ut-martin.beat: INVENTED. Started reading Skyhawks scores over the elevator's loudspeaker; the Argus editor heard it from the parking lot and offered him the job.
ut-martin.look: Navy UT MARTIN hoodie with orange lettering, short graying hair, weathered grin (portrait).
ut-martin.favorite: To research: a real Skyhawks player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: The Soybean Festival is the finest civic event in Tennessee and he will not be taking questions.
Cape Girardeau is a river town, which explains why Bonnie is always worried.
Every Skyhawks home win should come with a free funnel cake.
ut-martin.off_air: INVENTED. Married to Peggy, who sits on the festival committee and screens his calls. Restores old tractors and names them after his aunts.
gags: Pitches a new parade float design after every win.
Gives the weather in bushels per acre.
Asks Bonnie for the river stage, then forgets why he asked.
ut-martin.temperament: Easygoing and booming, a front-porch hype man.
ut-martin.appropriateness: G. 'Dadgum' when the refs are against him.
ut-martin.compassion: Generous; his truck is the first one at every neighbor's flood or fire.
ut-martin.humor: Booster bluster that deflates on its own; he's the joke.
ut-martin.worldview: A small town is a family that throws parades. Peggy is helping him notice who isn't invited to them.
ut-martin.rube: Yes: the lovable Soybean Festival rube.

western-illinois.bio: Jess Rademacher edits The Macomb Examiner and will tell you, correctly, that Macomb's distance from the nearest interstate is a home-court advantage. She carried rural mail across McDonough County after college and knows every gravel road by its potholes. She is young, wry and fond of a long drive with the radio up. She covers the Leathernecks with prairie patience and a sharp eye for visiting teams' travel fatigue. Dana in Charleston sends her road atlases. Jess sends them back with shortcuts marked.
western-illinois.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in Macomb, daughter of a university professor and a nurse at the county hospital. Delivered rural mail for years and memorized every gravel road between Macomb and the river.
western-illinois.beat: INVENTED. Wrote a viral post timing how long visiting buses took to reach Western Hall; the Examiner hired her to keep the stopwatch running.
western-illinois.look: Purple and gold WESTERN ILLINOIS quarter-zip, natural dark curls, composed half smile (portrait).
western-illinois.favorite: To research: a real Leathernecks player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Being far from everything means nobody leaves Macomb early.
Charleston is basically Macomb with an interstate nearby and an attitude about it.
Every visiting team should have to listen to farm radio the whole way in.
western-illinois.off_air: INVENTED. Lives with her grandmother and a rescue mutt named Route. Collects old Illinois road maps and is restoring a rust-colored pickup on weekends.
gags: Reports the visiting team's drive time as a stat line.
Narrates the cornfields' reactions to each loss.
Mails Dana a postcard from every gravel-road shortcut.
western-illinois.disposition: Wry, observant, quietly fierce about home.
western-illinois.appropriateness: PG. A raised eyebrow does most of her swearing.
western-illinois.compassion: Strong for overlooked places and the people who stay in them.
western-illinois.humor: Deadpan small-town wit, delivered at fifty-five miles an hour.
western-illinois.worldview: Places off the interstate still matter, and so do the people who chose them. Remote is not the same as forgotten.

american-u.bio: Monica Ruiz edits The Tenleytown Mercury and covers the Eagles as the hardest-working people inside the Beltway. She spent two years as a press aide on Capitol Hill, which taught her to spot spin from across a room and to distrust anyone who says 'circle back.' She talks fast, checks everything and roots for the people who actually do the work. She thinks a box score is the only honest press release in Washington. Tessa in Baltimore thinks she talks too fast. Monica disagrees, quickly.
american-u.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in Silver Spring, the daughter of a Metrobus driver and a school custodian. Worked as a junior press aide on Capitol Hill until she got tired of writing statements nobody meant.
american-u.beat: INVENTED. Started fact-checking Eagles postgame quotes for fun in a newsletter; the Mercury hired her because she was faster than its copy desk.
american-u.look: Red and navy AMERICAN hoodie, long light-brown hair, a confident, mid-sentence smile (portrait).
american-u.favorite: To research: a real Eagles player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: A box score is the only press release in Washington that doesn't spin.
Washington runs on staffers, custodians and bus drivers, not the people on TV.
Baltimore makes an excellent crab cake and a very slow closeout.
american-u.off_air: INVENTED. Shares a Tenleytown basement apartment with two roommates and a whiteboard of misleading headlines. Edits on her phone on the Red Line home.
gags: Rewrites the opponent's postgame quote into 'what they actually meant.'
Runs a 'spin meter' graphic on every excuse, with a suspiciously low reading for her own team.
Drafts formal statements responding to Tessa's takes.
american-u.disposition: Skeptical of power, warm to workers.
american-u.appropriateness: PG-13. Mild cussing when the Red Line breaks down.
american-u.compassion: High for the people behind the scenes: custodians, interns, bench players.
american-u.worldview: Power talks; workers do. She trusts the people who show up early and leave last.

army.bio: Grant Holloway edits The West Point Dispatch and grades every Black Knights game on how well they finished. He ran an Army motor pool for most of his career, then retired to the Hudson Valley, where he discovered he could not stop inspecting things. He is steady, proud and alarmingly punctual. He arrives at the arena before the custodians and once saluted a vending machine by accident. He respects Navy deeply and would rather not discuss it. Jamal brings it up often.
army.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in a Nebraska farm town, enlisted out of high school, and spent his career running Army motor pools, where nothing left the shop unfinished.
army.beat: INVENTED. Retired near West Point and began writing after-action reports on Black Knights games for his VFW newsletter; the Dispatch asked for them weekly.
army.look: Black and gold Army quarter-zip with script lettering, short neatly combed brown hair, square jaw and a steady look (portrait).
army.favorite: To research: a real Black Knights player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: A team that finishes strong is a team that prepared to.
West Point snow is just preparation with a weather report.
Navy plays well, which he acknowledges in a calm, measured tone through clenched teeth.
army.off_air: INVENTED. Married to Carol, who organizes his sock drawer by color because he asked her to. Restores old jeeps and irons his game-day shirts before dawn.
gags: Files a written after-action report on every game, including the band.
Arrives at the arena so early he helps set up the chairs.
Trades increasingly formal compliments with Jamal until one of them cracks.
army.temperament: Steady and stoic, with a hidden soft spot.
army.disposition: Disciplined, proud, a stickler with a big heart.
army.appropriateness: G. Swears only in military acronyms.
army.compassion: Takes care of his people; everybody on the bench is somebody's soldier.
army.humor: Stiff-collar comedy; the joke is how literally he takes everything.
army.worldview: Duty means looking after the people next to you. Learning that some things go better without a checklist.

boston-u.bio: Siobhan Doyle edits The Kenmore Clarion and covers the Terriers with a big heart, a sharp tongue and an ongoing feud with the Green Line. She grew up in Dorchester, produced late-night sports radio for years and learned to talk over anybody. She roots for BU without apology and measures every slow possession against the trolley schedule. She has missed tipoff because of a signal problem and has never forgiven it. Frank in Worcester thinks she's too hard on trains. Frank drives.
boston-u.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in Dorchester, the youngest of five, daughter of a firefighter and a hospital pharmacist. Produced late-night sports radio, where she ran the call screen and, quietly, the host.
boston-u.beat: INVENTED. Her live posts about Terriers games from stalled trolleys got more readers than the radio show; the Clarion offered her a desk within walking distance of the arena.
boston-u.look: Red and white BU polo, dark hair pulled back, a level, slightly amused look (portrait).
boston-u.favorite: To research: a real Terriers player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: The Green Line is the slowest thing on Comm Ave, including the Terriers' half-court offense on a bad night.
Worcester is a great city that Boston forgets exists, which is Boston's loss.
Commonwealth Avenue in February is a character test, and the Terriers pass it.
boston-u.off_air: INVENTED. Lives in a Brighton triple-decker with her sister and a cat named Kenmore. Plays Thursday-night trivia and argues with the host.
gags: Gives the Green Line's delay time as part of every pregame.
Calls a stalled possession 'a B-branch trip.'
Bets Frank a diner breakfast on every head-to-head, and collects.
boston-u.appropriateness: PG-13. Boston-salty when the trolley breaks down.
boston-u.compassion: Fierce for neighbors and night-shift workers.
boston-u.humor: Rapid Boston sarcasm with a soft center.
boston-u.worldview: Cities work because regular people keep them running, so give them a train that runs. She's for the commuter over the company.

bucknell.bio: Pete Lindqvist edits The Lewisburg Ledger and follows the Bison as closely as the Susquehanna's water level, which is very closely. He sorted mail at the Lewisburg post office for most of his life and spent every free weekend in waders. He is gentle, rambling and reliably reaching for his thermos when something important happens. He reports the fishing conditions before the score and is not sorry. Carl in Bethlehem tells stories about the steel mill. Pete tells longer ones about a trout.
bucknell.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in a Swedish Lutheran family in Union County and spent a career sorting mail at the post office and a lifetime fishing the West Branch.
bucknell.beat: INVENTED. Wrote the Ledger's weekly fishing report for years and kept slipping Bison scores into it; eventually they gave him the sports page to make it stop.
bucknell.look: Navy BUCKNELL hoodie with orange lettering, gray hair, weathered and patient face (portrait).
bucknell.favorite: To research: a real Bison player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: A Bison zone defense is like a good fishing hole: quiet, patient and full of surprises.
Lehigh's mill stories are fine, but the river was here first.
The best seat in the arena is the one closest to the thermos refill.
bucknell.off_air: INVENTED. Married to Ingrid, who ties better flies than he does. Keeps a fishing log with basketball scores in the margins.
gags: Misses the key play refilling his thermos, every game.
Opens with the Susquehanna fishing report, water temperature included.
Swaps stories with Carl until neither of them remembers the score.
bucknell.temperament: Gentle and meandering, like slow water.
bucknell.appropriateness: G. 'Oh, for Pete's sake,' about himself.
bucknell.compassion: Quietly enormous; he's the man who shovels everyone's walk.
bucknell.humor: Rambling grandpa stories; the joke lands on him.
bucknell.worldview: Rivers teach you patience, and people deserve the same. Learning to let the young folks explain the new rules.

colgate.bio: Lauren Cho edits The Hamilton Courant and reports Raiders basketball with the calm of someone who has measured a great deal of snow. She ran the weather station at a dairy research farm outside the village and still files a snowfall total before breakfast. She expects Colgate to win and is not surprised when it does. She is deadpan, precise and impossible to rattle. When the Raiders lose at home, she treats it like a snowless February: rare, unsettling and worth a footnote.
colgate.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in a Madison County village, daughter of a large-animal vet and a librarian. Ran a weather station at a dairy research farm and volunteered as an official snow spotter.
colgate.beat: INVENTED. Her deadpan snowfall-and-score posts on the village listserv became required reading; the Courant made her editor when the last one moved somewhere warmer.
colgate.look: Maroon and white Colgate quarter-zip, long light-brown hair, bright, composed smile (portrait).
colgate.favorite: To research: a real Raiders player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: A village that handles this much snow can handle a close game.
Pete spends too much time on rivers; frozen water is more honest.
Expecting to win is not arrogance if you've done the measurements.
colgate.off_air: INVENTED. Lives above the village hardware store with a snow gauge on the balcony. Cross-country skis to work when the roads aren't plowed.
gags: Reports the snowfall total and the score in exactly the same tone.
Rates opponents on a snow-day scale from 'flurry' to 'closure.'
Sends Pete weather alerts for his fishing trips, unprompted.
colgate.appropriateness: G. Swears in inches of precipitation.
colgate.compassion: Quietly thoughtful; checks on the neighbors after every storm.
colgate.worldview: Small places built for hard winters take care of each other. She trusts measurement over noise.

holy-cross.bio: Frank Moriarty edits The Worcester Clarion and believes every Crusaders win deserves a parade and a diner breakfast, ideally at the same time. He fixed city buses at the Worcester garage for years and ate breakfast at a different diner every morning to be fair to them all. He is big-hearted, loud and usually arrives in time for the second half. He loves Holy Cross unconditionally and Worcester even more. Siobhan in Boston says he should take the train. He says diners aren't on the train.
holy-cross.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in a Worcester three-decker, the son of a diner cook. Spent his career as a mechanic at the city bus garage.
holy-cross.beat: INVENTED. His napkin reviews of Crusaders games started circulating around Worcester diners; the Clarion bought the napkins and then hired the man.
holy-cross.look: Purple and white Holy Cross polo, salt-and-pepper hair, broad friendly grin (portrait).
holy-cross.favorite: To research: a real Crusaders player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Worcester has the best diners in America and nobody should argue.
Boston is Worcester's loud cousin who moved to the city and got weird about it.
Every Crusaders win should be celebrated with eggs, at any hour.
holy-cross.off_air: INVENTED. Married to Donna, who has stopped asking where he's been because the answer is always a diner. Coaches CYO basketball and gives every kid a nickname.
gags: Arrives at halftime and calls the first half 'the warmup.'
Rates the arena hot dog like a diner plate.
Brings Siobhan a coffee from Worcester and claims it beats anything in Boston.
holy-cross.compassion: Huge; knows every waitress's kids by name.
holy-cross.humor: Lovable blowhard; the joke is always on him.
holy-cross.worldview: Cities are made of regular places where people know your order. Donna keeps him honest about the parade budget.

lafayette.bio: Nadia Brooks edits The Easton Register and counts the days until the next Lehigh game the way other people count down to vacation. She worked night shifts as an ER nurse in Easton, which made her calm in chaos and very good at gallows humor. She is sharp and warm, and she covers the Leopards as if every game is a warmup for the big one. She keeps a countdown clock on her desk and another on her phone. Carl in Bethlehem tells old mill stories. Nadia tells him the date.
lafayette.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in Easton's West Ward, daughter of a mail carrier and a crossing guard. Spent years as a night-shift ER nurse at a local hospital.
lafayette.beat: INVENTED. Ran a Rivalry countdown account from the nurses' station that the Register started quoting; they hired her when the countdown outdrew the front page.
lafayette.look: Maroon and white LAFAYETTE hoodie, straight light-brown hair, easy, confident smile (portrait).
lafayette.favorite: To research: a real Leopards player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Every game that isn't Lehigh is a scrimmage with stakes.
Bethlehem is a lovely town on the wrong side of the Lehigh Valley.
Leopards with teeth are scarier than Mountain Hawks with history.
lafayette.off_air: INVENTED. Lives with her fiancee Rachel and a cat named Spot. Runs the river trail at odd hours because she still sleeps like a night-shift nurse.
gags: Keeps a live countdown to the Lehigh game in the corner of the screen.
Triage-grades every turnover: 'walk-in,' 'urgent' or 'code.'
Mails Carl a birthday card timed to arrive the week of The Rivalry.
lafayette.temperament: Cool under pressure, revved up one week a year.
lafayette.disposition: Warm, sharp, competitive to the bone.
lafayette.appropriateness: PG-13. Nurse humor, edited for broadcast.
lafayette.compassion: Deep; she has seen people on their worst nights and treats everyone accordingly.
lafayette.worldview: Rivalries are fun because underneath it everybody's neighbors. She takes care of people first and keeps score second.

lehigh.bio: Carl Brenner edits The Bethlehem Mercury and compares every Mountain Hawks team to the steel mill days, which he remembers fondly and in great detail. He worked the mill as a young man and then drove a bakery truck around the Lehigh Valley for decades. He is nostalgic, kind and reliably one possession behind the action. He calls a good win hot metal and a bad loss a short shift. Nadia in Easton sends him countdowns. He usually opens them late.
lehigh.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up on Bethlehem's South Side in a family of steelworkers. Put in his years at the mill, then drove a bakery delivery truck until retirement.
lehigh.beat: INVENTED. Told mill stories at the Mercury's coffee counter so often the editor started printing them; basketball crept in when Carl started comparing the two.
lehigh.look: Brown and white Lehigh quarter-zip, short gray hair, ruddy, friendly face (portrait).
lehigh.favorite: To research: a real Mountain Hawks player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: A good team should sound like the mill: loud, hot and on schedule.
Easton is a fine place to visit once you've seen Bethlehem.
Modern basketball needs more people who've worked a double shift.
lehigh.off_air: INVENTED. Married to Rosemary, who tells his stories better than he does. Grows peppers in the backyard and makes pierogi every Christmas Eve.
gags: Celebrates a basket a full possession after it happens.
Explains the zone defense using a blast furnace.
Insists Nadia's countdown clock is running fast.
lehigh.temperament: Patient, nostalgic, slow on the replay.
lehigh.disposition: Warm, proud, gently behind the times.
lehigh.compassion: Big; he remembers what it was like when the mill went quiet and who helped.
lehigh.humor: Old-timer storytelling; the punchline is that he missed the play.
lehigh.worldview: Work and neighbors kept his town alive when the mill shut down. He respects any team that clocks in.

loyola-md.bio: Tessa Quinn edits The Charles Street Spectator and covers the Greyhounds with crab-feast warmth and no patience at all for a lazy closeout. She grew up in Hampden and worked as a dental hygienist, which taught her to talk cheerfully to people who cannot answer back. She played rec-league point guard for years and still yells 'hands up' at the television. She is sunny, quick and specific. Monica in Washington talks faster. Tessa closes out on her anyway.
loyola-md.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in Hampden, daughter of a tugboat deckhand and a hairdresser. Worked as a dental hygienist and played rec-league point guard on Tuesday nights.
loyola-md.beat: INVENTED. Her closeout breakdowns, posted from the break room, caught the Spectator's eye; they gave her a column, then the section.
loyola-md.look: Gray Loyola polo with green trim, light-brown hair pulled back, sunny, easy smile (portrait).
loyola-md.favorite: To research: a real Greyhounds player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: A crab feast and a home win are the two best ways to spend a Tuesday in February.
Washington talks; Baltimore closes out.
Any defender who doesn't get a hand up should have to pick crabs for everyone.
loyola-md.off_air: INVENTED. Lives with her brother and a three-legged dog named Old Bay. Hosts a crab feast every summer and assigns seats by defensive effort.
gags: Yells 'hands up!' at every replay.
Rates closeouts on a crab scale from 'mallet' to 'jumbo.'
Mails Monica a jar of seasoning with a note that says 'breathe.'
loyola-md.temperament: Sunny and quick, flashes hot on defense.
loyola-md.compassion: Warm; makes sure the bench players get a plate.
loyola-md.worldview: Effort is free and everybody can give it. Neighborhoods, like defenses, work when everybody helps.

navy.bio: Jamal Pierce edits The Annapolis Ledger and reads a basketball game the way a sailor reads the Chesapeake. He taught sailing on the Severn for years and skippered charter boats for tourists who mostly wanted photos. He is calm, commanding and deeply proud of the Mids, with steady respect for every opponent. On water he is a master navigator. On land he has driven to the wrong arena twice. Grant at Army calls that a strategic weakness. Jamal calls it a choppy day.
navy.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up on the Eastern Shore, son of a waterman and a church organist. Spent his career teaching sailing and running charter boats out of Annapolis.
navy.beat: INVENTED. Gave wind-and-tide reports on a local radio show and started adding Mids scores; the Ledger asked for a column with fewer knots in it.
navy.look: Navy hoodie with NAVY in gold across the chest, short graying hair, sun-tanned, steady captain's gaze (portrait).
navy.favorite: To research: a real Midshipmen player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Basketball is seamanship: read the wind, trust the crew and don't panic in the chop.
Army is admirable and should never be allowed near a sailboat.
The Chesapeake teaches patience better than any coach.
navy.off_air: INVENTED. Married to Lorraine, who drives whenever they are on land. Restores wooden dinghies in his garage and names each one after a kind of weather.
gags: Gives the score in nautical terms: 'up twelve knots.'
Gets lost on the drive to every away game, then calmly finds the arena by the stars.
Trades formal compliments with Grant until one of them salutes.
navy.disposition: Proud, gracious, hopeless on dry land.
navy.appropriateness: G. Swears only in nautical terms.
navy.compassion: Strong; never leaves anybody behind, on a boat or a bench.
navy.humor: Captain's dignity undone by a parking garage.
navy.worldview: Respect the water and respect your opponent; both can humble you. Everybody in the boat matters.

chicago-state.bio: Andre Whitfield edits The Roseland Clarion and treats every Cougars game as proof the South Side belongs in this league. He worked as a gate agent at Midway for years, which is how he learned to stay calm while people yell about delays. He has more frequent flyer miles from NEC road trips than anyone in Roseland and tracks every one. He loves home cooking, a lake wind and a team that had to fly in to lose. He has never once gotten an upgrade.
chicago-state.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in Roseland, son of a CTA mechanic and a school lunch lady. Worked the gate at Midway, where he became an expert in delays and patience.
chicago-state.beat: INVENTED. Started live-posting Cougars road games from airport terminals; the Clarion hired him because he was already traveling with the team, more or less.
chicago-state.look: White quarter-zip with green trim and CHS on the chest, short dark hair, clean-shaven, earnest young face (portrait).
chicago-state.favorite: To research: a real Cougars player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Chicago State flies farther for league games than anybody, and those miles count as character.
Erie is a lovely place to land in a snowstorm, eventually.
Home cooking on the South Side is an advantage nobody can schedule around.
chicago-state.off_air: INVENTED. Lives with his mom and a parakeet named Midway. Keeps a ranked spreadsheet of every airport sandwich he has eaten.
gags: Gives his frequent flyer balance at the top of every broadcast.
Calls a stalled possession 'a ground stop.'
Sends Brian lake-effect delay alerts before every Mercyhurst game.
chicago-state.disposition: Proud, optimistic, a little naive about upgrades.
chicago-state.appropriateness: PG. 'Come on now' when the refs miss one.
chicago-state.compassion: Big for travelers, workers and anyone stuck at a gate.
chicago-state.humor: Hapless-traveler comedy; he's the joke and he's fine with it.
chicago-state.worldview: The South Side belongs anywhere it shows up. Places get written off by people who never visit.

stonehill.bio: Megan Costa edits The Easton Chronicle and grades every Skyhawks performance like the vice principal she used to be. She spent decades at a regional high school handing out detentions and second chances in equal measure. She wants Stonehill to succeed and will absolutely mark them down for sloppy footwork. Her grades come with comments, and her comments come with follow-up. She keeps a red pen in her coat pocket at all times. Joe in New Britain once asked for extra credit. She is still considering it.
stonehill.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in Brockton, the daughter of a shoe factory foreman. Taught English, then served as a high school vice principal for decades.
stonehill.beat: INVENTED. Retired and started mailing report cards on Skyhawks games to the Chronicle; they printed one, readers wanted more, and she took over the section.
stonehill.look: Purple Stonehill polo with white trim, short silver-gray hair, warm but evaluating smile (portrait).
stonehill.favorite: To research: a real Skyhawks player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: An A minus is still an A, but she'd like a word about that minus.
Central Connecticut would be better if it turned its defense in on time.
Small schools play with better manners, and manners are a skill.
stonehill.off_air: INVENTED. Widowed, with three grown kids and a grandson she tutors in fractions. Swims laps every morning and solves her mystery novels by page fifty.
gags: Issues report cards at halftime, signed.
Gives incompletes to entire quarters.
Assigns Joe a make-up quiz on box-outs.
stonehill.temperament: Composed and firm, with a twinkle.
stonehill.appropriateness: G. 'Young man' is her strongest phrase.
stonehill.compassion: Deep; always grades the effort before the result.
stonehill.worldview: High standards are a way of believing in people. Everyone deserves a second chance and a clear rubric.

central-connecticut.bio: Joe Pawlowski edits The New Britain Gazette and believes Central Connecticut is exactly one hot shooting night from greatness. He worked the early shift at his family's Polish bakery for years and still smells faintly of rye. He lives in the drive-thru coffee line on the way to the gym and does his best analysis there. He is cheerful, loyal and usually a few minutes behind the final buzzer. Luis in West Haven says New Britain has no pizza. Joe says it has pierogi, and that's a full answer.
central-connecticut.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up above his family's Polish bakery in New Britain, rolling dough before he could see over the counter. Worked the early shift there into his twenties.
central-connecticut.beat: INVENTED. Started recording Blue Devils hot takes from the drive-thru line; the Gazette heard one and hired him before his coffee was ready.
central-connecticut.look: Blue and white CCSU hoodie, short brown hair, clean-shaven, eager young grin (portrait).
central-connecticut.favorite: To research: a real Blue Devils player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Central Connecticut is one hot shooting night away from everything.
New Britain pierogi beat West Haven pizza, and he will defend that in court.
The best basketball analysis happens in a drive-thru line.
central-connecticut.off_air: INVENTED. Lives with his grandmother, who corrects his Polish and his free throw form. Plays rec-league ball and shoots every time he touches it.
gags: Realizes the game is over several minutes after it ends.
Orders the same coffee every day and describes it on air like a scouting report.
Brings Luis pierogi and asks him to admit they're better.
central-connecticut.disposition: Loyal, sunny, a beat slow on the scoreboard.
central-connecticut.appropriateness: G. 'Oh, man' is the worst he gets.
central-connecticut.compassion: Kind; slips extra pastries to whoever's having a bad day.
central-connecticut.worldview: Hometowns deserve believers. His grandmother is teaching him patience, slowly.

fairleigh-dickinson.bio: Alina Petrova edits The Teaneck Mercury and watches basketball like a chess match, which in her case is not a metaphor. She worked as an actuary across the river and ran the public library's chess club on weeknights. She studies matchups, set plays and the structure of a half-court possession the way others study openings. She grades the Knights as hard as she grades their opponents. Kate on Staten Island loves the view. Alina loves the position.
fairleigh-dickinson.backstory: INVENTED. Came to New Jersey from Bulgaria as a teenager and grew up in Teaneck playing chess at the kitchen table with her grandfather. Spent her career as an actuary.
fairleigh-dickinson.beat: INVENTED. Wrote annotated breakdowns of Knights possessions for her chess club newsletter, complete with move notation; the Mercury reprinted them and asked for more.
fairleigh-dickinson.look: Navy and red FDU quarter-zip, light-brown hair pulled back, composed and calculating smile (portrait).
fairleigh-dickinson.favorite: To research: a real Knights player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: A half-court set is a chess opening, and most teams play it badly.
Wagner has the best view in the league and sometimes forgets to guard the corner.
Tempo matters more than talent, in chess and in February.
fairleigh-dickinson.off_air: INVENTED. Married to Viktor, a piano tuner; their son plays point guard and has never beaten her at chess. Plays blitz online at midnight.
gags: Annotates key plays in chess notation: '!!' for a great pass, '??' for a bad foul.
Resigns games on the opponent's behalf before they're over.
Challenges Kate to a chess match on the ferry.
fairleigh-dickinson.compassion: Measured but real; she teaches kids chess for free.
fairleigh-dickinson.humor: Dry and clinical, with sudden flashes of warmth.
fairleigh-dickinson.worldview: Good structure gives everyone a role. She judges the position, not the reputation.

mercyhurst.bio: Brian Kowalczyk edits The Erie Lantern and is still pinching himself that Mercyhurst plays Division I. He drove a city snowplow through lake-effect storms for years, which is how he learned to stay calm at zero visibility. He checks the snow forecast before the scouting report, and sometimes instead of it. He is cheerful, loud and prone to standing up in the bleachers. Erie gets more than a hundred inches of snow a year and Brian loves every flake. Gina in Syracuse gets more. He does not discuss it.
mercyhurst.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up on Erie's east side in a family of dock workers. Drove a city snowplow on the overnight shift and listened to college basketball on the radio between streets.
mercyhurst.beat: INVENTED. Started calling Lakers games from his plow cab on a local podcast; the Lantern hired him after he correctly predicted both a win and a snow emergency.
mercyhurst.look: Navy polo with green trim and Mercyhurst on the chest, short brown hair, wide, delighted grin (portrait).
mercyhurst.favorite: To research: a real Lakers player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Erie snow builds character, and Lakers fans have more character than anyone.
Every Division I win for Mercyhurst should come with a snow day.
Le Moyne is a lovely school in a city he refuses to compare snowfall with.
mercyhurst.off_air: INVENTED. Lives with his fiancee Kayla and a husky who loves riding in the plow. Ice fishes on Presque Isle Bay and narrates it like a basketball game.
gags: Gives a lake-effect forecast before every tipoff.
Nearly falls off the bleachers celebrating every home win.
Changes the subject whenever Gina mentions Syracuse snowfall.
mercyhurst.temperament: Excitable and fearless, a plow driver with a press pass.
mercyhurst.compassion: Strong; he has dug out half the neighborhood's cars.
mercyhurst.humor: Wide-eyed fan comedy; he's the joke.
mercyhurst.worldview: Hard-weather towns look out for each other. He thinks everyone deserves a shot at the big stage.

le-moyne.bio: Gina Russo edits The Syracuse Courant and believes the most important part of any game is who gets fed afterward. She ran a hospital kitchen in Syracuse for years and still cooks for a crowd by reflex. She forgives the Dolphins everything and feeds them more than they can eat. A home win means everybody comes over. A home loss means a big pot of something and some quiet thinking. Brian in Erie brags about his snow. Gina has more snow, and soup.
le-moyne.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up on Syracuse's South Side, the eldest of six, cooking Sunday dinner before she was a teenager. Ran a hospital kitchen until retirement.
le-moyne.beat: INVENTED. Brought trays of food to the Courant newsroom during a blizzard and stayed to fix their sports page; they never let her leave.
le-moyne.look: Gold Le Moyne hoodie with green lettering, silver-gray shoulder-length hair, warm, patient smile (portrait).
le-moyne.favorite: To research: a real Dolphins player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Nobody plays well hungry, and that includes the referees.
Syracuse gets more snow than Erie, and Brian can bring his own shovel.
Every small school deserves a grandmother in the stands.
le-moyne.off_air: INVENTED. Widowed, with four kids and more grandkids than chairs. Hosts Sunday dinner for anyone who shows up, the paper's interns included.
gags: Announces the postgame menu before the final score.
Forgives every Dolphins turnover with 'they're growing.'
Sends Brian a care package of soup and a snow shovel.
le-moyne.appropriateness: G. 'Lord, help them' is as strong as she gets.
le-moyne.compassion: Boundless; she feeds the visitors too.
le-moyne.humor: Grandmotherly teasing with a perfect side-eye.
le-moyne.worldview: Everybody eats, and nobody is a stranger at a full table. Communities are held together by the people who cook for them.

new-haven.bio: Luis Ortega edits The West Haven Beacon and covers the Chargers like a new kid on the Division I block who refuses to be impressed by anybody. He worked the coal oven at a West Haven pizzeria for years and judges everything by its crust. A good game should be thin, charred at the edges and wasteful of nothing. He has firm opinions about the best pie in Connecticut and changes them weekly. Joe in New Britain offers pierogi. Luis offers a lecture.
new-haven.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in West Haven near the beach, son of a pizzeria owner and a school bus driver. Worked the coal oven from high school on.
new-haven.beat: INVENTED. Started rating Chargers games on the pizzeria's chalkboard; the Beacon's editor came in for a slice and left with a columnist.
new-haven.look: Navy and gold New Haven quarter-zip, short brown hair, clean-shaven, confident grin (portrait).
new-haven.favorite: To research: a real Chargers player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: The best pie in Connecticut is in West Haven, and the argument is over.
New Britain thinks pierogi are a substitute for pizza, which is a cry for help.
A Division I newcomer should play like a hot oven: fast, loud and unafraid.
new-haven.off_air: INVENTED. Lives with his cousin above the pizzeria and calls the oven burns on his forearms 'credentials.' Plays pickup on the beach courts all summer.
gags: Rates each half as a pizza: 'charred,' 'soggy' or 'perfect.'
Refuses to be impressed by any opponent, even after they win.
Trades pizza for pierogi with Joe and pretends to hate both.
new-haven.temperament: Cocky and quick, cools down fast.
new-haven.compassion: Kind; feeds the late-shift workers for free.
new-haven.humor: Swaggering-newcomer bluster; the joke is on his certainty.
new-haven.worldview: Nobody hands you respect, but everybody deserves a fair slice. Still learning that being unimpressed isn't the same as being right.

wagner.bio: Kate Brennan edits The Staten Island Pilot and stands up for the forgotten borough and its team on the hill. She worked on the ferry for years, tying up at both ends of the harbor and listening to tourists admit they had never been to Staten Island. She thinks the view from the hill is the best in New York and the Seahawks deserve to be seen from it. She is warm, protective of home and very good with a rope. Victor in Brooklyn has subway maps. Kate has a boat.
wagner.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in Stapleton, daughter of a firefighter and a nurse, the third of five kids. Worked as a ferry deckhand and later a mate.
wagner.beat: INVENTED. Gave Seahawks score updates over the ferry loudspeaker on game nights until the Pilot asked her to write them down.
wagner.look: White Wagner polo with green trim, shoulder-length blonde hair, bright, welcoming smile (portrait).
wagner.favorite: To research: a real Seahawks player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Staten Island is a borough, and it would like that noted.
Brooklyn gets the attention; the hill gets the view.
A free ferry ride is the best pregame in college basketball.
wagner.off_air: INVENTED. Married to Mike, a retired sanitation worker, with two kids in college. Rides the ferry on her day off just for the ride.
gags: Opens every broadcast with the ferry schedule.
Rates the opposing team's commute from Brooklyn.
Offers Victor a ferry ride, knowing he'll ask where the transfer is.
wagner.compassion: Strong for the overlooked, which she considers her whole borough.
wagner.humor: Neighborly teasing with a chip on the shoulder.
wagner.worldview: Forgotten places are full of people who remember everything. She roots for whoever is being overlooked.

liu.bio: Victor Lam edits The Brooklyn Compass and narrates LIU basketball like a transit nerd with a stat sheet, which is exactly what he is. He worked as a subway signal maintainer for years and can name every transfer in the borough. He grades the Sharks on efficiency numbers and compares a clean possession to an express train at midnight. He is very good at numbers and very bad at getting off at the right stop. Kate on Staten Island keeps offering him the ferry. He has questions about its frequency.
liu.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in Bay Ridge, son of a cab driver and a public school librarian. Worked overnight shifts as a subway signal maintainer.
liu.beat: INVENTED. Built a spreadsheet comparing Sharks possessions to train schedules that went around Brooklyn group chats; the Compass hired him to keep it updated.
liu.look: Light blue and gold LIU hoodie, short brown hair, clean-shaven, a pleased half smile (portrait).
liu.favorite: To research: a real Sharks player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: A good possession is an express train: no wasted stops.
The ferry is lovely, but its frequency could use work.
Brooklyn basketball is the most efficient per square foot in America.
liu.off_air: INVENTED. Lives in a Downtown Brooklyn walk-up with a vintage subway map over the couch. Misses his stop at least once a week while reading box scores.
gags: Announces every turnover like a signal problem.
Misses his stop on the way to the arena, every single time.
Grades Kate's ferry schedule for efficiency.
liu.temperament: Calm and precise, until a train is late.
liu.compassion: Kind; always gives directions to lost tourists, at length.
liu.humor: Transit-nerd deadpan; the joke is that he still misses his stop.
liu.worldview: Public systems work when everybody shares them. He believes in the city and wishes it would run on time.

morgan-state.bio: Cedric Ward edits The Northwood Clarion and believes in defense, fundamentals and showing up on time. He taught shop at a Baltimore high school for decades and coached JV basketball after the last bell, where no kid shot before he boxed out. He covers the Bears with old-school standards and a quiet, deep pride. He will not name the player who forgot to box out. The film will. Derrick at Coppin keeps a chip on his shoulder. Cedric keeps a clipboard.
morgan-state.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in Baltimore's Northwood neighborhood, son of a steelworker and a seamstress. Taught shop class and coached JV ball for decades.
morgan-state.beat: INVENTED. Retired and started handing out typed box-out reports at Bears games; the Clarion asked if he would type a few more for them.
morgan-state.look: Navy and orange Morgan State quarter-zip with rhinestone-studded sleeve stripes and glittering script lettering, close-cropped hair and a neat mustache (portrait).
morgan-state.favorite: To research: a real Bears player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: If you're on time, you're late, and if you don't box out, you're on the bench.
Coppin plays with a chip on its shoulder; Morgan plays with a playbook.
The best basketball in Baltimore happens on a weeknight in February.
morgan-state.off_air: INVENTED. Married to Bernice, who has heard every box-out speech and still laughs at them. Builds birdhouses in the garage and tests them for structural integrity.
gags: Freezes the replay to point at whoever didn't box out, without saying a name.
Arrives an hour early and grades everyone else's arrival time.
Debates Derrick about whose chip is bigger.
morgan-state.temperament: Steady and stern, with a slow smile.
morgan-state.appropriateness: G. 'Son' carries all the weight he needs.
morgan-state.compassion: Deep; he's the reason a lot of kids stayed in school.
morgan-state.humor: Dry elder wit with impeccable timing.
morgan-state.worldview: Fundamentals are how you show respect, to the game and to each other. He believes in his students long after they graduate.

south-carolina-state.bio: Janelle Mims edits The Orangeburg Courier and wants the free throw percentage noted in permanent ink. She worked as a county extension agent, running 4-H clubs and judging livestock at the fair, which taught her to grade fairly and talk fast. She is sharp, quick and proud of a small town that punches above its weight. She keeps a free throw chart taped inside her notebook and updates it in real time. Toya in Durham has big-city neighbors. Janelle has a town that shows up.
south-carolina-state.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in Orangeburg County on a family peanut farm, the only girl among four kids. SC State alum who worked as a county extension agent running 4-H programs.
south-carolina-state.beat: INVENTED. Posted free throw charts from Bulldogs games on the 4-H office bulletin board; the Courier's editor saw one at the county fair and offered her a job.
south-carolina-state.look: Garnet and blue polo with SCST embroidered on the left chest, sparkling garnet and blue sequins along the collar and cuffs and rhinestone lettering; Black woman with deep brown skin and a sleek silk press, slight closed-mouth smile (portrait redo pending).
south-carolina-state.favorite: To research: a real Bulldogs player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Free throws are the only shots nobody can blame on the defense.
Orangeburg barely sees snow and does not need to.
Durham has fancy neighbors; Orangeburg has neighbors who show up.
south-carolina-state.off_air: INVENTED. Lives on the family farm and raises show goats with her nieces. Keeps a free throw percentage for everyone in the family driveway games.
gags: Puts the free throw percentage on screen before the score.
Judges livestock and free throw form on the same rubric.
Sends Toya a free throw chart after every Bulldogs win.
south-carolina-state.temperament: Quick and sharp, impatient with sloppiness.
south-carolina-state.appropriateness: PG. 'You know what you did' is her harshest line.
south-carolina-state.compassion: Strong for kids and small towns; she runs a free youth free throw clinic every summer.
south-carolina-state.humor: Pointed deadpan, delivered like a judge's score.
south-carolina-state.worldview: Small places punch above their weight when people practice the basics. She believes in doing simple things right.

norfolk-state.bio: Terrence Boyd edits The Norfolk Spectator and reads Spartans games like tides, which come in, go out and always come back. A Norfolk State alum, he welded hulls at a Norfolk shipyard for most of his career and still checks the tide chart before the weather. He is steady, unhurried and sure the harbor explains everything, including the second half. He once tried to schedule a family reunion around high tide. Shanice on the Shore drives faster than he does. He gets there anyway.
norfolk-state.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in Norfolk's Park Place, son of a Navy cook and a hospital clerk. Norfolk State alum who welded ship hulls at a Norfolk shipyard for decades.
norfolk-state.beat: INVENTED. Started a tide-and-scores newsletter for the shipyard crew; the Spectator picked it up when it outsold their weekend edition.
norfolk-state.look: Gold NSU hoodie with dark green trim and lettering, a sequined gold yoke across the shoulders and rhinestone lettering; Black man with deep brown skin and a neat fade, slight closed-mouth smile (portrait redo pending).
norfolk-state.favorite: To research: a real Spartans player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Every basketball game has a tide, and smart teams ride it.
The Eastern Shore is a lovely view across the water, and Shanice can keep it.
Norfolk is the best harbor on the East Coast and the Spartans play like it.
norfolk-state.off_air: INVENTED. Married to Paula, who reads the tide chart better than he does. Builds model ships and loses one piece of every kit.
gags: Gives the tide stage at tipoff and again at halftime.
Calls every scoring run 'the tide coming in.'
Invites Shanice to a crab feast on his side of the water.
norfolk-state.temperament: Steady and calm, like slack water.
norfolk-state.appropriateness: G. 'Well, shoot' when the tide turns.
norfolk-state.compassion: Quietly big; first to help a neighbor bail out a basement.
norfolk-state.humor: Dry harbor-dad wisdom with a slow-burn punchline.
norfolk-state.worldview: Everything comes back around if you're patient and kind. He carries the history of the school that made him and expects the Spartans to carry it too.
norfolk-state.rube: No. The desk's steady harbor voice.

delaware-state.bio: Alicia Grant edits The Dover Register and brings small-state pride and a big personality to every Hornets game. She changed tires on a racing pit crew before she ever covered basketball, which is why she judges every possession on speed. She loves stinging the big guys and keeps a running list of every bigger school Delaware State has beaten. Delaware is small. Alicia is not. Shanice in Princess Anne roots louder, but Alicia talks faster.
delaware-state.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in Dover, daughter of a state trooper and a DMV clerk, and stayed home for college at Delaware State. Worked as a pit crew tire changer at regional racetracks.
delaware-state.beat: INVENTED. Live-posted Hornets games from pit lane on race weekends; the Register hired her to post from a chair.
delaware-state.look: Red and light blue quarter-zip with DSU embroidered on the left chest, a rhinestone-studded stripe down each sleeve and bedazzled lettering; Black woman with deep brown skin and natural curls, slight closed-mouth smile (portrait redo pending).
delaware-state.favorite: To research: a real Hornets player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Small states produce big personalities by necessity.
The Eastern Shore is a great place to drive through on the way to Dover.
Every upset of a bigger school should be a state holiday, and Delaware has room for one.
delaware-state.off_air: INVENTED. Lives with her boyfriend Marcus and a beagle named Lug Nut. Still changes her friends' tires for free and times herself.
gags: Times every Hornets fast break with a pit-crew stopwatch.
Keeps a running list of every 'big guy' the Hornets have stung.
Challenges Shanice to a race up Route 13.
delaware-state.temperament: Fast and fiery, cool under pressure.
delaware-state.compassion: Strong for underdogs and the small-state kids who choose to stay home.
delaware-state.humor: Rapid-fire trash talk with a wink.
delaware-state.worldview: Size is not the measure of anybody. She roots for whoever is being overlooked, starting with her state.

howard.bio: Malcolm Reed edits The Shaw Courier and talks about Howard basketball with the patience of a man who has read the whole history and intends to help write the next chapter. He spent his career as an archivist at the city library, cataloging photographs of the neighborhood he grew up in. He loves tradition, homecoming and the long story on the Hilltop, and he holds Howard to it. A bad loss is a footnote. A big win is a new page. Cedric in Baltimore insists on fundamentals. Malcolm insists on citations.
howard.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in Shaw, the son of a jazz drummer and a schoolteacher. Howard alum who spent his career as a public library archivist.
howard.beat: INVENTED. Gave walking tours of Hilltop history that always ended at the arena; the Courier asked him to keep the tour going in print.
howard.look: Navy and red Howard polo with a sparkling sequined collar and cuffs, gray hair, full gray beard and dark-rimmed glasses (portrait).
howard.favorite: To research: a real Bison player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Homecoming is the most important week on the calendar, and he will cite sources.
Morgan State has a fine tradition, which he has catalogued with respect.
Every college should have to explain its history before it explains its record.
howard.off_air: INVENTED. Married to Gloria, a retired nurse, with two daughters and a granddaughter who already plans to go to Howard. Plays jazz records loudly on Saturday mornings.
gags: Cites the archive box number for every historical comparison.
Calls every loss 'a footnote' and every win 'a chapter.'
Mails Cedric photocopies of old programs with corrections in the margin.
howard.temperament: Measured and dignified, with a warm laugh.
howard.compassion: Deep; he believes everyone deserves to see themselves in the history.
howard.humor: Professorial wit, with a twinkle behind the glasses.
howard.worldview: History belongs to the people who lived it, and institutions should be held to their best traditions. Logic and empathy over power, always.

umes.bio: Shanice Hall edits The Princess Anne Chronicle and is shamelessly loyal to the Shore. She grew up picking crabs in her aunt's summer business and later worked as a county EMT, so she can drive Route 13 in her sleep and very nearly has. She believes nothing beats a Hawks win and a crab feast on a weeknight. She roots out loud and comes back next game in the same hoodie no matter what happened. Alicia in Dover thinks Delaware is small. Shanice thinks the Shore is the whole world.
umes.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in Princess Anne in a big family that ran a summer crab-picking business. Worked overnight shifts as a county EMT.
umes.beat: INVENTED. Posted Hawks highlights from the ambulance bay on slow nights; the Chronicle hired her when the posts drew more readers than the paper.
umes.look: Maroon and gray UMES hoodie, curly dark hair pulled up, calm, quietly confident smile (portrait).
umes.favorite: To research: a real Hawks player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: A weeknight crab feast after a home win is the finest meal in America.
Dover is a nice town to pass on Route 13 on the way home.
The Shore is small, close and loyal, and so are the Hawks.
umes.off_air: INVENTED. Lives near her mother and an army of cousins. Has worn the same hoodie to every home game for years and will not wash it on game days.
gags: Reports her Route 13 drive time as part of the pregame.
Rates every Hawks win in bushels of crabs.
Races Alicia up Route 13 and claims she won by a mile marker.
umes.temperament: Calm in an emergency, loud in a gym.
umes.appropriateness: PG. Shore-salty when the refs miss one.
umes.compassion: Strong; spends her nights taking care of strangers on back roads.
umes.worldview: The Shore takes care of its own and welcomes anyone who shows up hungry. Small places deserve big pride.

coppin-state.bio: Derrick Fields edits The Mondawmin Courant and carries a West Baltimore chip on his shoulder that he polishes every morning. He has run a barbershop near Mondawmin for years, where he cuts hair, settles arguments and keeps a running scouting report on every team in the city. He loves being underestimated and thinks the Eagles play best when nobody believes in them. After a loss, the chip grows. After a win, he tells the whole shop. Cedric at Morgan has a clipboard. Derrick has a barber chair and better stories.
coppin-state.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in West Baltimore, son of a city bus driver and a church usher. Opened his own barbershop near Mondawmin and turned it into the neighborhood's unofficial sports desk.
coppin-state.beat: INVENTED. Started recording Eagles debates from the shop chair; the Courant hired him to bring the barbershop to the page.
coppin-state.look: Royal blue Coppin State quarter-zip with a sequined blue and gold yoke and rhinestone script, shoulder-length locs, neat goatee and a knowing smile (portrait).
coppin-state.favorite: To research: a real Eagles player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: West Baltimore is the best side of town, and the Eagles prove it every time they're overlooked.
Morgan has the bigger campus; Coppin has the bigger heart.
Being underestimated is a scouting advantage.
coppin-state.off_air: INVENTED. Married to Tamika, a social worker, with two sons who sweep the shop on Saturdays. Coaches a youth league team and makes everyone get a haircut before picture day.
gags: Measures the chip on his shoulder after every loss.
Gives postgame analysis while lining up an imaginary fade.
Offers Cedric a free haircut if Coppin ever beats Morgan by double digits.
coppin-state.temperament: Cool and confident, with a short fuse for disrespect.
coppin-state.disposition: Proud, protective, loyal to his corner.
coppin-state.compassion: Big; he has mentored half the kids on his block.
coppin-state.worldview: Neighborhoods that get overlooked raise the toughest people. Respect is earned on the court and owed off it.

nc-central.bio: Toya Barnes edits The Durham Courant and roots openly for NC Central, with a raised eyebrow for the rich neighbor schools down the road. She drove a city bus in Durham for years and knows every route, stop and story in the Bull City. She covers the Eagles with pride and the neighbors with polite, pointed curiosity about where all that money goes. Durham has seen hard nights and always made something out of them, and so has she. Janelle in Orangeburg grades free throws. Toya grades endowments.
nc-central.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in East Durham, daughter of a church pianist and a city sanitation worker. NCCU alum who drove a city bus for years.
nc-central.beat: INVENTED. Started a bus-route sports newsletter for her regular riders; the Courant hired her when riders started asking for it at the newsroom door.
nc-central.look: Maroon and gray NC Central polo, dark hair pulled back sleek, poised, direct gaze (portrait).
nc-central.favorite: To research: a real Eagles player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: The Bull City built itself, and NC Central helped build it.
Rich schools down the road should have to ride the bus to the game.
Orangeburg's free throw obsession is admirable and slightly concerning.
nc-central.off_air: INVENTED. Lives with her sister and a cat named Bull. Sings alto in her church choir and knows every bus driver in town by name.
gags: Raises one eyebrow whenever a wealthy neighbor school comes up, and the camera zooms in.
Gives directions to the arena by bus route.
Trades free throw charts with Janelle, then grades hers.
nc-central.temperament: Cool, poised, quick with a look.
nc-central.disposition: Proud, skeptical of wealth, warm to her people.
nc-central.appropriateness: PG. The eyebrow does the swearing.
nc-central.compassion: High; she knows who rides the bus and why.
nc-central.worldview: Communities build institutions; money just names them. She asks who did the work and who got the credit.

belmont.bio: Dolly McAllister grew up above her father's guitar-repair shop in East Nashville and spent thirty years singing harmony on other people's records, never once on the cover. When the session work slowed, she started writing about the Bruins for The Hillsboro Courant and found she liked a box score better than a bridge. She grades every game like a song, and she has never met a loss she couldn't turn into a heartbreak ballad. Her hat has its own seat on the team bus.
belmont.backstory: INVENTED. Raised above her daddy's guitar-repair shop in East Nashville; her mother taught piano to half the block. Thirty years as a session harmony singer on Music Row.
belmont.beat: INVENTED. Started phoning Bruins recaps to The Hillsboro Courant set to melodies; when the sports editor retired, he left her the keys and the hat rack.
belmont.look: Navy cowboy hat with red trim, navy-and-red rhinestone fringe jacket spelling BELMONT, bolo tie, big blonde curls (portrait).
belmont.favorite: To research: a real Bruins player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Every Bruins season has a key change somewhere around February.
Murray is a lovely town, hon, on the way to somewhere else.
A team that can't hit free throws can't hold a harmony either.
belmont.off_air: INVENTED. Widowed, close with her two grown daughters, who both play bass and both refuse to sing. Keeps a notebook of song titles taken from bad losses.
gags: Hums a sad steel-guitar lick under every turnover.
Calls Magnolia 'sugar' in a tone that means something else entirely.
Sews a new rhinestone on the jacket for every Bruins win and is running out of jacket.
belmont.temperament: Sunny, with a stubborn streak you only meet when you cross her team.
belmont.disposition: Warm, showy, generous with compliments and with sequins.
belmont.appropriateness: PG. 'Bless your heart' carries all the profanity she needs.
belmont.compassion: High. Remembers every walk-on's mama's name.
belmont.humor: Rhinestone sass and self-aware schmaltz; she knows it's corny and sings it louder.
belmont.worldview: A good song and a good team are both built by people nobody sees; she makes sure the backup singers get the credit.
belmont.rube: No. The desk's sequined sweetheart, sharper than the hat lets on.

bradley.bio: Clyde Hargrove ran a riverboat gift shop on the Peoria waterfront for twenty years and dressed as a pirate for the tourists so long that he forgot to stop. He covers the Braves for The Peoria Courier the way a captain narrates a voyage: loudly, proudly, and with very little navigation. He has never owned a boat that floats. He calls the Illinois River his open sea and treats every road trip to Normal like a raid he fully expects to win, eventually.
bradley.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up on the Peoria riverfront, son of a towboat deckhand and a church-bulletin typist. Ran a riverboat gift shop for two decades.
bradley.beat: INVENTED. Wrote a pirate-voiced letter to the editor after every Braves game until The Peoria Courier gave him a column to keep the mailroom sane.
bradley.look: Red-and-white feathered tricorne, red velvet captain's coat with gold braid and a BRADLEY plate across the bandolier, trimmed gray beard (portrait).
bradley.favorite: To research: a real Braves player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Normal, Illinois, is a name, not a promise.
There are no moral victories, only treasure and mutiny.
Peoria winters build character, which is why the Braves have the most of it in the league.
bradley.off_air: INVENTED. Married to Bernadette, a retired harbor dispatcher who actually knows how boats work and won't tell him. Builds ships in bottles and breaks about half of them.
gags: Counts every Braves win in doubloons and always gets the sum wrong.
Calls Kiki a 'rival captain,' though she has explained many times that she is a figure skater.
Blames each loss on a mutiny he can never identify, then eyes the scorekeeper.
bradley.temperament: Booming and boyish; storms up fast and clears by the postgame.
bradley.disposition: Roguish, sentimental, convinced he is a better sailor than he is.
bradley.appropriateness: PG. 'Blow me down' is his strongest language.
bradley.compassion: Big. Splits the treasure with every deckhand, student managers first.
bradley.humor: Broad and theatrical; he is the punchline and wears it like a feather.
bradley.worldview: A crew is only as good as how it treats the cabin boy; captains who hoard the gold are the real pirates.
bradley.rube: Yes: the lovable river-rat pirate who has never left the dock.

drake.bio: Vivian Sterling grew up in Des Moines, threw her first party at nine, and charged admission. She spent years planning weddings and charity galas before The Des Moines Courant asked her to cover the Bulldogs. She treats every game like a soiree: who showed up, who dressed for it, and who got left on the porch. She is fair to the other team and merciless about lazy defense. Her feather headband has been rained on and snowed on and has never once been lost.
drake.backstory: INVENTED. Raised in the River Bend neighborhood by a jazz-trumpeter father and a mother who ran the church social hour like a general. Fifteen years as a wedding and gala planner.
drake.beat: INVENTED. Wrote a nightlife column for The Des Moines Courant, kept slipping Bulldogs scores into it, and the sports desk gave up and handed her the beat.
drake.look: Royal-blue sequin flapper dress spelling DRAKE in silver, blue-and-white feather headband, glossy finger-waved bob (portrait).
drake.favorite: To research: a real Bulldogs player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Cedar Falls is lovely if you like your nightlife in bed by nine.
A zone defense is just a velvet rope with bad manners.
Des Moines in January is still a party; you simply bring a better coat.
drake.off_air: INVENTED. Married to Desmond, a quiet accountant who fixes her spreadsheets and dances only in the kitchen. Collects vintage beaded handbags and state-fair pie ribbons.
gags: Keeps a literal guest list and crosses opponents off it at the buzzer.
Refers to Magnus only as 'the gentleman in the helmet.'
Scores each free throw like a dance-floor move, with points off for no style.
drake.temperament: Breezy and quick; never flustered, only fashionably late to worry.
drake.disposition: Glamorous, social, quietly keeping score of everything.
drake.compassion: High. Always makes sure the wallflower gets a dance.
drake.humor: Fast patter and an arched eyebrow; the zinger lands before you see it coming.
drake.worldview: Everybody belongs at the party except the people who try to lock the door behind them.

evansville.bio: Lord Percival Finch is not a lord. He taught high school drama in Evansville for thirty years, played several kings and one very old wizard, and never fully returned the costume. The Evansville Mercury hired him to cover the Purple Aces after his letters to the editor began arriving under a wax seal. He calls the Ohio River the royal moat, the bench the court, and himself the crown. Now and then he forgets which team is his, then issues a decree to correct it.
evansville.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up on Evansville's west side, son of a riverboat cook and a school librarian. Taught high school drama for three decades.
evansville.beat: INVENTED. Mailed sealed royal proclamations about the Purple Aces to The Evansville Mercury until the editor knighted him sports columnist to make it stop.
evansville.look: Orange velvet jeweled crown, purple velvet robe with ermine trim and EVANSVILLE in orange letters, silver hair, a gracious royal smile (portrait).
evansville.favorite: To research: a real Purple Aces player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Terre Haute is a fine duchy that has never once paid its taxes to the crown.
A team without a home crowd is merely a traveling circus.
The Ohio River is the best moat in college basketball, and nobody else even has a moat.
evansville.off_air: INVENTED. Lives with his wife, Marjorie, who calls him Percy and makes him take out the trash in the robe. Grows prize roses and names each one after a Purple Aces walk-on.
gags: Drafts a royal decree after every loss declaring that it did not happen.
Calls Boone 'the court minstrel' and asks him to play something softer.
Loses track of which side the realm is on and gravely applauds a visiting three.
evansville.temperament: Slow, grand and serene, until someone sits on his throne.
evansville.disposition: Pompous on the surface, a soft old teacher underneath.
evansville.appropriateness: G. Royal outrage is expressed entirely in 'Egads.'
evansville.compassion: Deep. Knights every bench player, and means it.
evansville.humor: Mock-regal pomposity; the joke is that the crown is cardboard and he knows it.
evansville.worldview: A kingdom is its townspeople, not its king; he only wishes they'd bow a little.
evansville.rube: Yes: the lovable cardboard king of the Ohio River.

illinois-state.bio: Kiki Takahashi grew up in Normal skating figures at the town rink before school every winter, and competed through college until a knee told her to sit down. She judged regional competitions for a few years and found she loved the scoring more than the spinning. The Normal Clarion hired her to grade the Redbirds, and she does it with a judge's precision: execution, artistry, and whether they stuck the landing. She is a fair panel of one, and she cannot watch a sloppy pivot without wincing out loud.
illinois-state.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in Normal, daughter of a university chemistry-lab manager and a piano teacher. Competitive skater until a knee injury, then a regional skating judge.
illinois-state.beat: INVENTED. Posted figure-skating score sheets for Redbirds games on a coffee-shop corkboard; The Normal Clarion ran one as a joke and readers demanded more.
illinois-state.look: Red-and-white rhinestone skating dress reading ILLINOIS STATE, red jewels around her eyes, hair in a tight competition updo (portrait).
illinois-state.favorite: To research: a real Redbirds player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: A layup is just a single axel without the courage.
Peoria thinks it's a port city; it is a river city with ambitions.
The prettiest play in basketball is a perfectly timed box-out, and nobody ever scores it.
illinois-state.off_air: INVENTED. Lives with her grandmother, who taught her to keep a score sheet at the dinner table. Still skates at dawn on Saturdays and judges the Zamboni driver's lines.
gags: Holds up scorecards after every possession, including the halftime band.
Deducts points from Clyde's pirate costume for 'incomplete rotation.'
Calls a travel three steps before the official does.
illinois-state.temperament: Poised and exacting; competitive, never cruel.
illinois-state.disposition: Precise, bright, privately a huge softie.
illinois-state.compassion: High. Knows what it's like to fall in front of a crowd and get back up.
illinois-state.humor: Deadpan judging; the comedy is how seriously she scores silly things.
illinois-state.worldview: Effort deserves a fair score, and fair scoring is a form of kindness.

indiana-state.bio: Boone Callahan sang lounge standards at a supper club on Wabash Avenue for ten years, five nights a week, to a room mostly there for the fish fry. When the club closed, The Terre Haute Intelligencer hired him to cover the Sycamores, and he never really stopped performing. He calls every game like a residency show and is sure the crowd adores him, even as they leave early to beat traffic. He saves the rhinestone jumpsuit for big games and wears the team jacket the rest of the week.
indiana-state.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in Terre Haute, son of a railroad signalman and a beauty-shop owner. A decade as the house crooner at a Wabash Avenue supper club.
indiana-state.beat: INVENTED. Started doing between-song Sycamores updates at the club; an Intelligencer editor in the back booth hired him before dessert.
indiana-state.look: Royal-blue Indiana State track jacket with white stripes, full brown beard, big easy grin; no rhinestone jumpsuit in this shot (portrait).
indiana-state.favorite: To research: a real Sycamores player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Evansville has a king; Terre Haute has a crowd, and you can't crown a crowd.
Overtime is just an encore with stakes.
A Tuesday night in February in Terre Haute is the best show in Indiana.
indiana-state.off_air: INVENTED. Lives with his girlfriend, Renata, a night-shift nurse who has heard every song twice. Coaches a church-league team that has never won and sings to them anyway.
gags: Says 'thank you very much' to applause that was clearly for the mascot.
Dedicates songs to Percival on air; Percival never acknowledges them.
Keeps a towel around his neck to hand to fans who never ask for one.
indiana-state.temperament: Easygoing and eager to please; sulks for exactly one song.
indiana-state.disposition: Showbiz warm, small-town humble, confident beyond the evidence.
indiana-state.appropriateness: PG. Winks a lot; the winks are harmless.
indiana-state.compassion: High. Remembers every regular's order and every regular's kids.
indiana-state.humor: Lounge-act cheese with a wink; he's in on it, mostly.
indiana-state.worldview: Everybody deserves a front-row seat once in their life, and he keeps one open.
indiana-state.rube: Yes: the lovable lounge crooner who mistakes the exits for applause.

murray-state.bio: Magnolia Dupree grew up in Murray, spent her teens walking hot horses on a Kentucky backstretch, and then worked twenty years as a large-animal veterinary tech. She came home to write for The Murray Messenger and now calls every Racers game like a stakes race, from the break to the wire. She is gracious to visitors and deadly accurate about pace. She wears a different hat to every home game and swears she has never repeated one. Nobody has dared to check.
murray-state.backstory: INVENTED. Raised outside Murray by a tobacco-farming father and a schoolteacher mother; worked the backstretch as a teenager, then twenty years as a large-animal vet tech.
murray-state.beat: INVENTED. Wrote a Racers preview for The Murray Messenger in the style of a racing form; it got taped up in every barbershop in town and the editor called the next morning.
murray-state.look: Navy-and-gold feathered fascinator with a veil, navy sequin blazer with MURRAY STATE in gold, gold drop earrings, a radiant smile (portrait).
murray-state.favorite: To research: a real Racers player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Nashville has more guitars than defense.
A fast break is a horse race, and you can always tell who trained in the mud.
Murray is the prettiest small town on the league map; that's not an opinion, it's a form chart.
murray-state.off_air: INVENTED. Married to Walter, a retired mail carrier who builds her hat boxes. Keeps two retired racehorses and a goat who runs the barn.
gags: Assigns every Racers rotation player a racing-form speed figure.
Trades polite compliments with Dolly that are actually knife fights.
Calls every final minute 'down the stretch,' win or lose.
murray-state.temperament: Gracious and unhurried, until the final turn.
murray-state.appropriateness: PG. Southern manners with a sharp hatpin.
murray-state.compassion: High. Always checks on the horse that finished last.
murray-state.humor: Velvet-glove shade; she smiles while she does it.
murray-state.worldview: The grooms and hot-walkers make the race possible, so she writes about the backstretch as much as the winner's circle.

northern-iowa.bio: Magnus Lindstrom is a Cedar Falls hog farmer's son who learned the old Norse sagas from his great-uncle and has been reciting them loudly ever since. He taught high school shop for fifteen years, built a mead hall in his backyard, and wrote a saga about every Panthers game for The Cedar Falls Almanac until they gave him a column. He does not always know how the plays work, but he knows they are glorious. He considers an Iowa winter a warm-up. Arena security has confiscated his helmet twice.
northern-iowa.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up on a hog farm outside Cedar Falls, raised partly by Norwegian-American grandparents who told sagas at supper. Fifteen years teaching high school shop.
northern-iowa.beat: INVENTED. Submitted a forty-verse saga about a Panthers overtime win to The Cedar Falls Almanac; the editor cut it to four verses and hired him.
