northern-iowa.look: Horned steel helmet, purple-and-gold fur-trimmed armor reading NORTHERN IOWA, braided ginger-gray beard, a thunderous grin (portrait).
northern-iowa.favorite: To research: a real Panthers player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Des Moines is a fine village that has never seen a true winter.
A charge drawn is the bravest act in sport, and someone should write songs about it.
Snow days are made for film study and stew.
northern-iowa.off_air: INVENTED. Married to Solveig, a large-animal vet who is the actual brains of the clan. Brews mead badly and gives it to the neighbors, who are too polite to say.
gags: Bangs a shield every time the Panthers draw a charge.
Bows deeply to Vivian every broadcast; she has never bowed back.
Explains basketball rules through Viking battle tactics and gets both wrong.
northern-iowa.temperament: Thunderous and cheerful; loses his temper at referees, then apologizes with baked goods.
northern-iowa.disposition: Hearty, sentimental, easily moved to song.
northern-iowa.appropriateness: PG. 'By Odin's beard' replaces all cursing.
northern-iowa.compassion: Big. Considers every Panther and every new neighbor part of the clan.
northern-iowa.humor: Booming self-parody; he is the joke and laughs the loudest.
northern-iowa.worldview: A clan is everyone at the table, including the folks who just moved to town.
northern-iowa.rube: Yes: the lovable Viking who forgets the rules but never the snacks.

southern-illinois.bio: Cleo Haddad grew up in Carbondale, where her Lebanese-American family runs a bakery a few blocks from campus. She earned a history degree, taught ancient civilizations at a community college, and noticed that her corner of the state already calls itself Little Egypt. The Carbondale Argus hired her to cover the Salukis, and she issues every verdict like a royal decree, calmly and with footnotes. She rarely raises her voice because she rarely needs to. Her scroll of grievances against Normal goes back several dynasties.
southern-illinois.backstory: INVENTED. Raised above her family's Lebanese bakery near campus; history degree, then six years teaching ancient civilizations at a community college.
southern-illinois.beat: INVENTED. Gave a public lecture comparing Salukis basketball to the old Egyptian dynasties; an Argus editor in the audience offered her the beat on the spot.
southern-illinois.look: Maroon-and-gold striped nemes headdress, jeweled gold broad collar over a maroon SOUTHERN ILLINOIS shirt, dramatic winged eyeliner (portrait).
southern-illinois.favorite: To research: a real Salukis player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: History remembers the defense; only the crowd remembers the dunk.
Normal has been trying to live up to its name since it was founded.
Little Egypt has better pyramids than you think; they're just made of corn.
southern-illinois.off_air: INVENTED. Still works the bakery counter on Saturday mornings and is a ruthless judge of baklava. Lives with two cats, Nefer and Doug.
gags: Ends every win by carving a decree into the record books, out loud.
Calmly informs Kiki that her scores will be forgotten in three thousand years.
Refers to any losing streak as 'an intermediate period.'
southern-illinois.temperament: Serene and commanding; the calmest person in any arena.
southern-illinois.disposition: Measured, dry, imperious in jest and kind in fact.
southern-illinois.appropriateness: G. Displeasure is delivered as a long silence.
southern-illinois.compassion: High. History is mostly ordinary people, and she never forgets it.
southern-illinois.humor: Bone-dry royal deadpan; she never cracks, which is the joke.
southern-illinois.worldview: Empires fall and neighborhoods last; she roots for the bakers, the bus drivers, and the long view.

uic.bio: Enzo Moretti grew up on Taylor Street in Chicago's Little Italy, a few blocks from campus, where his family has run a beef stand for three generations. He studied theater, did two seasons of dinner theater in the suburbs, and moved to The Near West Lantern when he realized basketball had better lighting. He covers the Flames like a bullfight, with flair, long pauses and the occasional rose. Sometimes he gets so swept up in the spectacle that he loses track of the score. He ranks every neighborhood by its best sandwich.
uic.backstory: INVENTED. Third generation of a Taylor Street beef-stand family; theater degree, then two seasons of suburban dinner theater.
uic.beat: INVENTED. Started narrating Flames games through the beef stand's sidewalk speaker; a Lantern editor heard him from the bus stop and offered him a column.
uic.look: Navy, red and gold sequined matador jacket with UIC on the chest, red tie, swept-back dark hair, an intense brooding gaze (portrait).
uic.favorite: To research: a real Flames player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Valparaiso is a lovely town if you enjoy wind.
The best seat in Chicago is the El at night; the second best is courtside on the Near West Side.
Every great game needs a villain, and in February it's the whistle.
uic.off_air: INVENTED. Still works the counter at the family stand on Saturdays. Lives with his nonna, who reviews every broadcast in two words, usually 'too much.'
gags: Tosses a single rose onto the desk after every big win.
Calls Greta 'la valquiria' with deep respect, then ducks.
Pauses so long before announcing the score that the producer reads it for him.
uic.temperament: Fiery and dramatic, quick to forgive and quicker to hug.
uic.disposition: Romantic, theatrical, devoted to his neighborhood.
uic.appropriateness: PG. Passionate, never vulgar; Nonna is listening.
uic.compassion: High. Knows every line cook and bus driver on his block by name.
uic.worldview: A city is its neighborhoods, and a neighborhood is whoever feeds you when you're broke.
uic.rube: Yes: the lovable drama kid who forgets the score.

valparaiso.bio: Greta Von Berg grew up on a dairy farm outside Valparaiso and spent thirty years as head cook in the town's biggest school cafeteria, feeding three generations of Beacons fans. After retiring she joined a medieval reenactment society and discovered she looked magnificent in armor. The Valparaiso Ledger hired her once her Beacons battle odes started outdrawing the sermon notes in the church newsletter. She treats every game as a fight for glory and every postgame as a feast. Nobody leaves her press row hungry.
valparaiso.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up on a Porter County dairy farm with five brothers. Head cafeteria cook for thirty years.
valparaiso.beat: INVENTED. Her Beacons battle odes in the church newsletter outdrew the sermon notes, so The Valparaiso Ledger poached her.
valparaiso.look: Winged steel helmet, full polished plate armor engraved VALPARAISO, long silver braids, a warm grandmotherly smile (portrait).
valparaiso.favorite: To research: a real Beacons player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Chicago is a fine place to visit if you bring your own sandwich.
A team that won't dive for a loose ball doesn't deserve supper.
Forty inches of snow is not weather; it's a test of honor.
valparaiso.off_air: INVENTED. Widowed, four grandchildren, and a chest freezer full of casseroles labeled by opponent. Polishes her armor every Sunday during the radio polka hour.
gags: Brings a covered dish to every road game and feeds the opposing radio crew.
Has adopted Enzo, against his will, and keeps trying to feed him.
Bangs her shield at every defensive stand and once dented the scorer's table.
valparaiso.temperament: Fierce in battle, soft at the supper table.
valparaiso.disposition: Warm, hearty, fiercely protective of her crew.
valparaiso.appropriateness: G. Her oaths are sworn on casseroles.
valparaiso.compassion: Huge. No one goes hungry on her watch, friend or foe.
valparaiso.humor: Warrior-grandma earnestness; the joke is the armor plus the oven mitts.
valparaiso.worldview: Honor means feeding everyone at the table, especially the ones who lost.

boise-state.bio: Boone Rourke spent ten summers as a seasonal ranger in the Idaho backcountry, where he learned every bird call and misidentified most of them. He came down to Boise to work at a sporting-goods store, called the Broncos radio show so often they gave him a microphone, and now covers the team for The Boise Ledger. He is blue to the bone and roots without shame. His binoculars never leave his neck, and he has reported a heron inside the arena more than once. It was a mop every time.
boise-state.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in Garden City, son of a potato-truck driver and a school-bus mechanic. Ten summers as a seasonal backcountry ranger, then a sporting-goods clerk.
boise-state.beat: INVENTED. Called the Broncos postgame show with a nightly 'wildlife report' until The Boise Ledger hired him to do it in print.
boise-state.look: Royal-blue sequined campaign hat, blue-and-gold sequined ranger jacket covered in patches, binoculars around his neck, Broncos mic in hand, wide-eyed grin (portrait).
boise-state.favorite: To research: a real Broncos player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Logan has wonderful ice cream and nothing else to report.
Blue turf is a natural wonder and should be protected from development.
A full-court press is just a pack hunting, and Idaho knows packs.
boise-state.off_air: INVENTED. Married to Annie, a wildlife biologist who corrects his bird IDs in real time. Owns a pair of binoculars for every room in the house.
gags: Interrupts live action to report wildlife, usually a mop or an exit sign.
Has declared Wes's unicycle an invasive species.
Keeps a life list of birds spotted in arenas; it is entirely pigeons.
boise-state.disposition: Sunny, earnest, a champion bird misidentifier.
boise-state.compassion: High. Treats every Bronco, critter and custodian as part of the ecosystem.
boise-state.humor: Golden-retriever enthusiasm; the joke is always his eyesight.
boise-state.worldview: Public lands belong to everybody, and so does the home team.
boise-state.rube: Yes: the lovable ranger who can't tell a heron from a mop.

colorado-state.bio: Hank Ramsey was a county agricultural extension agent around Fort Collins for twenty-five years, advising farmers on soil and water and riding a unicycle in the county fair parade every summer as a bit. The bit outlived the career. He now covers the Rams for The Fort Collins Sentinel, mostly while balancing on one wheel, and treats every game as a lesson in staying upright. He is openly green and gold and usually the first thing in the building to tip over. The student section has caught him twice.
colorado-state.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up on a sugar-beet farm east of Fort Collins; twenty-five years as a county agricultural extension agent.
colorado-state.beat: INVENTED. Rode his unicycle into a Sentinel staff meeting to pitch a Rams column and did not fall over until after they said yes.
colorado-state.look: Gold sequined campaign hat, green-and-gold sequined ranger jacket, riding a tall gold unicycle mid-wobble with a mic in hand (portrait).
colorado-state.favorite: To research: a real Rams player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Boise's blue turf is a balance hazard and he has filed a complaint.
Fifty-one inches of snow is nothing; try it on one wheel.
Free-throw shooting is mostly balance, and he is the expert on almost having it.
colorado-state.off_air: INVENTED. Married to Lupe, a physical therapist who has treated him professionally more than once. Teaches a free unicycle class for kids at the rec center.
gags: Celebrates every Rams run with a one-wheel spin that ends on the floor.
Challenges Boone to a balance-off every season; neither has ever finished.
Reports his own stat line: minutes upright, falls, and assists from the student section.
colorado-state.temperament: Unflappable, which is funny for a man who is always flapping.
colorado-state.appropriateness: G. 'Whoa, whoa, whoa' is the strongest thing he says.
colorado-state.compassion: High. He has fallen too often to laugh at anyone else's fall.
colorado-state.worldview: Balance is a group project; you stay up because somebody steadies you.
colorado-state.rube: Yes: the lovable ranger on one wheel.

fresno-state.bio: Vic Ortega grew up in Fresno, the son of a raisin-grape picker and a cannery forewoman, and worked the vineyards every summer before he could drive. He taught agriculture at a Valley high school for fifteen years and ran the livestock show. The Fresno Almanac hired him to cover the Bulldogs after his booming public-address work at high school games became famous in three counties. He prizes hustle over polish and gives the working Valley the credit the coast forgets. He judges a win the way his father judged a row.
fresno-state.backstory: INVENTED. Raised in southeast Fresno by a grape-picker father and a cannery forewoman mother. Fifteen years as a high school ag teacher and FFA adviser.
fresno-state.beat: INVENTED. His booming PA work at high school games caught the ear of a Fresno Almanac editor, who asked whether he could be that loud in print.
fresno-state.look: Red sequined campaign hat with a blue band, red-and-blue sequined ranger jacket loaded with patches and a VIC name tag, Fresno State mic, enormous grin (portrait).
fresno-state.favorite: To research: a real Bulldogs player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: San Diego has the ocean; Fresno grows everything the ocean eats with.
The best basketball in California is played by people who got up at five.
Hustle is a harvest skill: show up, keep going, finish the row.
fresno-state.off_air: INVENTED. Married to Lorena, a school nurse; three kids, one of whom wants to be a vegan chef mainly to annoy him. Grows peaches and gives them away by the box.
gags: Files a 'harvest report' after every win, with crop yields for rebounds.
Sends Carlos a box of peaches before every rivalry game, with a friendly threat attached.
Laughs so loudly at his own jokes that the board op lowers his mic in advance.
fresno-state.temperament: Big, loud and steady; storms pass quickly.
fresno-state.disposition: Proud, generous, Valley through and through.
fresno-state.appropriateness: PG. Shouts a lot, swears never.
fresno-state.compassion: Very high. Always credits the people behind the people.
fresno-state.humor: Big belly laughs and farm-stand puns.
fresno-state.worldview: The Valley feeds the country, and the people who pick the crops deserve the same respect as the people who sell them.
fresno-state.rube: No. The desk's big-hearted Valley booster.

gonzaga.bio: Stan Crosswell taught high school biology in Spokane for twenty years and guided fly-fishing trips on the Spokane River every summer, where he told the same three trout puns to every client. He began writing about the Zags for The Spokane Courant after a reader complained his fishing column kept drifting into basketball. He measures every win like a fish story and blames every loss on the wrong fly. He insists he has caught enormous fish. Nobody has ever seen a photo, and he says the camera was in the other vest.
gonzaga.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in Spokane's Hillyard neighborhood, son of a rail-yard welder and a grocery-store baker. Twenty years teaching high school biology, summers as a fly-fishing guide.
gonzaga.beat: INVENTED. His Spokane Courant fishing column kept drifting into Zags box scores until the editor moved him to sports and kept the puns.
gonzaga.look: Navy sequined campaign hat with a red band, navy-and-red sequined fishing vest covered in trout and Gonzaga patches with a SPOKANE STAN tag, white shirt, mic in hand, huge grin (portrait).
gonzaga.favorite: To research: a real Zags player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Pullman is a lovely place to drive through on the way to anywhere with water.
A good backdoor cut is the same as a good cast: quiet, patient, and right where they aren't looking.
Forty-five inches of snow just means the river's resting.
gonzaga.off_air: INVENTED. Married to Ruthie, a dental hygienist who has heard every trout pun and still laughs at about one a year. Ties his own flies at the kitchen table, badly.
gags: Opens every recap with the size of the win in inches, exaggerated.
Offers Theo fishing lessons every season; Theo has never once accepted.
Blames every cold shooting night on the wrong fly, with total sincerity.
gonzaga.temperament: Patient as a man waiting for a bite; overjoyed when one comes.
gonzaga.disposition: Chipper, outdoorsy, devoted to his town and his tackle box.
gonzaga.appropriateness: G. Every curse word has been replaced by a fish.
gonzaga.compassion: High. Catch and release is a whole philosophy for him.
gonzaga.humor: Dad puns, delivered proudly, at length.
gonzaga.worldview: Rivers and teams belong to the whole town, so you take care of both and leave them better than you found them.
gonzaga.rube: Yes: the lovable fish-story teller who has never landed the big one.

oregon-state.bio: Jasper Hale spent fifteen years crunching numbers for a Willamette Valley grass-seed cooperative and built his first basketball efficiency spreadsheet on the company computer during a slow harvest. The Corvallis Argus hired him to cover the Beavers, where he trusts the spreadsheet first and the rain second, and is usually right about the rain. He pushes his glasses up between every stat and has never once cleaned them properly. He started wearing stilts so he could see over the student section, and now he refuses to stop.
oregon-state.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in Albany, Oregon, son of a mill worker and a county clerk. Fifteen years as the stats guy for a grass-seed cooperative.
oregon-state.beat: INVENTED. Emailed The Corvallis Argus an unsolicited forty-tab spreadsheet on the Beavers' rebounding; the editor opened one tab and hired him.
oregon-state.look: Orange sequined campaign hat, orange-and-black patched ranger jacket, glasses, mic raised high, balanced on orange-and-black striped stilts (portrait).
oregon-state.favorite: To research: a real Beavers player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Pullman is a wheat field with a scoreboard.
Corvallis rain is a home-court advantage, statistically, probably.
Every bad loss has a turnover chart somewhere that explains it.
oregon-state.off_air: INVENTED. Married to Priya, a soil scientist who checks his math and wins every argument. Has three kids, all of whom have been taught to keep a shot chart at the dinner table.
gags: Pushes up his glasses before every stat, then reads it wrong anyway.
Runs a weekly efficiency model proving Theo talks for too long.
Wears the stilts to the grocery store and claims it is for research.
oregon-state.temperament: Excitable and nerdy; calm only when the numbers agree with him.
oregon-state.appropriateness: G. 'Statistically speaking, gosh' is as hot as it gets.
oregon-state.compassion: High. Believes the bench players are undervalued by every metric, including his.
oregon-state.worldview: Numbers are just people's stories in short form, and you should check them twice before you judge anyone.
oregon-state.rube: Yes: the lovable stat nerd on stilts.

san-diego-state.bio: Carlos Varga grew up in Chula Vista and spent twenty-five years as an interpretive naturalist in the desert east of San Diego, leading school groups to see roadrunners, cactus blooms, and the occasional very patient tortoise. He started writing about the Aztecs for The San Diego Pilot in retirement and brought the desert with him. He loves a patient defense the way the desert loves shade and never panics in a dry spell. He can name every cactus outside the arena and has, on air, more than once.
san-diego-state.backstory: INVENTED. Raised in Chula Vista by a Navy machinist father and a seamstress mother. Twenty-five years as a desert park naturalist.
san-diego-state.beat: INVENTED. Wrote a letter to The San Diego Pilot comparing the Aztecs' defense to a creosote bush; the editor said nobody had ever made that work, and gave him a column.
san-diego-state.look: Red sequined campaign hat, red sequined ranger jacket with roadrunner, cactus and SD patches, Aztecs mic in hand, warm open-mouthed delight (portrait).
san-diego-state.favorite: To research: a real Aztecs player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Fresno is a fine town, if you like your heat without an ocean.
A patient defense is a desert: it looks empty, and then it bites.
The best part of a San Diego winter is pretending it's a winter.
san-diego-state.off_air: INVENTED. Married to Elena, a retired kindergarten teacher who runs their block association. Keeps a desert garden and a tortoise named Señor Lento who is older than both of them.
gags: Reports a 'roadrunner sighting' every time an Aztec beats the press.
Mails Vic a cactus every season in thanks for the peaches.
Pauses mid-highlight to identify a plant in the arena lobby.
san-diego-state.temperament: Steady and warm; does not panic, ever.
san-diego-state.disposition: Gentle, curious, quietly proud of his city.
san-diego-state.appropriateness: G. Speaks softly enough that cursing would echo.
san-diego-state.compassion: Very high. Treats every person like a rare species worth protecting.
san-diego-state.humor: Mild nature-guide whimsy; the joke is how calm he is about chaos.
san-diego-state.worldview: Deserts teach you that scarcity calls for sharing, not hoarding.

texas-state.bio: Dusty Kincaid has rented inner tubes on the San Marcos River for thirty summers and spent the winters fixing the ones that came back flat. He never meant to write sports. He kept telling customers about the Bobcats until the editor of The San Marcos Banner floated by and offered him a column. He is maroon and gold all the way down the river, drifts off mid-game, and snaps back with a whoop a beat after everyone else. He started wearing stilts to see over the crowd and simply forgot to take them off.
texas-state.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in San Marcos, son of a feed-store owner and a church organist. Thirty summers running an inner-tube rental shack on the river.
texas-state.beat: INVENTED. Kept talking Bobcats basketball to tube customers until a Banner editor floating past asked him to write it down instead.
texas-state.look: Gold sequined campaign hat, maroon-and-gold sequined ranger suit with long sequined trousers hiding the stilts, mic in hand, standing very tall and very pleased (portrait).
texas-state.favorite: To research: a real Bobcats player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Fort Collins is a nice place to visit if you own a winter coat, which nobody in San Marcos does.
Any game can be fixed with a slow float and a cold drink afterward.
The river is the best scout in Texas; it always knows where the current is.
texas-state.off_air: INVENTED. Married to Rosalinda, a high school band director who keeps him on time. Owns more inner tubes than chairs.
gags: Drifts off on air and snaps back with a yeehaw a full beat late.
Challenges Hank to a stilts-versus-unicycle race every season and loses on purpose.
Rates every win by how many tubes it would float.
texas-state.temperament: Easygoing to the point of horizontal.
texas-state.disposition: Relaxed, friendly, Hill Country through and through.
texas-state.compassion: High. Has pulled more strangers out of the river than he can count.
texas-state.worldview: A river belongs to everybody who floats it, so you pick up your trash and help the next fella out.
texas-state.rube: Yes: the lovable river drifter on stilts.

utah-state.bio: Wes Talbot grew up in Logan, scooped ice cream at the campus creamery through college, and is finishing a graduate degree in dairy science that he has been finishing for some time. He rides a unicycle up and down the Cache Valley because his bike was stolen and he decided it was a sign. The Logan Courier hired him to cover the Aggies after he live-blogged a home win while pedaling around the concourse. He is polite, earnest, and a little out of breath, and he apologizes to the team every time he doubted them.
utah-state.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in Logan, the youngest of six, son of a dairy farmer and a public-school secretary. Creamery scooper, now a long-running grad student in dairy science.
utah-state.beat: INVENTED. Live-blogged an Aggies home win while pedaling around the concourse; The Logan Courier hired him the next morning, mostly to make him sit down.
utah-state.look: Navy sequined campaign hat, navy-and-silver sequined ranger jacket with Aggies patches, tie, mic in hand, pedaling a tall unicycle (portrait).
utah-state.favorite: To research: a real Aggies player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Boise's blue turf is a lot, and he says that with love.
Sixty inches of snow is just an excuse for more ice cream.
The ride up Logan Canyon after a win is the best drive in the West.
utah-state.off_air: INVENTED. Engaged to Marisol, an engineering student who rebuilt his unicycle twice. Rates ice cream flavors in a notebook he shares with no one.
gags: Apologizes to the team on air after every win for having doubted them.
Tries to out-pedal Boone's enthusiasm and runs out of breath first.
Says 'golly' with full sincerity at least once a broadcast.
utah-state.temperament: Earnest and polite; nervous until the final buzzer, then relieved.
utah-state.appropriateness: G. 'Golly' and 'oh my heck' are his ceiling.
utah-state.compassion: High. Thanks the ushers by name.
utah-state.worldview: Good manners are free, and so should be the second scoop.
utah-state.rube: Yes: the lovable, breathless kid on one wheel.

washington-state.bio: Theo Whitlock grew up on a wheat farm outside Pullman and still manages the grain elevator his grandfather helped build. On weekends he is the loudest actor in the Palouse community theater, which says a great deal. The Pullman Courier hired him to cover the Cougs after his halftime speeches at a booster dinner ran past the dessert. He is crimson, loud and proud, a shameless ham who turns every result into a speech, and the producer gives him the hook most nights. He considers the hook a standing ovation.
washington-state.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up on a Palouse wheat farm; manages the family grain elevator and stars in community theater on weekends.
washington-state.beat: INVENTED. Gave a booster-dinner toast so long and stirring that a Pullman Courier editor in the crowd offered him a column just to end it.
washington-state.look: Crimson sequined campaign hat, crimson-and-silver sequined ranger jacket covered in Palouse patches, Cougars mic in hand, delighted grin (portrait).
washington-state.favorite: To research: a real Cougars player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Corvallis is lovely if you like your weather wet and your statistics wetter.
Rolling wheat fields are the most beautiful thing in the West, and that includes the mountains.
A long bus ride home from a win is the finest theater in America.
washington-state.off_air: INVENTED. Married to Darlene, a county extension nutritionist who times his speeches with a kitchen timer. Has played every leading role in the local theater, some of them twice.
gags: Takes a bow on the desk after every Cougs win until the producer cuts the lights.
Delivers a monologue whenever Jasper cites a stat.
Narrates the wheat harvest report during timeouts.
washington-state.temperament: Loud and big-hearted; never once has used his indoor voice.
washington-state.disposition: Proud, theatrical, endlessly sentimental about the Palouse.
washington-state.compassion: High. Remembers every farm family that drives three hours to a game.
washington-state.humor: Hammy oratory; the joke is how long it goes.
washington-state.worldview: Small towns hold the country together, and somebody ought to give a speech about it.

denver.bio: Augustus Pike ran the ring-toss booth at Colorado county fairs for twenty years and later worked as a street performer downtown, where he learned to sell anything with a top hat and a grin. He covers the Pioneers for The Denver Ledger as if every game were the greatest show at altitude, and he still cannot believe his luck. He sells every win as a miracle and blames every loss on the thin air, even when the thin air was clearly on our side. His top hat has been confiscated at two airports.
denver.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in Englewood, Colorado, son of a bus driver and a florist. Twenty years running fair games, then busking downtown.
denver.beat: INVENTED. Started barking Pioneers scores from a street corner downtown; a Denver Ledger editor bought a ticket to nothing and hired him.
denver.look: Rainbow sequined top hat, crimson-and-gold sequined Regency frock coat with gold embroidery and a white jabot, Denver mic in hand, gleeful grin (portrait).
denver.favorite: To research: a real Pioneers player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Seattle has rain; Denver has air, and less of it, which is better.
Visiting teams should be issued oxygen and a pamphlet.
Forty-nine inches of snow is just the sky saying 'step right up.'
denver.off_air: INVENTED. Married to Delphine, a hospital pharmacist who keeps the household finances very far away from him. Juggles for the neighborhood kids every Fourth of July.
gags: Blames every loss on the altitude, even home losses.
Tries to sell Jace a timeshare in the thin air every broadcast.
Introduces the starting five like a circus lineup, 'never before seen!'
denver.disposition: Theatrical, generous, always selling something he believes in.
denver.appropriateness: PG. Huckster patter, never a con.
denver.compassion: High. Hands out free tickets to kids who look like they need one.
denver.humor: Carnival bombast; the bit is his own unshakeable optimism.
denver.worldview: The best show in town should be one anybody can afford to see.
denver.rube: Yes: the lovable Mile High barker.

loyola-marymount.bio: Lance Montgomery spent ten years as the warm-up comic for television game shows in Los Angeles, the man who tells the audience when to clap. He moved to The Westchester Sentinel to cover the Lions when he realized he was clapping louder than the audience. He scores every game like a prize round and grins through every result, and he has never noticed that the punchline is usually him. He times his biggest calls to the jets roaring low overhead. He has perfect teeth and can't stop showing them.
loyola-marymount.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in Torrance, son of a school custodian and an aerospace secretary. A decade as a game-show warm-up comic.
loyola-marymount.beat: INVENTED. Did a warm-up set at a Lions home game as a favor, got a bigger laugh than the halftime show, and The Westchester Sentinel signed him on.
loyola-marymount.look: Split crimson-and-navy sequin tuxedo jacket with an LMU crest, white shirt, navy bow tie, slicked hair, LMU mic, toothy showman's grin (portrait).
loyola-marymount.favorite: To research: a real Lions player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Malibu is a beach with a basketball team attached.
Every possession is a prize round if you believe hard enough.
The best sound in college basketball is a jet passing over Westchester after a home win.
loyola-marymount.off_air: INVENTED. Married to Teresa, a hospital social worker who stopped laughing at his bits years ago and loves him anyway. Owns eleven bow ties, all crimson or navy.
gags: Tells the Lions what they've won after every victory, in full prize-reveal voice.
Offers Brody a lovely parting gift after every rivalry game.
Pauses mid-sentence whenever a jet goes over, then pretends he planned it.
loyola-marymount.temperament: Upbeat and unsinkable; frowns only off camera.
loyola-marymount.disposition: Smooth, eager, a showman with a soft heart.
loyola-marymount.compassion: High. Gives the best seats to the families who drove in from the Valley.
loyola-marymount.humor: Game-show cheese; he is always the contestant who loses the car.
loyola-marymount.worldview: Everybody deserves a moment in the spotlight, even the folks who never win the big prize.
loyola-marymount.rube: Yes: the lovable game-show grin who never notices he's the joke.

pacific.bio: Rex Stockwell sold used cars on a Stockton lot for twenty-five years, filmed his own late-night commercials, and became famous in three counties for a jingle nobody asked for. He covers the Tigers for The Stockton Clarion the same way he sold sedans: loudly, sunnily, and with a big discount on any bad news. He oversells every win, marks down every loss, and has never once read the fine print on his own predictions. He still owns the striped jacket from the commercials and wears it with real pride.
pacific.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in south Stockton, son of a cannery mechanic and a diner waitress. Twenty-five years selling used cars, with homemade TV ads.
pacific.beat: INVENTED. Ran a 'Tigers win, prices drop' promotion on his lot; The Stockton Clarion wrote about it, then offered him a column so he would stop calling the newsroom.
pacific.look: Orange-and-black tiger-stripe sequin tuxedo jacket with black lapels, orange bow tie, Pacific mic, the brightest grin in Stockton (portrait).
pacific.favorite: To research: a real Tigers player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Moraga is a lovely town if you can find it.
Stockton is the most underrated city in California, and that is not a sales pitch, mostly.
Every season deserves an extended warranty.
pacific.off_air: INVENTED. Married to Gloria, a bookkeeper who quietly fixed his business for twenty years. Still sings the jingle at family birthdays, uninvited.
gags: Opens every win with 'come on down to the lot' energy and a fake price tag.
Tries to sell Fergus a certified pre-owned rivalry every season.
Lists the losses as 'minor cosmetic damage.'
pacific.compassion: High. Gave a lot of first cars to kids with no credit.
pacific.humor: Pitchman bombast; he never notices the joke is his own forecast.
pacific.worldview: A fair deal is the only deal worth making, even if he oversells the paint job.

pepperdine.bio: Brody Haskins was a Malibu lifeguard for twenty summers and taught surf lessons to every tourist who could stand up and many who couldn't. He wandered into a Waves game to get out of the sun and fell hard. The Malibu Courant hired him for his enthusiasm and quickly learned about his attention span. He roots hard until the swell comes up, then narrates the ocean until somebody reminds him there is a game. He wears the dinner jacket over board shorts, and nobody has ever seen his legs on camera.
pepperdine.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in Oxnard, son of a strawberry-farm foreman and a nurse. Twenty summers as a Malibu lifeguard and surf instructor.
pepperdine.beat: INVENTED. Wrote a surf report that accidentally included a Waves box score; the readers loved it and The Malibu Courant made it permanent.
pepperdine.look: Royal-blue sequin dinner jacket with orange sequin lapels and cuffs, blue bow tie, sun-bleached shaggy blond hair, Waves mic, totally stoked grin (portrait).
pepperdine.favorite: To research: a real Waves player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: LMU has jets; Pepperdine has the ocean, and the ocean always wins.
A fast break is basically a clean left-hander.
Malibu is a small town; everybody just has a very big driveway.
pepperdine.off_air: INVENTED. Lives with his partner, Kai, a marine biologist who explains the swell to him properly. Owns nineteen surfboards and one pair of real shoes.
gags: Gives a full swell report mid-game, unprompted.
Calls Lance 'bro' on air with deep, confusing affection.
Describes every three-pointer as 'gnarly' and every turnover as 'a wipeout, dude.'
pepperdine.temperament: Mellow until a wave or a dunk appears, then stoked.
pepperdine.compassion: High. Has pulled a lot of people out of the water, and never makes them feel dumb.
pepperdine.humor: Surfer drift; the joke is that he wanders off mid-sentence.
pepperdine.worldview: The ocean belongs to everybody, so the beach should too.
pepperdine.rube: Yes: the lovable surfer who forgets there's a game.

portland.bio: Wendell Ashby piloted cargo ships up the Columbia and the Willamette for twenty-two years, and he still steers conversations the same way: slowly, carefully, and around imaginary sandbars. He retired, grew a magnificent mustache, and started covering the Pilots for The Portland Register because, as he says, the name was a sign. He navigates every game like a river trip and runs aground on his own metaphors at least once a night. He wears the aviator goggles because he once confused the Pilots with airplanes and decided to commit.
portland.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in St. Johns, Portland, son of a shipyard welder and a ferry ticket agent. Twenty-two years as a river pilot.
portland.beat: INVENTED. Wrote a letter to The Portland Register explaining the Pilots' offense in nautical charts; the editor framed it, then hired him.
portland.look: Purple sequined ship captain's greatcoat with gold epaulets and white facing, aviator goggles on his cap, big handlebar mustache, Pilots mic (portrait).
portland.favorite: To research: a real Pilots player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Seattle drinks coffee to wake up; Portland drinks it to have opinions.
Every basketball team needs a good first mate, and the first mate never gets the credit.
The Bluff has the best view of any campus in the league, and that's a nautical fact.
portland.off_air: INVENTED. Married to Ingrid, a retired tugboat captain who outranks him and reminds him. Builds model sternwheelers in the garage and names them after Pilots road trips.
gags: Calls every turnover a sandbar and every steal a favorable current.
Signals Jace with a foghorn whenever Seattle comes to town.
Gets so tangled in a nautical metaphor that he has to drop anchor and start over.
portland.temperament: Steady and unhurried, with a captain's sudden bellow.
portland.appropriateness: PG. 'Barnacles' is the strongest thing he says.
portland.compassion: High. Knows every deckhand's name and every dockworker's kid.
portland.humor: Pun-heavy and self-defeating; he is the first to laugh at his own shipwreck.
portland.worldview: The river carries everybody, so everybody should get a fair passage.
portland.rube: Yes: the lovable river captain who runs aground on his own puns.

saint-marys.bio: Fergus Byrne was the children's librarian in Moraga for twenty years and ran a Saturday story hour so popular that grown-ups started sneaking in. His stories always circled back eventually, which is how he covers the Gaels for The Moraga Messenger: slowly, by the fire, with a few embellishments on the wins. He is quietly devoted, never raises his voice, and gets caught doing it exactly once a season. His grandfather left him a lot of sayings, and Fergus is still working through them.
saint-marys.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in Vallejo, son of an Irish-born shipyard electrician and a school-cafeteria cook. Twenty years as a children's librarian.
saint-marys.beat: INVENTED. Began reading Gaels box scores aloud at story hour, with sound effects; a Moraga Messenger editor whose kid attended offered him a column.
saint-marys.look: Navy sequin blazer with a red Celtic-knot Western yoke, one red sequin sleeve, patterned tie, wry half-smile, Gaels mic (portrait).
saint-marys.favorite: To research: a real Gaels player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: San Francisco is a beautiful city with too many opinions about dinner.
A good game, like a good story, makes you wait for the ending.
Moraga is quiet the way a library is quiet: something is always happening.
saint-marys.off_air: INVENTED. Married to Siobhan, a middle-school vice principal who knows exactly how his stories end. Plays the tin whistle badly at every family gathering.
gags: Tells every recap as a fireside story and takes forever to reach the score.
Raises his voice once a season, always at a call, then apologizes for a week.
Quotes his grandfather's sayings to Hollis, who never understands them.
saint-marys.temperament: Calm, wry and patient; slow to anger and quick to forgive.
saint-marys.appropriateness: PG. Mischief in the eyes, nothing on the tongue.
saint-marys.compassion: High. A librarian's instinct to let everybody in.
saint-marys.humor: Long-fuse storytelling; the joke is how long it takes.
saint-marys.worldview: Everyone's story deserves to be heard all the way through, especially the quiet ones.
saint-marys.rube: Yes: the lovable storyteller who never gets to the point on time.

san-diego.bio: Rafa Ibarra grew up in Linda Vista, a few blocks below Alcala Park, and paid for college singing boleros at weddings and quinceañeras across San Diego. He taught middle-school Spanish for a decade and still sings on weekends. The Linda Vista Chronicle hired him to cover the Toreros after a viral clip of him serenading a referee who had made a good call. He savors a stylish win, shrugs off a loss with a wink, and never lets Los Angeles have the last word. He has one eyebrow that does all the work.
san-diego.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in Linda Vista, son of a Navy cook and a hotel housekeeper. Wedding singer through college, then ten years teaching middle-school Spanish.
san-diego.beat: INVENTED. A clip of him serenading a referee after a good call went around the city; The Linda Vista Chronicle hired him before the song ended.
san-diego.look: Navy-and-gold sequined matador traje de luces with USD on the front, black tie, slick dark hair, thick mustache, a big wink, Toreros mic (portrait).
san-diego.favorite: To research: a real Toreros player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Los Angeles is a lovely place to drive through on the way home.
Mission Bay at sunset after a win is proof that the universe is fair.
A stylish win counts double, according to nobody but him.
san-diego.off_air: INVENTED. Married to Ana, an ER nurse who out-sings him at every party. Grows chiles on the balcony and gives them away at work.
gags: Sings a line of a bolero after every home win.
Winks at the camera every time he mentions Lance.
Translates the play-by-play into Spanish when he gets excited, then forgets to translate back.
san-diego.disposition: Charming, playful, proud of his barrio.
san-diego.appropriateness: PG. Flirty with the camera, never crude.
san-diego.compassion: High. Knows every family on his street and every kid he ever taught.
san-diego.humor: Wink-and-a-smile charm; the joke lands sideways.
san-diego.worldview: Neighborhoods like his built this city, and they deserve the view too.
san-diego.rube: No. The desk's crooner, smoother than his rivals.

san-francisco.bio: Hollis Wexford spent thirty years as maître d' at a grand Nob Hill hotel dining room, where he seated everyone else and never once got a reservation for himself. Retired, he covers the Dons for The Lone Mountain Mercury in the same spirit: plummy, delighted, and forgiving of nearly everything once dessert arrives. He is gently baffled by how the other half of the city lives and is trying, sincerely, to learn. He arrives at every home game exactly on time and is still always somehow late for dinner.
san-francisco.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in the Sunset District, son of a streetcar operator and a hospital laundress. Thirty years as a Nob Hill maître d'.
san-francisco.beat: INVENTED. Sent The Lone Mountain Mercury a restaurant-style review of a Dons game, three and a half forks, and the editor hired him on the spot.
san-francisco.look: Green velvet brocade smoking jacket embroidered in gold, gold lamé bow tie, silver hair, a delighted society-host smile, Dons mic (portrait).
san-francisco.favorite: To research: a real Dons player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Santa Clara treats basketball like a software update, and you can't update a soul.
The fog is San Francisco's sixth man and should be listed on the roster.
A good home crowd is like a good dining room: everyone feels expected.
san-francisco.off_air: INVENTED. Lives with his husband, Ellis, a retired cable-car gripman who books their dinners because Hollis cannot. Collects vintage menus and bow ties, in that order.
gags: Reviews every game in forks and spoons.
Asks Grant to explain an app, then calls it 'marvelous' without listening.
Misses the dinner reservation every postgame, without fail.
san-francisco.disposition: Plummy, delighted, sincerely trying to understand people unlike him.
san-francisco.appropriateness: G. Disapproval is expressed with 'oh, dear.'
san-francisco.compassion: Warm, a little sheltered, learning more every season.
san-francisco.humor: Gentle society comedy; the joke is how charmed he is by ordinary things.
san-francisco.worldview: A city should feed everybody, not just the people with reservations; he only learned that late, and he says so.
san-francisco.rube: Yes: the lovable Nob Hill host who never gets a table.

santa-clara.bio: Grant Silva grew up in Santa Clara, the son of a Portuguese-American orchard family whose apricot trees gave way to office parks. He spent a decade running product launches for a tech company and still cannot describe anything without a keynote reveal. The Santa Clara Standard hired him to cover the Broncos, and he reviews every game like a version release, filing losses as known issues and always promising the next update. He is relentlessly upbeat. His mother still asks when he is going to get a real job.
santa-clara.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in Santa Clara in a Portuguese-American family that farmed apricots before the office parks came. A decade managing tech product launches.
santa-clara.beat: INVENTED. Pitched The Santa Clara Standard a Broncos column with a slide deck; it was the first slide deck the editor had ever enjoyed.
santa-clara.look: Red-and-white velvet blazer patterned with mission bells and circuit-board lines, open white collar, red mic, keynote-stage grin (portrait).
santa-clara.favorite: To research: a real Broncos player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: San Francisco thinks fog is personality.
Every loss is just a known issue with a fix in testing.
The orchards were here first, and the Broncos should play like they remember.
santa-clara.off_air: INVENTED. Married to Dana, a public-school librarian who refuses to let him demo anything at dinner. Still keeps one apricot tree in the backyard, his grandmother's.
gags: Announces every win as a version number.
Sends Hollis release notes after every rivalry game; Hollis has never opened one.
Promises a 'big announcement' at halftime that is always a snack.
santa-clara.temperament: Upbeat and unshakable; never meets a problem he can't rename.
santa-clara.disposition: Bright, polished, sincere under the jargon.
santa-clara.appropriateness: G. Every curse word has been replaced with 'bug.'
santa-clara.compassion: Good. Remembers the orchard and the people who worked it.
santa-clara.humor: Tech-launch parody; he is the punchline and the presenter.
santa-clara.worldview: The best product is a neighborhood that still has room for the people who were there first.
santa-clara.rube: Yes: the lovable keynote guy who thinks everything is a launch.

seattle.bio: Jace Harmon spent fifteen years hosting a Seattle morning radio show, talking fast before sunrise and drinking coffee faster. When the station changed formats, he landed at The First Hill Dispatch covering the Redhawks, and he still sounds like it is six in the morning. He is caffeinated and openly Redhawk, peaks early, and reads every result through the bottom of his fourth cup. He owns a dozen umbrellas and has never opened one, because real Seattleites don't. He can name every coffee cart on First Hill.
seattle.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in Seattle's Beacon Hill, son of a ferry engineer and a school-bus dispatcher. Fifteen years as a morning-radio host.
seattle.beat: INVENTED. When his radio show was canceled, The First Hill Dispatch asked him to bring the morning-show energy to the Redhawks beat.
seattle.look: Red-and-green sequined dinner jacket with black velvet lapels, open black shirt, Redhawks mic, wide caffeinated grin (portrait).
seattle.favorite: To research: a real Redhawks player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Portland is just Seattle with fewer umbrellas and more opinions.
Rain is the best home-court advantage in the West.
Every game is better on the fourth cup of coffee.
seattle.off_air: INVENTED. Married to Noelle, a pediatric nurse who works nights, so they meet over coffee. Roasts his own beans in the garage and the neighbors have complained.
gags: Counts his coffees on air and narrates faster with each one.
Offers Wendell a coffee every game and calls it 'the good stuff, captain.'
Peaks at the opening tip and is whispering by the final minute.
seattle.temperament: Fast and frantic, then crashes cheerfully.
seattle.disposition: Upbeat, chatty, Seattle to the core.
seattle.appropriateness: PG. Talks too fast to swear.
seattle.compassion: High. Buys coffee for every security guard in the building.
seattle.humor: Rapid-fire morning-show patter; the joke is the crash.
seattle.worldview: A rainy city takes care of its own, and coffee is how you check on people.
seattle.rube: Yes: the lovable over-caffeinated morning guy.

alabama-am.bio: Reginald Toney spent thirty-five years as a rocket-engine test technician in Huntsville, counting down from ten so many times that he now does it in his sleep, according to his wife. A proud Alabama A&M graduate, he started writing about the Bulldogs for The Huntsville Sentinel in retirement and calls every run like a launch: ignition, liftoff, and the occasional scrub on the pad. He loves his school openly and a well-executed play even more. He still keeps a stopwatch in his shirt pocket and times the national anthem.
alabama-am.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in northwest Huntsville, son of a cotton-gin mechanic and a church choir director. Alabama A&M engineering graduate, then thirty-five years as a rocket-engine test technician.
alabama-am.beat: INVENTED. Called a Bulldogs comeback on the radio as a launch countdown from the stands; The Huntsville Sentinel heard about it and offered him a column the next week.
alabama-am.look: Maroon-and-white Alabama A&M University hoodie, close-cropped white hair, warm grandfatherly smile (portrait).
alabama-am.favorite: To research: a real Bulldogs player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Montgomery is a fine city for history; Huntsville is a fine city for the future.
A good inbounds play is a launch sequence: everybody knows their job, and nobody improvises.
The Hill is the best launch pad in the South.
alabama-am.off_air: INVENTED. Married fifty years to Bernice, a retired chemistry teacher who catches every error in his columns. Builds model rockets with his grandkids and has lost several to a neighbor's tree.
gags: Counts down the final ten seconds of every close game, out loud, every time.
Calls every turnover 'a scrub on the pad' and insists on a reset.
Debates Curtis about whether a proverb is better than a countdown; neither will yield.
alabama-am.temperament: Calm, precise and patient, until the final ten seconds.
alabama-am.disposition: Steady, proud, an engineer to the bone.
alabama-am.appropriateness: G. 'Abort, abort' is the strongest thing he says.
alabama-am.compassion: High. Mentors every young engineer who asks, and plenty who don't.
alabama-am.humor: Dry countdown humor; the joke is how seriously he times everything.
alabama-am.worldview: Great things get built by teams nobody photographs, and he makes sure they get named.

grambling.bio: Keisha Robinson grew up in Grambling, where the band is not an activity but a weather system. She played mellophone through college, became a middle-school band director, and still judges every halftime show like a contest. The Grambling Ledger hired her to cover the Tigers because she watched the games as closely as the bands, and it turned out she knew both cold. She is sharp on the hoops and fierce about her tiny town's outsized pride. She can hear a flat trumpet from the parking lot.
grambling.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up on a street off Main in Grambling, daughter of a postal carrier and a nursing professor. Played mellophone in college, now a middle-school band director.
grambling.beat: INVENTED. Wrote a Grambling Ledger letter rating a Tigers game and its halftime show side by side; the editor printed it and asked for one every week.
grambling.look: Black-and-gold Grambling quarter-zip, long straight dark hair, calm and confident expression (portrait).
grambling.favorite: To research: a real Tigers player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Baton Rouge has a big band; Grambling has the band.
A good offense should move like a marching band: everybody in step, nobody showing off.
Small towns make big noise, and the scoreboard should reflect that.
grambling.off_air: INVENTED. Lives with her aunt Celeste, who has never missed a home game in her life. Teaches private lessons on Saturdays and keeps a mellophone in her car just in case.
gags: Grades every halftime show and every half of basketball on the same scale.
Trades band-versus-band insults with Monique that are mostly compliments.
Hears a missed free throw as a flat note and winces.
grambling.temperament: Composed and sharp; gets loud only for the band.
grambling.disposition: Proud, disciplined, warm under the stern face.
grambling.appropriateness: G. A raised eyebrow does the work.
grambling.compassion: High. Knows which kids need a ride home after practice.
grambling.humor: Dry, quick and musical; her jokes are on the beat.
grambling.worldview: A small town can carry a big tradition, as long as everybody keeps showing up to rehearsal.

prairie-view.bio: Marcus Delane is a civil engineer who spent twenty years designing highway interchanges around Houston and still treats every drive like a site inspection. A Prairie View engineering graduate and the son of two Panthers, he moved back near campus and started writing about the team for The Prairie View Observer, steady as a long road and dry as a July afternoon. He roots with patience and a sense of humor about the heat. He has rated every gas station between Houston and campus and will share the list whether you ask or not.
prairie-view.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in Hempstead, Texas, son of a hay farmer and a county clerk who met as Prairie View students. Prairie View engineering graduate, twenty years designing highway interchanges.
prairie-view.beat: INVENTED. Wrote a Panthers season preview for The Prairie View Observer structured like a traffic study; it was the most-read thing in the paper that fall.
prairie-view.look: Purple-and-gold Prairie View polo with a rhinestone-studded stripe down each sleeve and bedazzled lettering, bald head, neat goatee, relaxed confident smile (portrait redo pending).
prairie-view.favorite: To research: a real Panthers player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Houston thinks it has traffic; it has never driven behind a hay trailer.
Steady wins, and heat makes everybody honest.
The best basketball in Texas happens in small gyms on hot nights.
prairie-view.off_air: INVENTED. Married to Yolanda, a pharmacist who sets the thermostat and the rules. Keeps a cooler in the truck at all times, stocked for everyone but himself.
gags: Reports the drive time to every road game like a traffic engineer.
Rates arenas by their air conditioning first and their crowd second.
Gets a correction from Simone about Houston every broadcast and pretends to take notes.
prairie-view.temperament: Measured and unflappable, even in August.
prairie-view.appropriateness: G. 'Well, that's not ideal' covers it.
prairie-view.compassion: High. Always pulls over for a stranded driver.
prairie-view.humor: Bone-dry understatement; the joke is how calm he stays while melting.
prairie-view.worldview: Good roads and good schools are how you get people home safe, so you build both carefully.

jackson-state.bio: Brianna Coleman grew up in west Jackson, a few blocks from campus, braiding her cousins' hair on the porch and sketching outfits in her notebooks. She earned a fashion-merchandising degree and now runs a small boutique that dresses half the city for homecoming. She covers the Tigers for The Jackson Almanac like a fashion critic who also knows every defensive rotation, and she is shamelessly loyal about both. She notices who showed up dressed to win, and she means effort as much as uniforms.
jackson-state.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in west Jackson, daughter of a high school football coach and a hospital records clerk, both Jackson State alumni. Fashion-merchandising degree, now owns a small boutique.
jackson-state.beat: INVENTED. Posted courtside 'best dressed and best defended' rankings after Tigers games; The Jackson Almanac turned them into a weekly column.
jackson-state.look: Navy-and-white JKST hoodie with a sequined yoke across the shoulders and rhinestone lettering, long braids, relaxed confident smile (portrait redo pending).
jackson-state.favorite: To research: a real Tigers player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Lorman is beautiful, but the stars are not a wardrobe.
Effort is the best outfit, and some teams show up undressed.
Jackson has more style per square foot than any city in the South.
jackson-state.off_air: INVENTED. Lives with her younger sister, who borrows everything and returns nothing. Sews costumes for a local youth theater on Sunday afternoons.
gags: Hands out a best-dressed award after every home game, sometimes to the referee.
Offers Darius a wardrobe consultation every season; he has never accepted.
Calls a bad loss 'a bad outfit day' and moves on.
jackson-state.temperament: Composed and confident; fierce only about her team.
jackson-state.disposition: Stylish, loyal, sharper than she lets on.
jackson-state.compassion: High. Dresses kids for prom for free when the family can't swing it.
jackson-state.humor: Fashion-critic snap; the joke is the runway voice on a rebound.
jackson-state.worldview: Everybody deserves to walk into a room feeling good about themselves, and she makes it her business.

alabama-state.bio: Curtis Mayes spent thirty years as an aircraft mechanic at the Air Force base in Montgomery and retired with a toolbox, a pension, and a head full of his grandmother's proverbs. An Alabama State graduate, he covers the Hornets for The Montgomery Beacon and cannot get through a game without quoting her, often in ways that don't quite apply. He is patient with his school and immovably proud of the city. He has never met a timeout he couldn't fill with a saying about gardens, rain or biscuits.
alabama-state.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in west Montgomery, son of a bus mechanic and a school cook, raised partly by a grandmother full of sayings. Alabama State graduate, then thirty years as an Air Force base aircraft mechanic.
alabama-state.beat: INVENTED. Called the Hornets postgame radio show with a proverb every night until The Montgomery Beacon gave him a column just to collect them.
alabama-state.look: Black-and-gold ALST quarter-zip with a sequined yoke across the shoulders and rhinestone lettering, bald head, neat goatee, relaxed confident smile (portrait redo pending).
alabama-state.favorite: To research: a real Hornets player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Huntsville counts down; Montgomery knows patience is the faster road.
A steady hand cooks the best meal, and a steady point guard does too.
Montgomery has more history per block than anywhere, and its people made most of it.
alabama-state.off_air: INVENTED. Married to Doris, a retired nurse who corrects the proverbs he gets wrong, which is most of them. Grows tomatoes and greens and gives away more than he eats.
gags: Opens every recap with 'my grandmother used to say' and sometimes makes it up.
Trades proverbs for countdowns with Reginald; both lose.
Mixes two proverbs together and then defends the result.
alabama-state.temperament: Patient and unhurried; hard to rattle, slow to judge.
alabama-state.appropriateness: G. His grandmother would approve of every word.
alabama-state.compassion: High. Learned early that a town takes care of its own.
alabama-state.humor: Folksy wisdom that wanders; the joke is the mangled proverb.
alabama-state.worldview: A city's history belongs to the ordinary people who marched and worked in it, and he tells their stories every chance he gets.

mvsu.bio: Lorraine Pickett grew up on her family's farm near Itta Bena and teaches high school math in Leflore County, where she makes every lesson about something real: yields, rain, and point differentials. She covers the Delta Devils for The Itta Bena Register as the hardest-working underdog in the league, and she has the spreadsheets. She is warm to the folks who work the land and cool to the folks who own too much of it. She thinks the horizon is the prettiest thing in America and dares you to argue.
mvsu.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up on a family farm outside Itta Bena, daughter of a farmer and a county extension agent, both Mississippi Valley State graduates. High school math teacher.
mvsu.beat: INVENTED. Wrote The Itta Bena Register a letter calculating the odds of a Delta Devils upset; the upset happened, and the editor hired her the next morning.
mvsu.look: White MVSU polo covered in white sequins with thin dark green trim and rhinestone lettering, deep brown skin, natural curls, relaxed confident smile (portrait redo pending).
mvsu.favorite: To research: a real Delta Devils player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Jackson is a fine city with a lot of nice outfits and no horizon.
Underdog math is still math, and the numbers say keep going.
The Delta is flat because it has nothing to hide.
mvsu.off_air: INVENTED. Lives with her grandfather, who still drives a tractor and calls every game on the porch radio. Teaches a free algebra night for adults at the library.
gags: Calculates an upset probability before every game and is cheerfully wrong.
Reminds Brianna that a horizon is free and an outfit is not.
Uses crop yields to explain rebounding margins.
mvsu.temperament: Clear-eyed and calm; stubborn when the numbers are on her side.
mvsu.appropriateness: G. Saves her strongest words for absentee landlords.
mvsu.compassion: Very high. Roots for anybody working twice as hard for half as much.
mvsu.humor: Dry farm-and-math humor; deadpan with a twinkle.
mvsu.worldview: The people who work the land should share in what it grows, and she'll show you the math.

alcorn.bio: Darius Hill is a forester who spent twenty years walking the woods around Lorman, marking timber and naming every tree he passed. He studied the night sky as a boy on his grandfather's porch and still keeps a telescope in the bed of his truck. He covers the Braves for The Lorman Banner with a slow smile and never a shout, and he knows the oldest stories in the county by heart. After a home loss, he recommends sitting on the porch until it settles. After a win, he points at the stars.
alcorn.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up on a family homestead outside Lorman, son of a pulpwood hauler and a church pianist. Twenty years as a state forester.
alcorn.beat: INVENTED. Began writing Braves recaps for The Lorman Banner as short stories set under the stars; readers clipped them and the editor kept asking for more.
alcorn.look: Purple-and-gold Alcorn State hoodie, close-cut graying hair, a neat goatee, a calm, kind look (portrait).
alcorn.favorite: To research: a real Braves player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Jackson is loud; the country is louder if you know how to listen.
Good defense is like a forest: everything is connected, and nothing moves alone.
There's no better drive home after a win than a dark country road with the windows down.
alcorn.off_air: INVENTED. Married to Felicia, a high school counselor who keeps the porch light on. Leads a stargazing night for kids every month from a hayfield.
gags: Points out a constellation after every home win.
Ignores Brianna's wardrobe advice with a slow, gracious smile.
Recommends the porch for every loss and means it.
alcorn.appropriateness: G. He has never raised his voice on air.
alcorn.compassion: Very high. Knows every elder's story and makes sure the young folks hear it.
alcorn.humor: Slow-burn country wit; the joke arrives a minute later.
alcorn.worldview: The land remembers everything, and so should the people who live on it.

uapb.bio: Tamika Jordan grew up in Pine Bluff fishing the Arkansas River with her grandmother before school, and she studied aquaculture at Arkansas-Pine Bluff because she wanted to know why the fish did what they did. She works at a fish hatchery and covers the Golden Lions for The Pine Bluff Courier like a patient angler. She is sharp about effort and generous about everything else. She keeps a tackle box in her car. She says the best fishing and the best basketball both reward the quiet ones.
uapb.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in Pine Bluff, daughter of a paper-mill worker and a hair stylist, raised on her grandmother's fishing trips. Aquaculture degree, now a hatchery biologist.
uapb.beat: INVENTED. Wrote a fishing report for The Pine Bluff Courier that drifted into Golden Lions predictions; the predictions were right, so the editor gave her the beat.
uapb.look: Black Arkansas-Pine Bluff quarter-zip with gold UAPB lettering, long straight dark hair, calm, confident smile (portrait).
uapb.favorite: To research: a real Golden Lions player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Itta Bena is lovely, but you can't fish a horizon.
A good defense is patient bait: it waits until the other side bites.
Pine Bluff deserves more credit than it gets, and so do its catfish.
uapb.off_air: INVENTED. Lives with her grandmother, who still outfishes her. Coaches a youth fishing club on Saturdays.
gags: Rates every win by what was biting and how many.
Sends Lorraine a catfish recipe after every rivalry game.
Calls a scoring drought 'a slow morning on the river' and stays calm.
uapb.temperament: Patient and level; never rushes a cast or a judgment.
uapb.appropriateness: G. Saves her strong words for the ones that got away.
uapb.compassion: High. Teaches every kid on the dock how to bait a hook.
uapb.humor: Easygoing angler humor; dry and observant.
uapb.worldview: Rivers and towns both need tending, and she shows up for both.

florida-am.bio: Andre Baptiste is a retired pharmacist who filled prescriptions in Tallahassee for thirty-five years and knows the medical history of half the town, discreetly. A Florida A&M graduate, he covers the Rattlers for The Tallahassee Clarion and holds everything to the standard of the Hill: quick, sharp and decisive. He loves a good strike on the court and a good band at halftime. He reviews every game the way he checked a prescription, twice, and calmly. He has never once let a bad call ruin his supper.
florida-am.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in Frenchtown, Tallahassee, son of a barber and a schoolteacher. Florida A&M pharmacy graduate, thirty-five years as a neighborhood pharmacist.
florida-am.beat: INVENTED. Wrote a letter to The Tallahassee Clarion grading a Rattlers win like a prescription, dosage and all; the editor called him the next morning.
florida-am.look: Orange Florida A&M polo with dark green trim, short gray hair, neat mustache, a warm, proud smile (portrait).
florida-am.favorite: To research: a real Rattlers player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Daytona Beach is a nice place to visit if you like your sand loud.
The quickest strike is the one you set up three passes earlier.
Tallahassee is a college town with a capitol attached, not the other way around.
florida-am.off_air: INVENTED. Married to Claudette, a retired English professor who edits his columns in red ink. Grows mangoes in a pot and insists the climate supports it.
gags: Calls every quick basket 'a clean strike' and nods with deep satisfaction.
Debates Isaiah about whether speed or precision matters more; precision always wins, according to him.
Checks the scorebook twice before he will announce a final.
florida-am.appropriateness: G. The strongest word in his vocabulary is 'unacceptable.'
florida-am.compassion: Very high. Spent a career quietly helping people afford their medicine.
florida-am.worldview: A community is only healthy if everybody can get what they need, and the Hill taught him to keep that standard.

texas-southern.bio: Simone Okafor grew up in Houston's Third Ward, the daughter of Nigerian-born parents, an engineer and a nurse, and spent five years as a radio traffic reporter, calling wrecks from a helicopter over freeways she still won't drive. She covers the Tigers for The Third Ward Lantern quick, confident and funny, and saves her eye-rolls for the glass towers downtown. She judges every offense by how it would handle rush hour. Her mother still asks when she will go to law school. Her braids, she says, are the only thing in Houston that survives August.
texas-southern.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in the Third Ward, daughter of a Nigerian-born petroleum engineer and a Nigerian-born nurse. Texas Southern graduate, then five years as a helicopter traffic reporter.
texas-southern.beat: INVENTED. When her traffic-radio station merged, The Third Ward Lantern hired her to bring the same speed and snark to the Tigers.
texas-southern.look: Maroon-and-gray TXSO hoodie with sequin-trimmed collar and cuffs and rhinestone lettering, deep brown skin, long braids, knowing smile (portrait redo pending).
texas-southern.favorite: To research: a real Tigers player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Prairie View thinks it's hot; it should try I-45 at five o'clock.
A fast break is the only lane in Houston that's actually moving.
The Third Ward has more heart than any skyline in Texas.
texas-southern.off_air: INVENTED. Lives near her parents, who host Sunday jollof for half the block, and a dog named Beltway. Runs the Saturday morning neighborhood cleanup.
gags: Gives every game a traffic report: congestion in the paint, merging delays on the wing.
Asks Marcus how the drive was, every time, just to hear him answer.
Blames the humidity for every missed free throw, and isn't wrong.
texas-southern.temperament: Quick, sharp and confident; unbothered by heat or hecklers.
texas-southern.disposition: Funny, proud, protective of her neighborhood.
texas-southern.compassion: High. Knows which neighbors need a ride and drives them.
texas-southern.humor: Rapid-fire Houston snark; the joke is always the freeway.
texas-southern.worldview: Neighborhoods like hers built this city, and the towers downtown should remember who pours their coffee.

bethune-cookman.bio: Isaiah Grant spent fifteen years changing tires on a regional stock-car pit crew, one of the few Black crewmen on the circuit, before his knees retired him. He then taught auto shop at a Daytona Beach high school. He covers the Wildcats for The Daytona Beach Mercury like a race on the sand: green flag, clean laps, and the occasional spinout. He roots with easy confidence and a sunny grin. He insists a fast break is just a pit stop in reverse and will diagram it if you let him.
bethune-cookman.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in Daytona Beach's Midtown, son of a motel cook and a citrus-packing forewoman, a few blocks from campus. Fifteen years on a stock-car pit crew, then a high school auto-shop teacher.
bethune-cookman.beat: INVENTED. Called a Wildcats comeback like the last lap of a race from the stands; a Daytona Beach Mercury editor in the next row hired him at the buzzer.
bethune-cookman.look: Maroon-and-gold BCU quarter-zip covered in sequins with rhinestone lettering, light-brown skin, short locs, relaxed confident smile (portrait redo pending).
bethune-cookman.favorite: To research: a real Wildcats player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Tallahassee is a fine town if you don't need an ocean.
A fast break is just a pit stop in reverse.
The beach in February is the best home-court advantage in the country.
bethune-cookman.off_air: INVENTED. Married to Charmaine, a dental hygienist who runs the household and the grill. Restores old pickups in the driveway and never finishes one.
gags: Waves an imaginary green flag at every tipoff and a checkered one at every win.
Argues speed versus precision with Andre and loses on the details.
Diagrams every play like a pit stop, with tire changes.
bethune-cookman.temperament: Easygoing and confident; quick to grin and slow to worry.
bethune-cookman.disposition: Sunny, friendly, a gearhead with a big heart.
bethune-cookman.compassion: High. Fixes neighbors' cars for free and pretends it was nothing.
bethune-cookman.humor: Good-natured gearhead humor; he talks about basketball in horsepower.
bethune-cookman.worldview: Anybody can learn to fix something if somebody takes the time to show them.

southern-u.bio: Monique Batiste grew up in Scotlandville, just below the bluff, in a Black Creole family that measures time by how long the roux has been on the stove. She has worked the line at her aunt's restaurant since she was fifteen and now runs the kitchen. She covers the Jaguars for The Baton Rouge Courier like a gumbo, layer by layer, and roots out loud for Southern while cheerfully ignoring the giant school across town. She judges every game by its seasoning. She has never once followed a recipe and never once burned a roux.
southern-u.backstory: INVENTED. Grew up in Scotlandville, daughter of a shrimper and a school cafeteria manager in a Black Creole family. Line cook since fifteen, now head cook at her aunt's restaurant.
southern-u.beat: INVENTED. Brought gumbo to press row at a Jaguars game; a Baton Rouge Courier editor asked who she was, and she talked basketball until he hired her.
southern-u.look: Columbia-blue-and-gold Southern polo with sequin-trimmed collar and cuffs and rhinestone lettering, light-brown skin, short pixie cut, relaxed confident smile (portrait redo pending).
southern-u.favorite: To research: a real Jaguars player or era they can champion, with a source.
hot_takes: Grambling has a great band, and Southern has the better gumbo.
A good offense, like a good roux, needs patience and constant stirring.
The bluff over the river is the prettiest spot in Baton Rouge, and everybody else can keep the big stadium.
southern-u.off_air: INVENTED. Lives with her grandmother, who taught her every recipe and denies it. Cooks for the church fish fry every Friday in Lent.
gags: Rates every win by its seasoning and every loss as 'needs another hour on the stove.'
Sends Keisha a pot of gumbo before every rivalry game, as a peace offering and a threat.
Never names the giant school across town; just calls it 'the other place.'
southern-u.temperament: Warm and fiery; calm in a hot kitchen and loud in the stands.
southern-u.disposition: Proud, generous, born to feed people.
southern-u.appropriateness: PG. Kitchen language, cleaned up for air.
southern-u.compassion: Very high. Nobody leaves her kitchen hungry.
southern-u.humor: Spicy home-cook humor, all seasoning metaphors.
southern-u.worldview: Good food and good teams both come from people working together, and everybody gets a bowl.
